[Task from agent · from "Design alignment" (cli_afe2bbcd-ec7b-40bb-a0ee-8265f88d52db) · Claude Code · claude-cli-raw-opus · hop 1/8]
You are shipping "give this app a theme" as something an agent can be asked to do in a customer's repository, and proving it works from the first tap. Read this whole brief before starting.

WHERE THINGS STAND
The Ripul SDK has a theme system for a host app's own screens. Three trials on a second app, Sandsend Retreats, are written up in `docs/plans/sdk-theme-host-burden.md`: read it whole, it is the evidence for everything below. In short, a host now has three levels:
1. Settings only. A build-tool plug-in in the package (`RipulThemeRedirect`) themes the app with no change to its Swift: three lines of project settings, a theme document and its fonts. It reaches typefaces, the accent, hierarchy styles and wrapped system colours. It does not reach text with no colour of its own, lists, or the host's own colours. It is on `main` and NOT yet in a public release.
2. A few lines where it matters (a list, a text colour, the host's own colours).
3. Full migration with `ripul-theme migrate`, `check` and `lint`, which rewrites call sites to explicit accessors.
The levels mix, a file at a time. Peter, who owns the product, has decided this morning: the plug-in is how a host starts and the migration is for a host that wants the rest; and we ship BOTH the migration code and a skill that lets an agent migrate a customer's repository. His words: "We need to look at how we ship skills, let's do both, also, I want to add this as one of the optional tasks, when we start a new chat and offer starting prompts."

Standing rules to read first: Decision 9 in `docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md` and `.ripul/memories/project_theme_one_system_going_forward.md` (everything new on the base layer, nothing on the legacy engine); `.ripul/memories/feedback_generalizable_native_theme_strategies.md`; `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/ripulGuide.md` (how guides ship and the rules for writing one); `ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming-for-hosts.md`. Also ripul_guide topics `plans`, `trains`, `devices`. Your plan task is t_85739ddee2be in the plan `theme-aware-codebase`: mark it doing now with planTaskStatus, write to its note as you go, mark it done at the end. Agent messages get lost when the host reloads; the plan's log and the files you commit are the record.

WHAT I FOUND ABOUT HOW WE SHIP THIS KIND OF THING TODAY
Ripul ships guides, not skills. A guide is `chrome-extension/public/guides/<id>.md`, listed in `public/guides/index.json`, fetched by the `ripul_guide` tool, live with a web deploy, and it reaches Claude, Codex and Antigravity alike. An agent reads one only if it is pointed there. Nothing ships a skill in the other sense: a thing that appears in an agent's own skill list or that a person not using Ripul can pick up. The `sdk` guide has a short section "Giving the app a theme" written before the plug-in existed, so it describes only the migration route.
The starting prompts of an empty chat are in `chrome-extension/src/config/chatStarters.ts`: fixed rows per kind of chat; a coding chat has four plain rows and three that open a list of ideas (`PROJECT_SETUP_IDEAS`, `EXTENSION_IDEAS`, `ARTEFACT_IDEAS`). A tap fills the composer with the row's `example` and does not send. `V2WelcomeScreen.test.tsx` walks every row.

WHAT TO BUILD
1. The procedure, written once and well. What an agent does when asked to theme an app: find out what the app is (SwiftUI, how it is built, whether it has the package); work on a branch, never the default one; capture screenshots under the normal look before touching anything; start with the plug-in so the app is themed with no source change; write a theme document from what the person points at (a website, a brand file) and bundle fonts with their licences, saying when a font cannot be bundled; then, only where the person wants more, adapt the source with `ripul-theme migrate` and finish what it leaves by the published table; prove nothing moved under the normal look with the lint and a second set of screenshots, captured twice because a glass control differs between two captures of one build; stop and ask at real decisions (the host's own colours, which level they want); and hand back a ledger of what changed. The tool reads text, not Swift, so its output is a draft to verify. Everything in it must be true of the released package: check each claim against the code or by running it.
2. Ship it as a guide. A `theming` guide by the rules in ripulGuide.md, with an index entry whose `when` makes an agent open it at the right moment, and bring the `sdk` guide's theme section up to date so it points there and no longer describes only the migration.
3. Ship it as a skill file in the SDK package, for an agent that is not running inside Ripul: the same procedure in the form a coding agent's skill takes, with one command in the package's `tools/` that puts it where the agent in that repository will find it. The public release leaves out the SDK's `scripts/` folder and ships `tools/` and `docs/`. One source of truth for the two forms, so they cannot drift: say how you ensured that.
4. The starting prompt. In a new coding chat, a row for theming, as one of the rows that opens ideas: start with no change to the source; adapt the source for the rest; look at what a theme would reach and change nothing; make a theme from my website. Follow the wording and shape of the existing rows exactly, and keep the test passing. The prompts must work in a repository that is not an iPhone app by saying so plainly, and must send the agent to the guide first.
5. A short proposal, `docs/plans/shipping-skills.md`, for Peter to read on his phone: how Ripul could ship real skills, not only guides. Look at how each of the three CLIs the host launches discovers skills or their nearest equivalent, and at what the host passes them when it starts a session (`ripul-native-app/macOS/CliServerBase.swift` and the code around the harness note). Sections `## Problem`, `## What exists today`, `## Options`, `## Recommendation`, `## Open questions`. Lead with the recommendation. Say what you checked in code and what you reasoned. Do not build it.

RELEASE AND DEPLOY, WHICH ARE YOURS
- Web: `npx tsgo --noEmit`, then `npm run deploy:all` from a committed and pushed tree; confirm what went live.
- SDK: release 0.7.172, so that the plug-in, the tools and the skill file are in a public package. Before releasing, build WAC against the SDK as it is now: the plug-in commit was never built with WAC (a throwaway worktree of `~/Documents/WAC_ios_final-shift-rate-templates` under /tmp pointed at the local SDK; never edit, stash, reset or commit in a WAC checkout). Follow `.ripul/memories/feedback_sdk_release_from_clean_worktree.md` and `feedback_sdk_release_after_all_edits.md` exactly, run `git -C ~/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk pull --ff-only` first, and never force-push.
- Many sessions share this checkout. Commit only your own files: `git add <paths>`, then `git commit -m "…" -- <paths>`; never a bare `git commit`; if git says the index is locked, wait and retry; push at once; never stash, reset or check out files.
- With the default document nothing may change in Ripul's own app or in any host: the SDK theme tests pass, `ripul-theme check` on Ripul's sources reads zero, the SDK builds for the iOS simulator (the `--triple` form in CLAUDE.md) and macOS.

THE TEST FROM THE STARTER, WHICH IS THE POINT
When the guide is live and 0.7.172 is public, prove the whole path as a customer would meet it:
- Make a clean copy of Sandsend's default branch: `git -C ~/Documents/sandsend-retreats worktree add /tmp/sandsend-starter main` (never edit, commit, stash or reset in `~/Documents/sandsend-retreats` itself).
- Load the agent tools (`agent_comms_tools`) and call `spawn_agent` with cwd `/tmp/sandsend-starter`, harness `claude`, title "Sandsend: theme it from the starter", and as its task EXACTLY the text your "start with no change to the source" starter puts in the composer, plus one sentence a person would add: "The look to follow is the app's website, www.sandsendretreats.com." Nothing else: no hints, no paths, no mention of earlier trials. That agent is the customer's agent, and what it does with only that is the measurement.
- Do not rely on its reply reaching you. Watch its branch and its files. When it stops, measure what it did from git and the clock and judge it against the third trial: did it find and read the guide; did it reach a themed app with no Swift changed; did it meet the plug-in's trust step on a released package (the third trial could not test that) and get past it; did anything in the guide mislead it; did it prove nothing moved.
- Write it up as `## Fourth trial: from the starting prompt, on the released SDK` in `docs/plans/sdk-theme-host-burden.md`, leading with the answer in three lines, then fix in the guide and the skill whatever misled it and say what you changed.
- Put that app on Peter's iPhone by direct install (Sandsend's CLAUDE.md gives the commands for his phone), on the brand theme. His phone has been unreachable from this Mac since 10:40 today, by CoreDevice and by the bridge. A job is already waiting to install an earlier trial build (`/tmp/sandsend-zero-install.sh`, log beside it): stop that job and replace it with one of your own for the new build, on the same pattern, so the newest build is the one that lands. Peter judges work by what is on his phone and has said twice that work which stops at "committed" reads to him as nothing done.

YOUR REPORT, IN THE TASK NOTE AND AS YOUR FINAL REPLY
What shipped and where each lives; the live web build and the SDK version; the starter rows as they read; the fourth trial's answer; what you changed in the guide after it; the recommendation of the skills proposal in two lines; what is on Peter's phone or waiting to be; and for each claim whether you ran it or reasoned it.

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

# Claude

## Project Overview

Ripul is an AI-powered workflow automation platform. This is the monorepo containing all three packages.

### Monorepo Structure

```
ripul/
├── chrome-extension/     Web application + lightweight Chrome extension
├── ripul-native-app/     SwiftUI app (iOS + macOS) wrapping the web app
├── ripul-ios-sdk/        Swift Package bridging native apps ↔ web agent
└── website/              Public site at app.ripul.io (plain HTML, own deploy — see website/README.md)
```

| Package | Tech | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| **chrome-extension** | React 19, TypeScript, Cloudflare Pages/Workers | Primary codebase — web app deployed to `demo.ripul.io` (the canonical app host; all clients load it from there), plus a minimal Chrome extension for browser API proxying |
| **ripul-native-app** | SwiftUI, iOS + macOS | Native shell wrapping the web app in WKWebView with native tools, push notifications, Live Activities, CLI servers (macOS) |
| **ripul-ios-sdk** | Swift Package | Core bridge library — AgentView, AgentBridge, NativeTool protocol, capability system, web↔native communication |

### How They Fit Together

```
chrome-extension (web app)
        │ Embedded in WKWebView via agent-framework:* message protocol
ripul-native-app (native shell)
        │ imports RipulAgent SPM package
ripul-ios-sdk (bridge library)
```

The web app auto-detects its runtime context:
- **web-only** — standalone browser, graceful fallback
- **bridged** — minimal Chrome extension present
- **native** — running in WKWebView with native capabilities

### Development Focus
- **DO**: Develop features in the web application (chrome-extension)
- **DO**: Keep the lightweight Chrome extension minimal (only browser API features)
- **DON'T**: Frame this project as "a Chrome extension" — it's a web application
- **DON'T**: Add new features to the legacy full extension code

---

## Documentation

Each package has its own docs. Key cross-cutting references:

| Document | Location | Contents |
|----------|----------|----------|
| **PROJECT-STRUCTURE.md** | `chrome-extension/docs/` | Cross-repo architecture, message protocol, build commands |
| **GLOSSARY.md** | `chrome-extension/` | Core domain terms (Tool, Prompt, PromptTool, MCP, etc.) |
| **NATIVE-BRIDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md** | `chrome-extension/docs/` | Native iOS ↔ web communication patterns |
| **iOS Styling Guide** | `ripul-native-app/docs/` | Native glass effects, vibrancy, glass modifier library |
| **Build & Deploy** | `ripul-native-app/docs/` | How to build, install, and run on macOS and iOS |
| **[Tools System Architecture](chrome-extension/docs/architecture/toolsSystemArchitecture.md)** | `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/` | End-to-end guide: definitions → interceptors → handlers → CLI bridge → native tools |
| **[Private functions and store builds](ripul-native-app/docs/app-store-private-apis.md)** | `ripul-native-app/docs/` | What is private, which builds may carry it, the check that stops an upload, the pre-submission checklist |
| **[MCP Tool Surfaces](chrome-extension/docs/architecture/mcpToolSurfaces.md)** | `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/` | Cross-package map of every MCP/tool surface: why each context exists, consumers, transports, prefixes (`host_`/`device_`/`web_tool_`), gates. Start here for anything spanning CLI/native/device/extension tools |
| **[The Ripul Library](chrome-extension/docs/architecture/artefactLibrary.md)** | `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/` | The public library of artefacts: the rules (one revision, reviewed before it is listed, copy, report, block), storage, routes, where it shows on the web, in the apps and to agents, and the tests |
| **[Ripul guides](chrome-extension/docs/architecture/ripulGuide.md)** | `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/` | How product knowledge reaches agents on other people's repos: the one-paragraph harness note, the `ripul_guide` tool, and the guides in `public/guides/`. How to add a guide |
| **[The command orchestrator](chrome-extension/docs/architecture/commandOrchestrator.md)** | `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/` | A fast hosted model (Haiku) that turns one spoken sentence into app actions, with the app's registered actions as its tools. How to switch it on, how a request flows, the rules it keeps, what was measured, limits and tests |
| **[Shell chats](chrome-extension/docs/architecture/shellChats.md)** | `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/` | The Shell model: a chat whose messages run as commands in a zsh on the Mac host. What it does, its limits, how a turn flows, the server routes, the files and the tests |
| **[Workflow runs](chrome-extension/docs/architecture/workflowRuns.md)** | `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/` | How a Claude Code workflow run shows its phases and agents in a chat: what the CLI sends, the record a finished run leaves, the limits, and what is not built (stopping a run) |
| **[Sub-agents in a chat](chrome-extension/docs/architecture/agentRuns.md)** | `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/` | How a sub-agent shows as a full-width row in a chat, the row a workflow run has: what the CLI sends for it, where its title, totals and latest actions come from, the limits, and what is not built |
| **[Milestones in a chat](chrome-extension/docs/architecture/chatMilestones.md)** | `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/` | What a chat has achieved, recorded by the agent with the `milestone` tool and shown first in the chat's side panel: how one is stored, how its commits and deployments are bracketed, the jump that pages older history in, the two folds held to one fixture, the limits and the tests |

---

## Common Commands

### chrome-extension (Web App)

> **No local dev server.** The workflow is: edit → TypeScript check → `deploy:all`. All clients (browser, iOS, macOS) load the web app from Cloudflare. Do not start or look for a local dev server.

> **Deploys go through Trainyard.** `npm run deploy:all` boards the web train rather than deploying. It needs a pushed commit on `main`, and it waits and then reports what went live. One run serves every agent waiting. It holds while anyone is testing, refuses to ship a held-back commit, and reloads the host only when the other agents are idle. **Before a test that depends on the live build or the host, take a hold**: `ripul-train hold host-webview --reason "…" --ttl 20`, then `ripul-train release <id>` when done. For "don't ship this yet", use `ripul-train block <commit> --reason "…"`. Check the state with `ripul-train status`. A chat that asked for a train and is not mid-turn when it ends is told in its own chat, which starts its next turn (`ripul-train notices off` stops that). Rebuild the Mac host with `ripul-train request mac-host --wait`, not a raw `xcodebuild`, so the relaunch waits for every agent's turn to end. iPhone, simulator and TestFlight builds board trains too: `ship_ios.py` / `ship-ota.sh`, `ship_duo_sim.py` and `deploy-testflight.sh` request the `ios`, `ios-sim` and `testflight` tracks by themselves, and all native tracks share one lane, so builds queue instead of failing on the release lock. They ship committed work only. Take `ripul-train hold iphone` while testing on the phone. **To use a simulator, borrow one**: `ripul-train acquire simulators os=26 type=iPhone --reason "…" --wait` says which simulator is yours and waits if all that match are taken, `ripul-train release <lease>` gives it back, and `ripul-train pools` shows who holds what. An install to a borrowed simulator waits for its holder. `deploy:all:direct` skips all of this; `deploy:all` falls back to it by itself if Trainyard isn't running. Details are in `ripul-native-app/macOS/trainyard/README.md`, and the design in `docs/plans/agent-build-trains.md`.
>
> **Concurrent deploys queue; they no longer corrupt each other.** `build:prod` starts with `clean` (`premove public/js`), and wrangler uploads by listing `public/` then opening each file — so a build started by *any* session used to delete the files another session's upload was midway through sending. Symptom: `Failed to upload files … ENOENT: chunk-<build>-<hash>.js`, or an upload that crawls (459s measured, against 13s uncontended). `deploy:pages` now runs under a machine-wide lock (`scripts/with-deploy-lock.mjs`, atomic mkdir on `/tmp` — macOS has no `flock`). A second deploy waits and says who it is waiting for; a dead holder is detected by PID and its lock broken.
>
> **A healthy `deploy:all` is ~35 seconds.** If one runs into minutes, suspect contention rather than bandwidth.
>
> **Never trust the deploy exit code alone.** Wrangler can crash *inside its own error handler* (`TypeError: The "code" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('ENOENT')`) and still exit 0, and `concurrently` then runs the `&& seed` chain on top of a Pages deploy that never happened — so a failed deploy prints success end to end. `deploy:all` now ends with `verify:pages`, which compares the built `public/version.json` against the live `demo.ripul.io/version.json` (with no-cache headers — the custom domain can serve a stale `version.json` even past a query-string buster) and fails loudly on a mismatch.

```bash
cd chrome-extension
npm run build            # esbuild → public/js/
npm run build:prod       # Production build with minification
npm run build:extension  # Minimal extension → dist/minimal-extension/
npm run deploy:all       # Board the web train: pages + worker + webhook + seed tools + verify
npm run deploy:all -- --checked   # …when you already ran tsgo on this exact commit
npx tsgo --noEmit        # TypeScript check (required after changes)
```

### ripul-native-app

See [Build & Deploy docs](ripul-native-app/docs/build-and-deploy.md) for full details including OTA/IPA deployment.

```bash
cd ripul-native-app
xcodegen generate           # Required after clone or project.yml changes

# iOS — build and install to device (requires USB or same Wi-Fi)
# Use -derivedDataPath build so both steps read/write the same pinned location.
# Without it, ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/RipulNativeApp-*/ may match
# stale dirs from old checkouts and you'll install a stale binary.
xcodebuild -scheme RipulApp \
  -destination 'platform=iOS,id=00008150-001C544E0EBA401C' \
  -derivedDataPath build \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=C7AA358R56 CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
  build
xcrun devicectl device install app \
  --device 00008150-001C544E0EBA401C \
  build/Build/Products/Debug-iphoneos/Ripul.app

# iOS — OTA deploy (when device is not on the network)
# ship-ota.sh uses -configuration Debug (same as device builds) and the shared
# ripul-native-app/build DerivedData — so .o files are reused across device
# builds, OTA archives, and the Alice variant. First run ~3-5 min, warm ~30 sec.
# NEVER write ad-hoc scripts — fresh /tmp/ paths + Release config = full cold build.
nohup bash ripul-native-app/scripts/ship-ota.sh > /tmp/ship-ota.log 2>&1 & disown
# Skip Alice: SKIP_ALICE=1 nohup bash ripul-native-app/scripts/ship-ota.sh ...
# Progress: tail -f /tmp/ship-ota.log

# iOS — TestFlight (the front door for testers who are NOT on the device list)
# Dev OTA embeds a UDID list, so a new tester costs a UDID + registration +
# rebuild. TestFlight costs an email. Use it for anyone outside your inner loop;
# keep ship-ota.sh for your own iteration. ~15-20 min. Full runbook:
# ripul-native-app/docs/testflight-deploy.md
nohup bash ripul-native-app/scripts/deploy-testflight.sh > /tmp/ripul-testflight.log 2>&1 & disown
# Archive + export without uploading anything to Apple: ... deploy-testflight.sh export
# This is the ONE sanctioned exception to the "no fresh /tmp + Release" rule
# above: App Store signing REQUIRES Release, and a Release archive shares no .o
# files with the Debug caches, so it must not be pointed at build/.

# macOS — NOTE the separate DerivedData (`build-mac`, not `build`).
# `build` is the SHARED iOS DerivedData (device builds, ship-ota.sh's SHARED_DD,
# the Alice variant). A fresh build into it recreates Build/Products, which
# DELETES the macOS Debug/Ripul.app sitting there — and because the Dock
# bookmarks that bundle by path, the Ripul icon turns into a question mark and
# the host won't launch (observed 2026-09-07). Keeping macOS in its own
# DerivedData makes it immune to any iOS build. Dock THIS path.
xcodebuild -scheme RipulMac -destination 'platform=macOS' -derivedDataPath build-mac \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=C7AA358R56 CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic build
open ripul-native-app/build-mac/Build/Products/Debug/Ripul.app
```

### iPhones away from the Mac — `ripul-bridge` (Tailscale)

Agents: use the `host_bridge_*` tools (`bridge_status`, `bridge_install`, `bridge_ship`, `bridge_screenshot`, `bridge_debug`, …) — the Mac host wraps the command for you; people use **Devices** in the iPhone or Catalyst sidebar (one list of phones, with Live View of their apps and, under Whole Screen, the [device runner](ripul-native-app/device-runner/README.md) for everything else on the phone), and Settings → iPhones over Tailscale on the Mac to set up. A phone pairs by being plugged into the Mac once: nothing to choose or press (`ripul-bridge autopair`, run by the host when a phone is plugged in). Underneath, `ripul-native-app/device-bridge/ripul-bridge` does Xcode-level work on a paired iPhone anywhere on the tailnet: `install` (exact build read back), `launch`, `terminate`, `screenshot`, `debug` (attached LLDB), `mount-ddi`. `ship-ios.sh` uses it automatically when CoreDevice can't see the phone (route order CoreDevice → bridge → OTA; `--transport bridge` forces it). Start with `ripul-bridge status --deep`. The phone must be on **Wi-Fi or another phone's hotspot** with Tailscale on; on its own cellular it refuses new tunnels. `debug` remounts the disk image itself after a phone reboot; `ripul-bridge symbols <phone>` fetches debug symbols over the network once per iOS version. Setup, pairing and limits: [device-bridge/README.md](ripul-native-app/device-bridge/README.md).

### Mac Catalyst build path

Always use `ripul-native-app/build-catalyst` for Catalyst (`RipulApp`, destination `platform=macOS,variant=Mac Catalyst`). Build with `-derivedDataPath build-catalyst` from `ripul-native-app`, then launch and Dock `build-catalyst/Build/Products/Debug-maccatalyst/Ripul.app`. Never switch this path between rebuilds. Native macOS uses `build-mac`; iOS device/OTA uses `build`. The complete Catalyst signing command is in [build-and-deploy.md](ripul-native-app/docs/build-and-deploy.md#mac-catalyst).

### DerivedData: the sanctioned paths, and no others

These are the only sanctioned `-derivedDataPath` values. Use one of them. Never invent a new one.

| Path | Used for |
|---|---|
| `ripul-native-app/build` | iOS **device** + simulator-less archives, and `ship-ota.sh` (its `SHARED_DD`) |
| `ripul-native-app/build-variant-alice` | the Alice variant (`ship_ios.py` drives this; do not reuse it for anything else) |
| `ripul-native-app/build-iossim` | **iOS Simulator**, including iPhone Duo (`ship_duo_sim.py`) |
| `ripul-native-app/build-mac` | native macOS (`RipulMac`) |
| `ripul-native-app/build-mac-alice` | Ripul Host Alice, the second host for clean installs (`build_mac.py --variant alice`) |
| `ripul-native-app/build-catalyst` | Mac Catalyst (`RipulApp`, `variant=Mac Catalyst`) |

They are separate *on purpose*, for two different reasons.

**Products would delete each other.** An iOS build into `build` recreates `Build/Products`, which deletes a macOS or Catalyst `Ripul.app` sitting at the same path — that is what turns a Docked icon into a question mark.

**One Xcode: 27.1.** Every script builds with `/Applications/Xcode-27.1.app`, on both Macs, and no other Xcode should be installed beside it (Peter, 5 October 2026: "we need to be on 27.1 and that's it"). To try a newer one, use `ripul-native-app/scripts/try-xcode.sh`, and remove the old one when moving over. Before that date the two Macs held seven copies of four versions and scripts preferred different ones: the same commit was built with different toolchains on each Mac, and two toolchains sharing one DerivedData cost a full cold rebuild on every alternation. That is where the separate `build-iossim` came from. It stays: the scripts and their warm caches are built around these paths.

**Why this rule exists.** Sessions kept inventing a fresh path for one-off builds — `build-sim`, `build-simulator`, `build-iossim-artefacts` were three more names for the same simulator job — and nothing ever deleted them. By 2026-09-15 there were 16 such directories holding **26.4 GB**, and 18 `Ripul.app` bundles claiming the same two bundle ids. A throwaway path also costs you a *cold* build every time, since it shares no `.o` files with the warm caches. Those duplicates were deleted on 2026-09-25; `build-iossim` is the one simulator path that survives. Do not recreate the others.

If you genuinely need an isolated build, put it under `/tmp` so it cannot accumulate, and say so in your report.

### Which Ripul am I running?

Two different apps ship from this repo. They are separate applications, not two builds of one:

| App | Scheme | Bundle id | Display name | Icon |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mac host | `RipulMac` | `io.ripul.mac` | **Ripul Host** | teal |
| Catalyst | `RipulApp` | `io.ripul.app` | **Ripul** | navy |

Both produce a bundle named `Ripul.app` and both can sit in the Dock at once — hence the distinct display names and icons. Do not "fix" either back to a shared name or icon; that is the whole point of them.

To see what is actually running, by path:

```bash
pgrep -lf "Ripul.app/Contents/MacOS/Ripul"
```

Launch by **path**, never by bundle id. `open -b io.ripul.mac` can resolve to a stale copy — e.g. a months-old `/Applications/Ripul.app` — rather than the build you just made.

**One host per checkout, enforced.** A Debug Ripul Host that is not this checkout's `build-mac` product opens the canonical one and exits (`macOS/CanonicalHostGuard.swift`). Set `RIPUL_ALLOW_NONCANONICAL_HOST=1` to run a deliberate test copy. **And one running host per profile, enforced.** The host and its watchdog each hold a kernel lock in the profile's Application Support folder (`macOS/SingleInstanceLock.swift`, `SingleHostGuard.swift`); a second launch of the same profile brings the first forward and exits, and a second watchdog exits. Before 8 October 2026 two watchdogs could watch one host, and each reopened it when it exited. A host that keeps its own folder, installation id and login runs beside the real one: that is what a variant such as Alice is, so test a second instance with a variant. The one sanctioned second host is **Ripul Host Alice** (`io.ripul.mac.alice`): a different bundle id, so the guard leaves it alone. `python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/build_mac.py --variant alice --fresh` wipes it back to a first install and launches it beside the real host ([build-and-deploy.md](ripul-native-app/docs/build-and-deploy.md#a-second-host-for-clean-installs-ripul-host-alice)). Both run as `…/Ripul.app/Contents/MacOS/Ripul`, so stop hosts by full path, never `killall Ripul`. `build_mac.py` also unregisters every other `io.ripul.mac` copy from LaunchServices after each build. **One running Catalyst app per install, too.** A second copy of `io.ripul.app` (an installed one beside a developer build, or `open -n`) brings the first forward and closes within about three seconds (`iOS/SingleRunningCopy.swift`). Two copies share one installation id and fight over one relay seat; on 2026-10-07 that sent a phone 12-38 MB a minute. So to run a new build, quit the running one first. `RIPUL_ALLOW_SECOND_COPY=1` lets a deliberate second copy run.

Never copy the host into `/Applications` or keep backup `.app`s beside the product: on 2026-09-26 a March build in `/Applications` had been hosting for five days and answering the phone.

### ripul-ios-sdk

```bash
cd ripul-ios-sdk
swift build                    # Build the package
# iOS sim. Use --triple: the older `-Xswiftc -sdk …` form builds for macOS whatever
# it is given (measured 10 October 2026: it passed a type error planted inside
# `#if os(iOS)`), and 151 of the SDK's files are iOS-only.
swift build --triple arm64-apple-ios17.0-simulator --sdk "$(xcrun --sdk iphonesimulator --show-sdk-path)"
```

## Private Apple functions never ship in a store build

Ripul is going to the App Store. App Store review rejects private Apple functions, so a build that reaches **TestFlight or the App Store must contain none**. Development builds may: Live View's real touches are private, and are compiled into Debug builds only.

1. **Compile it out, don't switch it off.** Any line that reaches a private function (by `dlsym`, a selector or class name built from a string, an underscore key, an underscore override) goes inside `#if DEBUG || RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`. A runtime check leaves the name in the binary.
2. **Never set `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`, and never use a Debug configuration, for a build going to TestFlight or the App Store.** Never put either in a project file, xcconfig or scheme. `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD` belongs only on the command line of a direct install to your own device.
3. **Run the check; don't trust memory.**
   ```bash
   python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_private_apis.py source          # the code
   python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_private_apis.py all <app|ipa>   # the code and a built app
   ```
   `deploy-testflight.sh` runs it on the app it is about to upload and refuses when it fails. A developer-only name in the app, or a lookup nobody has reviewed, has no override.
4. **`RIPUL_ALLOW_KNOWN_PRIVATE_APIS=1` is for tester builds only**, while the known uses remain. **Never for a build submitted for App Store review.**
5. **Ripul Host (the Mac host) is distributed directly, not through the Mac App Store.** It uses private macOS functions to give windows keyboard focus.

Known uses still in every build on 29 September 2026: the in-app browser's mouse (`iOS/BrowserNativeMouse.swift`, the real risk), agent actuation of alerts and recognizers, the keyboard bar subclass, and a demangler lookup. The inventory, the ways out and the pre-submission checklist: [app-store-private-apis.md](ripul-native-app/docs/app-store-private-apis.md).

## Proving the build is live (do this FIRST — never unravel bundles)

When something looks broken on a client (Mac/iOS/web), **do not theorize about stale builds or pull apart chunks.** There is one immediate signal:

1. **Deployed version (server):** `curl -s https://demo.ripul.io/version.json` → `{ "version": "...", "builtAt": "..." }`. (`demo.ripul.io` is the canonical app host — all clients, including the native iOS/macOS shells, load it from there. Static file, served by Pages, not `/api`.) NOTE: `app.ripul.io` is **not the app** — since 8 October 2026 it is the public website (`website/`, a separate Cloudflare Worker), so it has no `version.json`, `/popup` or `/js/*`. Do not use it to check builds or assume the app is hosted there.
2. **Running version (client):** the app logs at boot, via `console.log`:
   - `[RIPUL] build=<version> origin=<host>`
   - `[RIPUL] LIVE ✓ running=<v> deployed=<v>` **or** `[RIPUL] STALE ✗ running=<v> deployed=<v>` (it self-checks against `/version.json`).

`LIVE ✓` (or running == deployed) → on the current build, **move on; not stale.** `STALE ✗` → force a reload/relaunch. (Wiping web data is NOT a staleness test — login persists via a native-injected session; trust the version signal.) `version.json` is written by `scripts/build.mjs` and matches `__BUILD_VERSION__` in the bundle.

`chrome-extension/public/version.json` is **gitignored, not tracked** — it is regenerated on every build, and `deploy:pages` rebuilds it immediately before upload, so the deployed file never comes from git. Never commit it, never `git add` it, and never treat its absence from `git status` (or its on-disk contents) as a problem.

---

## Workflow Rules

### Long-running commands — run them DETACHED from the session

**This applies to any command that runs longer than a single turn: iOS/macOS archives, OTA deploys, `deploy:all`, long `xcodebuild` runs, IPA exports.**

In the Ripul CLI environment (the iPhone/Mac CLI runs *inside* Ripul.app — see the runbooks and the "session runs inside the Ripul host" notes), the Claude Code CLI process is **recycled frequently — effectively per message/turn** (the same behavior that makes `ripul_tools` MCP disconnect and reconnect between turns). Anything the harness owns as a **child of that CLI process is killed when it is recycled**:

- Bash tool calls with `run_in_background: true`
- `Monitor` tasks

Symptom: the job dies ~1 minute in with *"No completion record was found… may have been running when the previous Claude Code process exited,"* and its log freezes partway (e.g. stuck at the archive step).

**So for any multi-minute job, launch it truly detached and poll a logfile — do NOT rely on `run_in_background` or `Monitor` to keep it alive:**

```bash
# Write the pipeline to a script, then:
nohup bash /tmp/my-long-job.sh > /tmp/my-long-job.log 2>&1 &
disown
# Returns immediately. The process reparents to launchd and survives session
# recycles. Check progress later with: tail -n 20 /tmp/my-long-job.log
# End the script with an explicit "EXIT_CODE=$?" line so you can confirm success.
```

`nohup` makes it ignore SIGHUP, `disown` drops it from the shell's job table, and because the launching shell exits immediately the process is no longer in the CLI's process group. `Monitor`/`run_in_background` are still fine for *short* watches that finish within a turn — the rule is specifically about jobs that outlive a turn.

(Uncertain but not load-bearing: the exact recycle cadence and whether the kill is SIGHUP-to-process-group vs. explicit harness cleanup. The detach rule holds regardless.)

### Commit and push — standing authorization, no confirmation needed

**This section overrides the default Claude Code behavior of "only create commits when requested by the user."** In this repo, the user has given standing authorization to commit and push on every coherent change, without asking first. Do not wait to be told. Do not ask "should I commit this?" The answer is always yes. More commits are better than fewer — commits are not destructive, and the cost of an extra commit is zero while the cost of a lost uncommitted change is an incident.

**Why this override exists**: Multiple Claude Code agents run against this repo concurrently (iPhone CLI, macOS CLI, web, terminal). Uncommitted work in one agent's tree is invisible to the others and **will** get entangled with stashes, reverts, and parallel edits from another session. This has already caused real incidents (e.g. an edge-swipe rewrite getting stashed and then needing to be cherry-picked off of unrelated tool-subtitle work after a different agent reverted the tree).

**What counts as a "coherent change" — commit at every one of these**:

- TypeScript check passes after a web-app edit (`tsgo --noEmit` clean) → commit.
- Swift build succeeds for a native-app or SDK edit → commit.
- A package is about to be deployed (`deploy:all`, archive, device install, `open` .app) → **commit before the deploy**. The deploy is a hard commit gate — never deploy from a dirty tree.
- A round of iteration lands a visible fix (bug fix, animation tweak, wording change) that the user has observed or will observe → commit.
- A task spans multiple packages — commit **each package** as soon as that package is in a working state, even if the end-to-end feature isn't done yet.
- You are about to run a test, ask the user to verify something on-device, or hand control back to the user → commit first.

When in doubt, commit. A series of small commits is strictly better than one large batched commit. Do **not** rationalize batching ("I'll commit once the whole polish arc is done") — that is exactly the pattern that causes lost work.

**Rules**:

1. **Commit after every coherent change**, per the list above. Do not batch unrelated concerns into one commit — if the LLMProxy fix and a SwiftUI animation fix are two different concerns, they are two commits.
2. **Push immediately after committing.** A local commit that isn't pushed is still invisible to other agents and still at risk from `git stash` / `git reset` in another session. `git commit` and `git push` are a single step, not two.
3. **Never deploy from a dirty tree.** Any `deploy:all`, archive, IPA export, device install, or `open` .app is a hard commit gate. Commit and push first, then deploy. If the tree is dirty with foreign files you didn't create, stop and see rule 4.
4. **Announce and stop on a foreign dirty tree at session start.** The first thing you do in any session that touches git-tracked files is run `git status`. If there are uncommitted changes you did not create, your **first response to the user** must announce them and ask what to do. Do not silently work around them. Do not stash them. Do not revert them. Those changes belong to another agent and only the user knows whether they're safe to touch.
5. **Never use `git stash` as a workflow tool.** Stashes are invisible to other agents and easy to lose. If you need to set work aside, commit it to a branch instead.
6. **If a task spans web + native + SDK**, commit and push each package's changes as soon as that package is in a working state — don't wait until everything builds end-to-end. Partial progress on `main` is strictly better than a pile of uncommitted cross-package edits that another agent might revert.
7. **Before doing anything destructive** (`git checkout HEAD --`, `git reset`, `git stash drop`, force push), re-read `git status` and `git stash list` and confirm with the user. Destructive operations in a multi-agent environment can wipe out another session's in-progress work.

**What "standing authorization" does NOT cover**: destructive operations (rule 7), force pushes, amending published commits, and committing files that look like secrets — these still require an explicit user confirmation every time. Standing authorization is for the happy path: edit → verify → commit → push.

### Session transcripts are captured automatically — commit however you like

Every commit a Claude session makes inside the Ripul host leaves that session's transcript on the repo's `claude-sessions` branch, so the chat can be picked up on another Mac if this one is lost. Plain `git commit` in the shell counts; no special tool is needed, and there is nothing for an agent to do.

- **How:** the host gives the CLI processes it launches its own git hooks directory, through `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment variables. Nothing is written to any repo. Each hook runs the repo's own hook of the same name first; `post-commit` then flags the commit. The host uploads the transcript a few seconds after the commit and again when the turn ends.
- **`git config core.hooksPath` showing `~/.ripul/session-capture/hooks` inside a session is this, not a fault.** Do not unset it or "repair" it.
- **Checking it:** `GET /host/diagnostics` on the host's port lists the last captures under `sessionCapture`, failures included.
- **Switch:** Settings → Coding Agents → Claude → Save Transcripts With Commits (on by default; also changeable from a paired phone).
- **Not covered:** Codex and Antigravity chats, and sessions started outside the host (a plain terminal).
- **Where it shows up:** the iPhone and Catalyst **Repos** screen. Each repo has two views of the same commits: **History** (`iOS/RepoGraphView.swift`) is git's own order, with a marker in the chat's colour on each commit a captured chat made, and **Chats** (`iOS/RepoChatsView.swift`) lists the chats, each row opening to all the commits that chat made. History never regroups by chat: on a branch several agents share, chats take turns, and grouping by adjacency split one chat into a block plus strays. There is no separate Sessions/Commits screen on iPhone any more.
- **Rescue:** a chat's detail has "Continue on <Mac>". That Mac fetches the branch and imports the newest transcript as a new chat of its own (`agent:gitRescueSession` → `importTranscriptOnHost.ts`, the same import a Move uses). The chat's original Mac is not contacted and keeps its copy. It is explicit and user-triggered, like Move; nothing re-homes a chat by itself.

Code: `ripul-native-app/macOS/SessionCapture.swift` (hook, queue, timing), `SessionCaptureRunner.swift`, `session-capture.mjs`. Tests: `bash ripul-native-app/Tests/SessionCapture/run.sh`.

### Git worktrees — branch isolation for features

Multiple agents often work on this repo concurrently. When an agent is working on a distinct feature (not a quick fix), it should use a **git worktree** to avoid interleaving commits with other agents on `main`.

**At the start of a session**, if the user describes a feature or multi-step task, ask:

> "Should I create a worktree for this? I'll work on a feature branch in an isolated directory so it doesn't interfere with other sessions on main."

If the user says yes, call the `EnterWorktree` tool with a descriptive name:
```
EnterWorktree({ name: "share-links" })
```

This creates a worktree directory with its own checkout on a new branch and **switches the session's working directory** to it. All subsequent file edits and git operations happen in that directory. Other agents on `main` are completely unaffected.

**Rules**:
1. **One worktree per feature** — don't create multiple worktrees in the same session.
2. **Commit and push normally** — session capture follows the commit, not the directory, so it works in a worktree too.
3. **Don't merge back yourself** — when the feature is done, tell the user it's ready for a PR from the feature branch. Don't merge into main without being asked.
4. **Quick fixes stay on main** — if the task is a one-commit bug fix or tweak, a worktree is overkill. Use your judgment.

### What to Deploy After Changes

The web app loads live from Cloudflare; the native app loads it in a WKWebView. Changes to different packages require different deploy steps to be testable:

| What changed | Deploy steps | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Web app only** (chrome-extension) | `deploy:all` | Web app is served from Cloudflare — all clients (browser, iOS, macOS) load it remotely |
| **iOS app only** (ripul-native-app, iOS scheme) | Rebuild `RipulApp` scheme and install to iPhone | Native shell runs on-device — web app is unchanged |
| **macOS app only** (ripul-native-app, Mac scheme) | Rebuild `RipulMac` scheme and `open` the .app | Native shell runs locally — web app is unchanged |
| **iOS SDK only** (ripul-ios-sdk) | Rebuild and install **both** native apps (iOS + macOS) | Both apps consume the SDK via SPM — SDK changes only take effect after rebuilding |
| **Web app + iOS app** | `deploy:all` first, then rebuild and install iOS app | Web app must be live before the native app loads it |
| **Web app + macOS app** | `deploy:all` first, then rebuild and launch macOS app | Same — web app must be live first |
| **Web app + iOS SDK** | `deploy:all`, then rebuild and install both native apps | Both sides need updating |
| **All three** | `deploy:all`, then rebuild and install both native apps | SDK is compiled into native apps, web app is loaded at runtime |

**Key insights**:
- Web-only changes (UI, chat, tools, worker) never require a native app rebuild — just `deploy:all`. All clients pick up the new web app automatically.
- A native rebuild is only needed when Swift code changes (native app or SDK).
- iOS and macOS are separate build schemes (`RipulApp` / `RipulMac`) — rebuild whichever platform you're testing on, or both if the change is in shared code or the SDK.

---

## Code Quality Rules

### After Code Changes (Web App)
1. **Always run TypeScript compilation check**:
   ```bash
   cd chrome-extension && npx tsgo --noEmit
   ```
2. Fix any TypeScript errors before considering the task complete

### Cross-Package Changes

| If you're changing... | You may also need to update... |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------|
| Web app message protocol | `AgentBridge.swift` in ripul-ios-sdk |
| Native tool schema format | `NativeTool.swift` in ripul-ios-sdk, tool registrations in ripul-native-app |
| Context adapter behavior | `src/hosted-app/NativeBridge.ts` in chrome-extension |
| Agent activity events | `AgentActivityAttributes.swift` in ripul-native-app, `AgentBridge.swift` in ripul-ios-sdk |
| Capability handlers | Both `src/minimal-extension/capabilities/` (extension) and `Shared/Capabilities/` (native) |
| Chat session model | `AgentBridge.swift` (SDK), `SessionsListSections.swift` (native app), web app session code |

---

## Technical Guidelines

### Styling (Web App)
- Use MUI theme tokens (`'text.primary'`, `'action.hover'`, `'divider'`) instead of hardcoded rgba values
- Never pass string tokens to `alpha()` — resolve via `theme.palette.X.main` first
- Use `useThemeColors()` hook for common color calculations
- **Colours and typefaces come from the theme, never from a literal.** No hex or `rgba(` colour and no `fontFamily` string at a call site. Read a palette token, `alpha()` of a palette value, a named colour (`useNamedColours()`, for a colour with a job that equals no palette value) or a family (`useFontFamilies()`: `text`, `display`, `code`). A colour that is data (syntax, terminal, a provider's or a model's) is marked `// theme-exempt: <reason>`. Before pushing, run `node scripts/check-theme-literals.mjs --strict <paths>` in `chrome-extension`. Every build runs the check: `src/logging/components/chat/` and `src/logging/panels/` are finished, so a literal there fails the build, and elsewhere it warns until that directory's stream finishes.
- See `chrome-extension/docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md`

### UI Element Traceability (Web App)
- Add `data-ui` attribute to every rendered element in React components
- Format: `ComponentName.section.element` — static values only, no runtime data
- **MUI compound components** (`TextField`, `Autocomplete`, `Slider`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, etc.) render multiple DOM layers — `data-ui` on the component prop lands on the outer wrapper `div`, not the interactive `<input>`. For any MUI component wrapping a focusable element, also pass `data-ui` through `slotProps`:
  ```tsx
  // ❌ data-ui only reaches the wrapper div
  <TextField data-ui="Foo.bar" />

  // ✅ data-ui also reaches the <input>
  <TextField
    data-ui="Foo.bar"
    slotProps={{ htmlInput: { 'data-ui': 'Foo.bar' } }}
  />
  ```

### API Client & Authentication (Web App)
- All authenticated API calls must flow through `useLlmProxyClient()` / `useLlmProxyService()` hooks
- Never create `ApiClient` instances with `ClerkAuthProvider` outside approved hooks
- See the chrome-extension CLAUDE.md for full details

### Native (iOS/macOS)
- **XcodeGen required**: The `.xcodeproj` is generated and gitignored — `project.yml` is the source of truth. Run `xcodegen generate` after cloning and after any changes to `project.yml` or source file additions/removals. Never edit the `.xcodeproj` directly.
- Prefer `.glassEffect(.clear)` over `.regular` for iOS 26+ glass effects
- Use `.ultraThinMaterial` fallback for pre-iOS 26
- **Native-first for block ports**: when porting a web block/UI to native, use the platform's native control wherever one exists (sidebar → `List(.sidebar)`, date → `DatePicker`/`UICalendarView`, menu → `Menu`/`Picker`, modal → sheet w/ detents). Mirror semantics exactly; rebuild presentation natively; drop web-only presentation knobs. Re-skinning the web look in SwiftUI is a defect. See the [CmsRender doctrine](ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/CmsRender/README.md) (Rule 0) and the iOS styling guide's "Native-first" section.
- **Present sheets with `.ripulSheet(isPresented:)` / `.ripulSheet(item:)`, never a bare `.sheet`.** Mac Catalyst ignores detents, so a bare sheet gets UIKit's fixed phone-sized box whatever the window size. The wrappers (`ripul-ios-sdk`, `SheetPresentation.swift`) size the sheet for the window by default; pass `size: .form` for a genuinely short form. The app build runs `scripts/check_sheet_sizing.py` and fails on a bare one.
- **Fonts and colours come from the theme accessors, never from a literal.** Write `.font(.ripul(.caption))`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))`, `Color.ripul(.danger)`, `UIColor.ripul(.canvas)`, and `Color.ripul(system: .secondarySystemBackground)` where no role fits; `.tint` and `Color.accentColor` stay as they are. Each default is the system value it replaces, so nothing changes on screen until a theme names the token. A style is replaced by the style form and a `Color` by the Color form: the two draw different pixels in a list row. A colour that is data (a provider's, a model's, a chat's) is marked `// theme-exempt: <reason>`. The contract, the table that gives the one token for each literal, and the limits are in [theming.md](ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md). Before pushing, run `python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_theme_tokens.py --paths <file or directory>...` and `python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py --lint`. The app build runs the check: `ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/Sessions/` is finished, so a direct font or colour there fails the build, and elsewhere it warns until that stream finishes.
- See `ripul-native-app/docs/ios-styling-guide.md`

## Shared project memories
Before working, read `.ripul/memories/MEMORY.md` relative to this repository root and follow the relevant category links. Only the enabled memories in that index are in scope. Save new memories as individual Markdown files with a name and description in YAML frontmatter in `.ripul/memories/`, and update its index. Do not search other memory stores or recover disabled memories.
### Memory scope tags

Every memory carries `metadata.scope` in its front matter: `repo` (with `metadata.repo`: `ripul`, `wac-cms`, …), `product` (what an agent using Ripul on some other repo needs to know), `person` (Peter's own rules, true in any repo) or `environment` (his machines, phones and accounts). Set it on every new memory. A memory about another codebase belongs in that codebase's own memory folder, not here: `.ripul/memories/reference_memories_live_with_their_repo.md` says where each one is.

- [iPhone device ID](device_iphone.md) — wireless deploy ID B1982F55, IPA export flow
- [Scroll stutter testing is idle](feedback_scroll_testing.md) — user tests chat scroll with nothing streaming; don't blame streaming content
- [Mobile-first product rule](feedback_mobile_first.md) — UX targets are iPhone + Catalyst; the Mac host is a server and needs no UX parity
- [Don't optimise for legacy chats](feedback_legacy_chat_tradeoffs.md) — on infra rollouts, prefer clean designs even if pre-existing chats degrade
- [Permission friction](feedback_permission_friction.md) — use broad prefix patterns, never exact-command grants; acceptEdits is the project default
- [Deploy flow](feedback_deploy_flow.md) — push works now (osxkeychain); commit → push → deploy:all
- [Wrangler em-dash bug](feedback_wrangler_em_dash.md) — pages deploy fails on multi-byte UTF-8 in HEAD commit; pass --commit-message explicitly
- [SessionChannel DO 128MB OOM](project_do_oom_lesson.md) — DO OOM resets isolate silently; cap body fetches by bytes + serialize concurrent fetches
- [iOS list consistency](feedback_list_consistency.md) — extend GlassListSection for swipe/tap; never roll custom DragGesture in a row
- [WAC payslip repo](project_wac_payslip_repo.md) — WAC_ios_final; shift-rate-templates merged into v3 (live branch since 2026-09-29); lowercase branch names; stale xcconfig = launch crash
- [WAC paywall security is not a concern](feedback_wac_paywall_security.md) — never weight client-side premium gating as a risk; billing is bookkeeping only
- [WAC client-side strategy](project_wac_client_side_strategy.md) — move derivations to the client, Rails (wac_new) becomes a simple data store, local store + delta sync needed first
- [One Xcode: 27.1](project_xcode_27_1.md) — only /Applications/Xcode-27.1.app on both Macs (done 5 Oct 2026); Xcode.app is a link to it on purpose; simulators show in Device Hub
- [TestFlight: when it is welcome](feedback_no_testflight.md) — sideload when he asks about a specific phone; TestFlight by invitation is what the public site says (8 Oct 2026)
- [GitKraken hooks removed](project_gitkraken_hooks.md) — GitKraken Desktop reinstalls Claude/Codex hooks on launch; opt-out key + managed-settings lock
- [Drive it myself, then ask](feedback_ask_me_to_test.md) — test by driving the app (simulator, browser, tools) before asking him; ask only for what needs a person, with exact steps (8 Oct 2026)
- [Finish the release chain](feedback_finish_the_release_chain.md) — done means on his phone and visible; never stop at committed or simulator-checked and ask about the last step (said twice: 3 and 10 Oct 2026)

        │ Embedded in WKWebView via agent-framework:* message protocol
ripul-native-app (native shell)
        │ imports RipulAgent SPM package
ripul-ios-sdk (bridge library)
```

The web app auto-detects its runtime context:
- **web-only** — standalone browser, graceful fallback
- **bridged** — minimal Chrome extension present
- **native** — running in WKWebView with native capabilities

### Development Focus
- **DO**: Develop features in the web application (chrome-extension)
- **DO**: Keep the lightweight Chrome extension minimal (only browser API features)
- **DON'T**: Frame this project as "a Chrome extension" — it's a web application
- **DON'T**: Add new features to the legacy full extension code

## Common Commands

### chrome-extension (Web App)

> **No local dev server.** The workflow is: edit → TypeScript check → `deploy:all`. All clients (browser, iOS, macOS) load the web app from Cloudflare. Do not start or look for a local dev server.

> **Deploys go through Trainyard.** `npm run deploy:all` boards the web train rather than deploying. It needs a pushed commit on `main`, and it waits and then reports what went live. One run serves every agent waiting. It holds while anyone is testing, refuses to ship a held-back commit, and reloads the host only when the other agents are idle. **Before a test that depends on the live build or the host, take a hold**: `ripul-train hold host-webview --reason "…" --ttl 20`, then `ripul-train release <id>` when done. For "don't ship this yet", use `ripul-train block <commit> --reason "…"`. Check the state with `ripul-train status`. A chat that asked for a train and is not mid-turn when it ends is told in its own chat, which starts its next turn (`ripul-train notices off` stops that). Rebuild the Mac host with `ripul-train request mac-host --wait`, not a raw `xcodebuild`, so the relaunch waits for every agent's turn to end. iPhone, simulator and TestFlight builds board trains too: `ship_ios.py` / `ship-ota.sh`, `ship_duo_sim.py` and `deploy-testflight.sh` request the `ios`, `ios-sim` and `testflight` tracks by themselves, and all native tracks share one lane, so builds queue instead of failing on the release lock. They ship committed work only. Take `ripul-train hold iphone` while testing on the phone. **To use a simulator, borrow one**: `ripul-train acquire simulators os=26 type=iPhone --reason "…" --wait` says which simulator is yours and waits if all that match are taken, `ripul-train release <lease>` gives it back, and `ripul-train pools` shows who holds what. An install to a borrowed simulator waits for its holder. `deploy:all:direct` skips all of this; `deploy:all` falls back to it by itself if Trainyard isn't running. Details are in `ripul-native-app/macOS/trainyard/README.md`, and the design in `docs/plans/agent-build-trains.md`.
>
> **Concurrent deploys queue; they no longer corrupt each other.** `build:prod` starts with `clean` (`premove public/js`), and wrangler uploads by listing `public/` then opening each file — so a build started by *any* session used to delete the files another session's upload was midway through sending. Symptom: `Failed to upload files … ENOENT: chunk-<build>-<hash>.js`, or an upload that crawls (459s measured, against 13s uncontended). `deploy:pages` now runs under a machine-wide lock (`scripts/with-deploy-lock.mjs`, atomic mkdir on `/tmp` — macOS has no `flock`). A second deploy waits and says who it is waiting for; a dead holder is detected by PID and its lock broken.
>
> **A healthy `deploy:all` is ~35 seconds.** If one runs into minutes, suspect contention rather than bandwidth.
>
> **Never trust the deploy exit code alone.** Wrangler can crash *inside its own error handler* (`TypeError: The "code" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('ENOENT')`) and still exit 0, and `concurrently` then runs the `&& seed` chain on top of a Pages deploy that never happened — so a failed deploy prints success end to end. `deploy:all` now ends with `verify:pages`, which compares the built `public/version.json` against the live `demo.ripul.io/version.json` (with no-cache headers — the custom domain can serve a stale `version.json` even past a query-string buster) and fails loudly on a mismatch.

```bash
cd chrome-extension
npm run build            # esbuild → public/js/
npm run build:prod       # Production build with minification
npm run build:extension  # Minimal extension → dist/minimal-extension/
npm run deploy:all       # Board the web train: pages + worker + webhook + seed tools + verify
npm run deploy:all -- --checked   # …when you already ran tsgo on this exact commit
npx tsgo --noEmit        # TypeScript check (required after changes)
```

### ripul-native-app

See [Build & Deploy docs](ripul-native-app/docs/build-and-deploy.md) for full details including OTA/IPA deployment.

```bash
cd ripul-native-app
xcodegen generate           # Required after clone or project.yml changes

# iOS — build and install to device (requires USB or same Wi-Fi)
# Use -derivedDataPath build so both steps read/write the same pinned location.
# Without it, ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/RipulNativeApp-*/ may match
# stale dirs from old checkouts and you'll install a stale binary.
xcodebuild -scheme RipulApp \
  -destination 'platform=iOS,id=00008150-001C544E0EBA401C' \
  -derivedDataPath build \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=C7AA358R56 CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
  build
xcrun devicectl device install app \
  --device 00008150-001C544E0EBA401C \
  build/Build/Products/Debug-iphoneos/Ripul.app

# iOS — OTA deploy (when device is not on the network)
# ship-ota.sh uses -configuration Debug (same as device builds) and the shared
# ripul-native-app/build DerivedData — so .o files are reused across device
# builds, OTA archives, and the Alice variant. First run ~3-5 min, warm ~30 sec.
# NEVER write ad-hoc scripts — fresh /tmp/ paths + Release config = full cold build.
nohup bash ripul-native-app/scripts/ship-ota.sh > /tmp/ship-ota.log 2>&1 & disown
# Skip Alice: SKIP_ALICE=1 nohup bash ripul-native-app/scripts/ship-ota.sh ...
# Progress: tail -f /tmp/ship-ota.log

# iOS — TestFlight (the front door for testers who are NOT on the device list)
# Dev OTA embeds a UDID list, so a new tester costs a UDID + registration +
# rebuild. TestFlight costs an email. Use it for anyone outside your inner loop;
# keep ship-ota.sh for your own iteration. ~15-20 min. Full runbook:
# ripul-native-app/docs/testflight-deploy.md
nohup bash ripul-native-app/scripts/deploy-testflight.sh > /tmp/ripul-testflight.log 2>&1 & disown
# Archive + export without uploading anything to Apple: ... deploy-testflight.sh export
# This is the ONE sanctioned exception to the "no fresh /tmp + Release" rule
# above: App Store signing REQUIRES Release, and a Release archive shares no .o
# files with the Debug caches, so it must not be pointed at build/.

# macOS — NOTE the separate DerivedData (`build-mac`, not `build`).
# `build` is the SHARED iOS DerivedData (device builds, ship-ota.sh's SHARED_DD,
# the Alice variant). A fresh build into it recreates Build/Products, which
# DELETES the macOS Debug/Ripul.app sitting there — and because the Dock
# bookmarks that bundle by path, the Ripul icon turns into a question mark and
# the host won't launch (observed 2026-09-07). Keeping macOS in its own
# DerivedData makes it immune to any iOS build. Dock THIS path.
xcodebuild -scheme RipulMac -destination 'platform=macOS' -derivedDataPath build-mac \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=C7AA358R56 CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic build
open ripul-native-app/build-mac/Build/Products/Debug/Ripul.app
```

Agents: use the `host_bridge_*` tools (`bridge_status`, `bridge_install`, `bridge_ship`, `bridge_screenshot`, `bridge_debug`, …) — the Mac host wraps the command for you; people use **Devices** in the iPhone or Catalyst sidebar (one list of phones, with Live View of their apps and, under Whole Screen, the [device runner](ripul-native-app/device-runner/README.md) for everything else on the phone), and Settings → iPhones over Tailscale on the Mac to set up.
