Always use `ripul-native-app/build-catalyst` for Catalyst (`RipulApp`, destination `platform=macOS,variant=Mac Catalyst`). Build with `-derivedDataPath build-catalyst` from `ripul-native-app`, then launch and Dock `build-catalyst/Build/Products/Debug-maccatalyst/Ripul.app`. Never switch this path between rebuilds. Native macOS uses `build-mac`; iOS device/OTA uses `build`. The complete Catalyst signing command is in [build-and-deploy.md](ripul-native-app/docs/build-and-deploy.md#mac-catalyst).

### DerivedData: the sanctioned paths, and no others

These are the only sanctioned `-derivedDataPath` values. Use one of them. Never invent a new one.

| Path | Used for |
|---|---|
| `ripul-native-app/build` | iOS **device** + simulator-less archives, and `ship-ota.sh` (its `SHARED_DD`) |
| `ripul-native-app/build-variant-alice` | the Alice variant (`ship_ios.py` drives this; do not reuse it for anything else) |
| `ripul-native-app/build-iossim` | **iOS Simulator**, including iPhone Duo (`ship_duo_sim.py`) |
| `ripul-native-app/build-mac` | native macOS (`RipulMac`) |
| `ripul-native-app/build-mac-alice` | Ripul Host Alice, the second host for clean installs (`build_mac.py --variant alice`) |
| `ripul-native-app/build-catalyst` | Mac Catalyst (`RipulApp`, `variant=Mac Catalyst`) |

They are separate *on purpose*, for two different reasons.

**Products would delete each other.** An iOS build into `build` recreates `Build/Products`, which deletes a macOS or Catalyst `Ripul.app` sitting at the same path — that is what turns a Docked icon into a question mark.

**One Xcode: 27.1.** Every script builds with `/Applications/Xcode-27.1.app`, on both Macs, and no other Xcode should be installed beside it (Peter, 5 October 2026: "we need to be on 27.1 and that's it"). To try a newer one, use `ripul-native-app/scripts/try-xcode.sh`, and remove the old one when moving over. Before that date the two Macs held seven copies of four versions and scripts preferred different ones: the same commit was built with different toolchains on each Mac, and two toolchains sharing one DerivedData cost a full cold rebuild on every alternation. That is where the separate `build-iossim` came from. It stays: the scripts and their warm caches are built around these paths.

**Why this rule exists.** Sessions kept inventing a fresh path for one-off builds — `build-sim`, `build-simulator`, `build-iossim-artefacts` were three more names for the same simulator job — and nothing ever deleted them. By 2026-09-15 there were 16 such directories holding **26.4 GB**, and 18 `Ripul.app` bundles claiming the same two bundle ids. A throwaway path also costs you a *cold* build every time, since it shares no `.o` files with the warm caches. Those duplicates were deleted on 2026-09-25; `build-iossim` is the one simulator path that survives. Do not recreate the others.

If you genuinely need an isolated build, put it under `/tmp` so it cannot accumulate, and say so in your report.

### Which Ripul am I running?

Two different apps ship from this repo. They are separate applications, not two builds of one:

| App | Scheme | Bundle id | Display name | Icon |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mac host | `RipulMac` | `io.ripul.mac` | **Ripul Host** | teal |
| Catalyst | `RipulApp` | `io.ripul.app` | **Ripul** | navy |

Both produce a bundle named `Ripul.app` and both can sit in the Dock at once — hence the distinct display names and icons. Do not "fix" either back to a shared name or icon; that is the whole point of them.

To see what is actually running, by path:

```bash
pgrep -lf "Ripul.app/Contents/MacOS/Ripul"
```

Launch by **path**, never by bundle id. `open -b io.ripul.mac` can resolve to a stale copy — e.g. a months-old `/Applications/Ripul.app` — rather than the build you just made.

**One host per checkout, enforced.** A Debug Ripul Host that is not this checkout's `build-mac` product opens the canonical one and exits (`macOS/CanonicalHostGuard.swift`). Set `RIPUL_ALLOW_NONCANONICAL_HOST=1` to run a deliberate test copy. **And one running host per profile, enforced.** The host and its watchdog each hold a kernel lock in the profile's Application Support folder (`macOS/SingleInstanceLock.swift`, `SingleHostGuard.swift`); a second launch of the same profile brings the first forward and exits, and a second watchdog exits. Before 8 October 2026 two watchdogs could watch one host, and each reopened it when it exited. A host that keeps its own folder, installation id and login runs beside the real one: that is what a variant such as Alice is, so test a second instance with a variant. The one sanctioned second host is **Ripul Host Alice** (`io.ripul.mac.alice`): a different bundle id, so the guard leaves it alone. `python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/build_mac.py --variant alice --fresh` wipes it back to a first install and launches it beside the real host ([build-and-deploy.md](ripul-native-app/docs/build-and-deploy.md#a-second-host-for-clean-installs-ripul-host-alice)). Both run as `…/Ripul.app/Contents/MacOS/Ripul`, so stop hosts by full path, never `killall Ripul`. `build_mac.py` also unregisters every other `io.ripul.mac` copy from LaunchServices after each build. **One running Catalyst app per install, too.** A second copy of `io.ripul.app` (an installed one beside a developer build, or `open -n`) brings the first forward and closes within about three seconds (`iOS/SingleRunningCopy.swift`). Two copies share one installation id and fight over one relay seat; on 2026-10-07 that sent a phone 12-38 MB a minute. So to run a new build, quit the running one first. `RIPUL_ALLOW_SECOND_COPY=1` lets a deliberate second copy run.

Never copy the host into `/Applications` or keep backup `.app`s beside the product: on 2026-09-26 a March build in `/Applications` had been hosting for five days and answering the phone.

## Private Apple functions never ship in a store build

Ripul is going to the App Store. App Store review rejects private Apple functions, so a build that reaches **TestFlight or the App Store must contain none**. Development builds may: Live View's real touches are private, and are compiled into Debug builds only.

1. **Compile it out, don't switch it off.** Any line that reaches a private function (by `dlsym`, a selector or class name built from a string, an underscore key, an underscore override) goes inside `#if DEBUG || RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`. A runtime check leaves the name in the binary.
2. **Never set `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`, and never use a Debug configuration, for a build going to TestFlight or the App Store.** Never put either in a project file, xcconfig or scheme. `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD` belongs only on the command line of a direct install to your own device.
3. **Run the check; don't trust memory.**
   ```bash
   python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_private_apis.py source          # the code
   python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_private_apis.py all <app|ipa>   # the code and a built app
   ```
   `deploy-testflight.sh` runs it on the app it is about to upload and refuses when it fails. A developer-only name in the app, or a lookup nobody has reviewed, has no override.
4. **`RIPUL_ALLOW_KNOWN_PRIVATE_APIS=1` is for tester builds only**, while the known uses remain. **Never for a build submitted for App Store review.**
5. **Ripul Host (the Mac host) is distributed directly, not through the Mac App Store.** It uses private macOS functions to give windows keyboard focus.

Known uses still in every build on 29 September 2026: the in-app browser's mouse (`iOS/BrowserNativeMouse.swift`, the real risk), agent actuation of alerts and recognizers, the keyboard bar subclass, and a demangler lookup. The inventory, the ways out and the pre-submission checklist: [app-store-private-apis.md](ripul-native-app/docs/app-store-private-apis.md).

## Proving the build is live (do this FIRST — never unravel bundles)

When something looks broken on a client (Mac/iOS/web), **do not theorize about stale builds or pull apart chunks.** There is one immediate signal:

1. **Deployed version (server):** `curl -s https://demo.ripul.io/version.json` → `{ "version": "...", "builtAt": "..." }`. (`demo.ripul.io` is the canonical app host — all clients, including the native iOS/macOS shells, load it from there. Static file, served by Pages, not `/api`.) NOTE: `app.ripul.io` is **not the app** — since 8 October 2026 it is the public website (`website/`, a separate Cloudflare Worker), so it has no `version.json`, `/popup` or `/js/*`. Do not use it to check builds or assume the app is hosted there.
2. **Running version (client):** the app logs at boot, via `console.log`:
   - `[RIPUL] build=<version> origin=<host>`
   - `[RIPUL] LIVE ✓ running=<v> deployed=<v>` **or** `[RIPUL] STALE ✗ running=<v> deployed=<v>` (it self-checks against `/version.json`).

`LIVE ✓` (or running == deployed) → on the current build, **move on; not stale.** `STALE ✗` → force a reload/relaunch. (Wiping web data is NOT a staleness test — login persists via a native-injected session; trust the version signal.) `version.json` is written by `scripts/build.mjs` and matches `__BUILD_VERSION__` in the bundle.

`chrome-extension/public/version.json` is **gitignored, not tracked** — it is regenerated on every build, and `deploy:pages` rebuilds it immediately before upload, so the deployed file never comes from git. Never commit it, never `git add` it, and never treat its absence from `git status` (or its on-disk contents) as a problem.

## Workflow Rules

### Long-running commands — run them DETACHED from the session

**This applies to any command that runs longer than a single turn: iOS/macOS archives, OTA deploys, `deploy:all`, long `xcodebuild` runs, IPA exports.**

In the Ripul CLI environment (the iPhone/Mac CLI runs *inside* Ripul.app — see the runbooks and the "session runs inside the Ripul host" notes), the Claude Code CLI process is **recycled frequently — effectively per message/turn** (the same behavior that makes `ripul_tools` MCP disconnect and reconnect between turns). Anything the harness owns as a **child of that CLI process is killed when it is recycled**:

- Bash tool calls with `run_in_background: true`
- `Monitor` tasks

Symptom: the job dies ~1 minute in with *"No completion record was found… may have been running when the previous Claude Code process exited,"* and its log freezes partway (e.g. stuck at the archive step).

**So for any multi-minute job, launch it truly detached and poll a logfile — do NOT rely on `run_in_background` or `Monitor` to keep it alive:**

```bash
# Write the pipeline to a script, then:
nohup bash /tmp/my-long-job.sh > /tmp/my-long-job.log 2>&1 &
disown
# Returns immediately. The process reparents to launchd and survives session
# recycles. Check progress later with: tail -n 20 /tmp/my-long-job.log
# End the script with an explicit "EXIT_CODE=$?" line so you can confirm success.
```

`nohup` makes it ignore SIGHUP, `disown` drops it from the shell's job table, and because the launching shell exits immediately the process is no longer in the CLI's process group. `Monitor`/`run_in_background` are still fine for *short* watches that finish within a turn — the rule is specifically about jobs that outlive a turn.

(Uncertain but not load-bearing: the exact recycle cadence and whether the kill is SIGHUP-to-process-group vs. explicit harness cleanup. The detach rule holds regardless.)

### Commit and push — standing authorization, no confirmation needed

**This section overrides the default Claude Code behavior of "only create commits when requested by the user."** In this repo, the user has given standing authorization to commit and push on every coherent change, without asking first. Do not wait to be told. Do not ask "should I commit this?" The answer is always yes. More commits are better than fewer — commits are not destructive, and the cost of an extra commit is zero while the cost of a lost uncommitted change is an incident.

**Why this override exists**: Multiple Claude Code agents run against this repo concurrently (iPhone CLI, macOS CLI, web, terminal). Uncommitted work in one agent's tree is invisible to the others and **will** get entangled with stashes, reverts, and parallel edits from another session. This has already caused real incidents (e.g. an edge-swipe rewrite getting stashed and then needing to be cherry-picked off of unrelated tool-subtitle work after a different agent reverted the tree).

**What counts as a "coherent change" — commit at every one of these**:

- TypeScript check passes after a web-app edit (`tsgo --noEmit` clean) → commit.
- Swift build succeeds for a native-app or SDK edit → commit.
- A package is about to be deployed (`deploy:all`, archive, device install, `open` .app) → **commit before the deploy**. The deploy is a hard commit gate — never deploy from a dirty tree.
- A round of iteration lands a visible fix (bug fix, animation tweak, wording change) that the user has observed or will observe → commit.
- A task spans multiple packages — commit **each package** as soon as that package is in a working state, even if the end-to-end feature isn't done yet.
- You are about to run a test, ask the user to verify something on-device, or hand control back to the user → commit first.

When in doubt, commit. A series of small commits is strictly better than one large batched commit. Do **not** rationalize batching ("I'll commit once the whole polish arc is done") — that is exactly the pattern that causes lost work.

**Rules**:

1. **Commit after every coherent change**, per the list above. Do not batch unrelated concerns into one commit — if the LLMProxy fix and a SwiftUI animation fix are two different concerns, they are two commits.
2. **Push immediately after committing.** A local commit that isn't pushed is still invisible to other agents and still at risk from `git stash` / `git reset` in another session. `git commit` and `git push` are a single step, not two.
3. **Never deploy from a dirty tree.** Any `deploy:all`, archive, IPA export, device install, or `open` .app is a hard commit gate. Commit and push first, then deploy. If the tree is dirty with foreign files you didn't create, stop and see rule 4.
4. **Announce and stop on a foreign dirty tree at session start.** The first thing you do in any session that touches git-tracked files is run `git status`. If there are uncommitted changes you did not create, your **first response to the user** must announce them and ask what to do. Do not silently work around them. Do not stash them. Do not revert them. Those changes belong to another agent and only the user knows whether they're safe to touch.
5. **Never use `git stash` as a workflow tool.** Stashes are invisible to other agents and easy to lose. If you need to set work aside, commit it to a branch instead.
6. **If a task spans web + native + SDK**, commit and push each package's changes as soon as that package is in a working state — don't wait until everything builds end-to-end. Partial progress on `main` is strictly better than a pile of uncommitted cross-package edits that another agent might revert.
7. **Before doing anything destructive** (`git checkout HEAD --`, `git reset`, `git stash drop`, force push), re-read `git status` and `git stash list` and confirm with the user. Destructive operations in a multi-agent environment can wipe out another session's in-progress work.

**What "standing authorization" does NOT cover**: destructive operations (rule 7), force pushes, amending published commits, and committing files that look like secrets — these still require an explicit user confirmation every time. Standing authorization is for the happy path: edit → verify → commit → push.

### Session transcripts are captured automatically — commit however you like

Every commit a Claude session makes inside the Ripul host leaves that session's transcript on the repo's `claude-sessions` branch, so the chat can be picked up on another Mac if this one is lost. Plain `git commit` in the shell counts; no special tool is needed, and there is nothing for an agent to do.

- **How:** the host gives the CLI processes it launches its own git hooks directory, through `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment variables. Nothing is written to any repo. Each hook runs the repo's own hook of the same name first; `post-commit` then flags the commit. The host uploads the transcript a few seconds after the commit and again when the turn ends.
- **`git config core.hooksPath` showing `~/.ripul/session-capture/hooks` inside a session is this, not a fault.** Do not unset it or "repair" it.
- **Checking it:** `GET /host/diagnostics` on the host's port lists the last captures under `sessionCapture`, failures included.
- **Switch:** Settings → Coding Agents → Claude → Save Transcripts With Commits (on by default; also changeable from a paired phone).
- **Not covered:** Codex and Antigravity chats, and sessions started outside the host (a plain terminal).
- **Where it shows up:** the iPhone and Catalyst **Repos** screen. Each repo has two views of the same commits: **History** (`iOS/RepoGraphView.swift`) is git's own order, with a marker in the chat's colour on each commit a captured chat made, and **Chats** (`iOS/RepoChatsView.swift`) lists the chats, each row opening to all the commits that chat made. History never regroups by chat: on a branch several agents share, chats take turns, and grouping by adjacency split one chat into a block plus strays. There is no separate Sessions/Commits screen on iPhone any more.
- **Rescue:** a chat's detail has "Continue on <Mac>". That Mac fetches the branch and imports the newest transcript as a new chat of its own (`agent:gitRescueSession` → `importTranscriptOnHost.ts`, the same import a Move uses). The chat's original Mac is not contacted and keeps its copy. It is explicit and user-triggered, like Move; nothing re-homes a chat by itself.

Code: `ripul-native-app/macOS/SessionCapture.swift` (hook, queue, timing), `SessionCaptureRunner.swift`, `session-capture.mjs`. Tests: `bash ripul-native-app/Tests/SessionCapture/run.sh`.

### Git worktrees — branch isolation for features

Multiple agents often work on this repo concurrently. When an agent is working on a distinct feature (not a quick fix), it should use a **git worktree** to avoid interleaving commits with other agents on `main`.

**At the start of a session**, if the user describes a feature or multi-step task, ask:

> "Should I create a worktree for this? I'll work on a feature branch in an isolated directory so it doesn't interfere with other sessions on main."

If the user says yes, call the `EnterWorktree` tool with a descriptive name:
```
EnterWorktree({ name: "share-links" })
```

This creates a worktree directory with its own checkout on a new branch and **switches the session's working directory** to it. All subsequent file edits and git operations happen in that directory. Other agents on `main` are completely unaffected.

**Rules**:
1. **One worktree per feature** — don't create multiple worktrees in the same session.
2. **Commit and push normally** — session capture follows the commit, not the directory, so it works in a worktree too.
3. **Don't merge back yourself** — when the feature is done, tell the user it's ready for a PR from the feature branch. Don't merge into main without being asked.
4. **Quick fixes stay on main** — if the task is a one-commit bug fix or tweak, a worktree is overkill. Use your judgment.

### What to Deploy After Changes

The web app loads live from Cloudflare; the native app loads it in a WKWebView. Changes to different packages require different deploy steps to be testable:

| What changed | Deploy steps | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Web app only** (chrome-extension) | `deploy:all` | Web app is served from Cloudflare — all clients (browser, iOS, macOS) load it remotely |
| **iOS app only** (ripul-native-app, iOS scheme) | Rebuild `RipulApp` scheme and install to iPhone | Native shell runs on-device — web app is unchanged |
| **macOS app only** (ripul-native-app, Mac scheme) | Rebuild `RipulMac` scheme and `open` the .app | Native shell runs locally — web app is unchanged |
| **iOS SDK only** (ripul-ios-sdk) | Rebuild and install **both** native apps (iOS + macOS) | Both apps consume the SDK via SPM — SDK changes only take effect after rebuilding |
| **Web app + iOS app** | `deploy:all` first, then rebuild and install iOS app | Web app must be live before the native app loads it |
| **Web app + macOS app** | `deploy:all` first, then rebuild and launch macOS app | Same — web app must be live first |
| **Web app + iOS SDK** | `deploy:all`, then rebuild and install both native apps | Both sides need updating |
| **All three** | `deploy:all`, then rebuild and install both native apps | SDK is compiled into native apps, web app is loaded at runtime |

**Key insights**:
- Web-only changes (UI, chat, tools, worker) never require a native app rebuild — just `deploy:all`. All clients pick up the new web app automatically.
- A native rebuild is only needed when Swift code changes (native app or SDK).
- iOS and macOS are separate build schemes (`RipulApp` / `RipulMac`) — rebuild whichever platform you're testing on, or both if the change is in shared code or the SDK.

## Technical Guidelines

### Styling (Web App)
- Use MUI theme tokens (`'text.primary'`, `'action.hover'`, `'divider'`) instead of hardcoded rgba values
- Never pass string tokens to `alpha()` — resolve via `theme.palette.X.main` first
- Use `useThemeColors()` hook for common color calculations
- **Colours and typefaces come from the theme, never from a literal.** No hex or `rgba(` colour and no `fontFamily` string at a call site. Read a palette token, `alpha()` of a palette value, a named colour (`useNamedColours()`, for a colour with a job that equals no palette value) or a family (`useFontFamilies()`: `text`, `display`, `code`). A colour that is data (syntax, terminal, a provider's or a model's) is marked `// theme-exempt: <reason>`. Before pushing, run `node scripts/check-theme-literals.mjs --strict <paths>` in `chrome-extension`. Every build runs the check: `src/logging/components/chat/` and `src/logging/panels/` are finished, so a literal there fails the build, and elsewhere it warns until that directory's stream finishes.
- See `chrome-extension/docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md`

### UI Element Traceability (Web App)
- Add `data-ui` attribute to every rendered element in React components
- Format: `ComponentName.section.element` — static values only, no runtime data
- **MUI compound components** (`TextField`, `Autocomplete`, `Slider`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, etc.) render multiple DOM layers — `data-ui` on the component prop lands on the outer wrapper `div`, not the interactive `<input>`. For any MUI component wrapping a focusable element, also pass `data-ui` through `slotProps`:
  ```tsx
  // ❌ data-ui only reaches the wrapper div
  <TextField data-ui="Foo.bar" />

  // ✅ data-ui also reaches the <input>
  <TextField
    data-ui="Foo.bar"
    slotProps={{ htmlInput: { 'data-ui': 'Foo.bar' } }}
  />
  ```

### API Client & Authentication (Web App)
- All authenticated API calls must flow through `useLlmProxyClient()` / `useLlmProxyService()` hooks
- Never create `ApiClient` instances with `ClerkAuthProvider` outside approved hooks
- See the chrome-extension CLAUDE.md for full details

### Native (iOS/macOS)
- **XcodeGen required**: The `.xcodeproj` is generated and gitignored — `project.yml` is the source of truth. Run `xcodegen generate` after cloning and after any changes to `project.yml` or source file additions/removals. Never edit the `.xcodeproj` directly.
- Prefer `.glassEffect(.clear)` over `.regular` for iOS 26+ glass effects
- Use `.ultraThinMaterial` fallback for pre-iOS 26
- **Native-first for block ports**: when porting a web block/UI to native, use the platform's native control wherever one exists (sidebar → `List(.sidebar)`, date → `DatePicker`/`UICalendarView`, menu → `Menu`/`Picker`, modal → sheet w/ detents). Mirror semantics exactly; rebuild presentation natively; drop web-only presentation knobs. Re-skinning the web look in SwiftUI is a defect. See the [CmsRender doctrine](ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/CmsRender/README.md) (Rule 0) and the iOS styling guide's "Native-first" section.
- **Present sheets with `.ripulSheet(isPresented:)` / `.ripulSheet(item:)`, never a bare `.sheet`.** Mac Catalyst ignores detents, so a bare sheet gets UIKit's fixed phone-sized box whatever the window size. The wrappers (`ripul-ios-sdk`, `SheetPresentation.swift`) size the sheet for the window by default; pass `size: .form` for a genuinely short form. The app build runs `scripts/check_sheet_sizing.py` and fails on a bare one.
- **Fonts and colours come from the theme accessors, never from a literal.** Write `.font(.ripul(.caption))`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))`, `Color.ripul(.danger)`, `UIColor.ripul(.canvas)`, and `Color.ripul(system: .secondarySystemBackground)` where no role fits; `.tint` and `Color.accentColor` stay as they are. Each default is the system value it replaces, so nothing changes on screen until a theme names the token. A style is replaced by the style form and a `Color` by the Color form: the two draw different pixels in a list row. A colour that is data (a provider's, a model's, a chat's) is marked `// theme-exempt: <reason>`. The contract, the table that gives the one token for each literal, and the limits are in [theming.md](ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md). Before pushing, run `python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_theme_tokens.py --paths <file or directory>...` and `python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py --lint`. The app build runs the check: `ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/Sessions/` is finished, so a direct font or colour there fails the build, and elsewhere it warns until that stream finishes.
- See `ripul-native-app/docs/ios-styling-guide.md`

You have a persistent file-based memory at `/Users/petermaude/.claude/projects/-Users-petermaude-Documents-ripul/memory/`. name: <short-kebab-case-slug>
description: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your one lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

entries.name: mcp__ripul_tools__ripul_guide
entries.description:
How to use Ripul, the harness this conversation runs in, one topic at a time. Read the relevant guide BEFORE the work it covers: Ripul has its own way of doing several things an agent would otherwise do with a built-in feature.

Call with no arguments for the current list of guides and when to read each. Call with `topic` to read one. Topics include:
- `session`: what ends your process, long-running jobs, what a commit does, asking the user, spoken messages. Read once at the start of work.
- `artefacts`: the user asks for an artefact or anything interactive. Make it a Ripul artefact, not an artifact or canvas of your own.
- `trains`: before you build, deploy, install to a phone or simulator, or test against something another agent may be using.
- `devices`: putting a build on an iPhone, or looking at, tapping through or recording an app on a phone, tablet or simulator.
- `browser`: a page your own fetch cannot read, or one that needs the user's sign-in; before any browser_ tool.
- `plans`: the user asks for a plan or design document, or for a review of one. Write a Ripul plan, not a plan in your own plan mode.
- `voice-and-media`: a message wrapped in <voice>, or an image, video, recording or files to show in the chat.
- `cms`: building or changing a site, portal or dashboard in the Ripul CMS.
- `sdk`: the repository is an iOS app that uses, or should use, the RipulAgent package.

topic.description: The id of the guide to read, for example `artefacts`. Leave out to list the guides.

content.content:
1	# What the SDK's theme system costs a host app
2	
3	A trial on Sandsend Retreats (branch `theme-trial`, commit `d19626c`), by an agent acting as the host's developer, using only the public package at v0.7.170, the `ripul_guide` tool and the app's own repository. 11 October 2026, 08:46 to 09:07. The SDK's home repository was not read at any point.
4	
5	## The answer
6	
7	- **20 minutes** from the first read to the build running on Peter's iPhone (measured, from the clock). About 10 were the agent working, 8 waiting for builds and screenshots, 2 measuring baselines. These are an agent's minutes: a person would take most of a day, because the work is reading 2,800 lines and editing 12 files.
8	- **706 lines added, 90 removed, in 27 files** (measured, `git diff main --shortstat`). The app was 1,633 lines of Swift. Only 78 of those lines are what `theming.md` promises a host writes (a token where a system value was).
9	- **202 of the lines are a script the SDK documents and does not ship**, and without it the View Explorer names no tokens.
10	- **Nine things the package did not tell me**, listed under "What did not work". Four were found by reading the SDK's source, three by a build or a screenshot going wrong, two are SDK faults that have no cure in the host.
11	- Release build: 2 seconds faster, 79 KB more code, 1.7 MB more app, nearly all of it fonts (all measured).
12	
13	## The ledger
14	
15	Clock times are from `date`, noted at each step. Lines are from `git diff main --numstat` unless marked "counted by hand", which means counted in the diff.
16	
17	| # | Clock | What and why | Lines, files | Learned from | Should the host do it? |
18	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| 1 | 08:46 to 08:50 | Read `theming.md` (985 lines), the seven files of `ThemeCore/` (1,776 lines), parts of `RipulBaseTokenProvider.swift`. Fetched the website's and install page's styles. | none | theming.md, the source | Reading, yes. Reading the source, no: see 5, 7, 9, 12. |
20	| 2 | 08:48 to 08:50 | Fonts. The website's are IvyPresto Display and Freight Sans Pro (Adobe Fonts, not allowed in an app). Chose Playfair Display and Source Sans 3, downloaded them with their licences, wrote where they came from. | 4 font files (1,592 KB), 2 licences (186 lines), `SOURCES.md` (14) | the website's CSS; a human decision | Yes. Choosing and licensing a font is the host's. |

156	### What a host still pays, and four proposals
157	
158	These were left out because each is a design decision. For each: the proposal I would make, its cost in my own working time (an agent's, reasoned from the size of the code, not measured), and its risk.
159	
160	**1. A theme layer a host can link without the rest (item 10).**
161	Proposal: a `RipulTheme` library product in `Package.swift`, with no dependencies, holding `ThemeCore/`; `RipulAgent` re-exports it, so nothing a host or WAC writes today changes.
162	Cost: about half a day. Eight files move; the usage-map reader and the root have a few reaches into the rest of the SDK to cut (the legacy refresh environment key, the token provider stays behind).
163	Risk: Xcode links a package product into every configuration, so Sandsend gets the saving only if nothing in its Release build imports `RipulAgent`; today its console is already Debug-only, so it would. The Release app would lose about 60 MB (reasoned from the first trial's measurement, not built). A module rename can break a host that spells a type `RipulAgent.RipulTheme`; none of ours does.
164	
165	**2. A host's own colours in the document (item 9).**
166	Proposal: a host declares its roles once in code, each with the colour it is today (`static let navy = RipulHostRole("navy", default: …)`), reads them with the same accessors (`.ripul(.navy)`), and names them in the same document under `roles`. The default is today's value, so the rule that nothing changes holds. The check, the lint and the usage map learn the declared names.
167	Cost: about a day, most of it the three tools and the tests.
168	Risk: two role types behind one accessor name can make `.ripul(.x)` ambiguous to the compiler where a host picks a name the SDK also uses; the alternative, turning the fixed enum into an open type, is cleaner to read and touches every `switch` over roles in the SDK. This is also the first step of moving WAC off the legacy engine, so its shape should be chosen with that in mind.
169	
170	**3. Text that has no colour of its own (item 7).**
171	Proposal: do not look for a root-level cure; it was measured not to exist. Make it mechanical instead: `migrate` adds `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))` to every `Text` with no foreground in its chain, and `check` counts a bare `Text` so a new one fails the build.
172	Cost: about half a day, plus a measurement pass in each container (a button, a link, a list row, a toolbar) to prove the added line is an identity there.
173	Risk: the tool reads text, not types, so a `Text` built in a helper is missed, and inside a control an explicit text role is drawn as the control's tint, which is right today and may surprise under a theme. It is still a line a text; it stops being a line a person writes.
174	
175	**4. Lists (item 8).**
176	Proposal: first spend two hours measuring whether a root can do it at all: `scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` set at the root reaches the lists below it, but a row's background set from outside a list does not (the first trial found that). If the root can carry the ground and UIKit's appearance can carry the rows, lists are themed with no edit. If not, one modifier, `.ripulThemedList()`, that `migrate` adds to each `List` and `Form`, with the rows' background applied by the SDK's `Section(themed:)`.
177	Cost: two hours to know, then half a day either way.
178	Risk: the system's grouped look has parts no public setting reaches on iOS 26 and later (the inset card's shape and its selected state); a themed row background may lose the system's highlight. Under the default document it must stay the system's own, which a modifier that does nothing until a theme names `surface` guarantees.
179	
180	Also still the host's, with no proposal here: a font feature in the document (lining figures), the colour of a large navigation title and of a section header, and a way to keep a serif without a second document.

237	### What was checked
238	
239	- Default document: 36 screenshots (18 screens, light and dark). 34 the same pixel for pixel as the untouched app on the same SDK; the other two are the photo gallery, whose glass close button differs by one to two thousand pixels between two captures of the same build (measured).
240	- Brand: 36 screenshots taken, 8 opened.
241	- The switch while running: as step 13. Both tab bar faults of the first run are gone (measured).
242	- `check` zero; `lint` one complaint, which is wrong (below).
243	- On the phone: installed and running, launched on the brand, which is kept. A screenshot of the phone a minute later showed Peter in another app, so I did not relaunch over him: **the brand on the phone's own screen is not seen by me.**
244	
245	### What did not work this time
246	
247	1. **`migrate` adds no `import RipulAgent`, and the page does not say a file needs one.** Nine files were rewritten to call `.ripul(…)` with nothing imported. I knew a cure (`@_exported import`, one line) only from the first run. A fresh host gets nine compile errors and adds nine lines.
248	2. **`lint` fails on the page's own first step.** With the root line added as step 1 says, `lint` exits 1: "the hunk adds and removes different numbers of lines", on `.ripulThemeRoot(theme: "standard")`. It also counts 51 replacements where `migrate` reported 55.
249	3. **`migrate` does not follow a host's font helper.** It follows an identifier wrapper; it does not follow `static func serif(_:weight:) -> Font`, which this app uses at 10 headings. `check` lists each. They are mechanical: the helper's body says which family.
250	4. **`--named` leaves `.black.opacity(…)`.** The page says `--named` writes the system form for black. Inside a gradient's colour list and a shadow it does not (6 lines), and `check` then fails on them.
251	5. **`-ripul.theme.document` lasts for one launch.** The page calls the key "the choice", which reads as kept. A launch argument overrides a default for that launch and is not stored. 252	6. **A host's agent cannot see what the explorer says.** `usage-map --explain` shows the map, not the answer. The answer is behind a tap in a console that needs a person signed in. I called `RipulTokenInspector.readout` from temporary code, as the first run did.
253	7. **A control named from a variable is not in the map:** `.identified(name + ".call")`, 8 of this app's 24 named places. The explorer says so plainly when asked; the page does not.
254	8. **The build line reads "768 identifiers … following .cmsInspectorID, .identified(".** 16 of the 768 are this app's; the rest and the first wrapper are the SDK's own screens. A host reading its build log cannot tell what was found in its own code.

263	
264	1. **A text colour, a line a text: 30 lines.** Unchanged from the first run, and it is the only cost that grows with every screen. The page is honest about it. Nothing warns when a new `Text` lacks it: `check` reads zero either way.

266	3. **A second document to keep a serif: 7 lines,** and with it the plain system look is no longer the app's look, so the picker must hide it (`systemTitle: nil`).
267	4. **The brand's own two colours by hand: 3 lines** of `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent) ? mine : theirs`.
268	5. **A label taken apart (5 lines) and a row's dimming moved to its texts (5 lines),** both only because a text colour cannot sit on a container.
269	6. **A lever to keep a theme (5 lines).**
270	7. **One import line** that the migration should have written.
271	8. **The whole package in Release.** 76,760 KB for the Release simulator app (measured), to read two JSON files.

273	
274	With 1, 2, 5 and 7 done by the SDK or its tool, this run's hand-written code would have been about 45 lines: a document, a root line, a picker, the build step and the two colours.

276	### Not measured
277	
278	- The brand on the phone's own screen, and the picker in the More menu, which no screenshot of mine shows: it needs a tap.
279	- The 28 brand screenshots I did not open.
280	- The View Explorer as a person sees it.
281	- What a fresh host's time would be: see "This run was not blind".
282	- An archive, TestFlight, Dynamic Type, Increased Contrast, VoiceOver, right-to-left.
283	- A person's time. Every minute here is an agent's.
284	
285	## Third trial: no change to the host's source
286	
287	Sandsend Retreats' `main` in a throwaway copy (`/tmp/sandsend-zero`, removed), against the SDK in this repository at commit `b09493db9` (not released). 11 October 2026. Xcode 27.1 (27A9269), Swift 6.4, XcodeGen 2.45.3, iPhone 18 Pro simulator on iOS 27.0. Every figure is marked measured or reasoned.
288	
289	Peter's question: "Is there any way to do this without us changing the host's source code?"
290	
291	- **Yes, it works.** Sandsend builds and runs themed with not one line of Swift added or changed (measured: `git status` shows `project.yml` and new files only). Under the system look all 36 screenshots match the untouched app: 34 pixel for pixel, and the 2 of the photo gallery differ only where two captures of one build differ.
292	- **What the host does: 3 lines of project settings and 8 new files.** The plug-in on the app target (3 lines of `project.yml`), one theme document (28 lines), four font files, two licences and a note. No root line, no Info.plist key, no build phase, no script. The pin line changes as for any SDK release.
293	- **What would stop me recommending it as the only route:** it rests on how the Swift compiler chooses between two declarations of one name, which the language does not promise; and it reaches less than the migration does, on this app most visibly the two lists, which stay the system's black and grey in dark beside navy pages.
294	
295	My recommendation: make this the way a host starts, and keep `migrate` for a host that wants the rest.
296	
297	### What was built
298	
299	All in the SDK, opt-in. A host that does not switch the plug-in on gets none of it.
300	
301	- **A build-tool plug-in, `RipulThemeRedirect`** (`Package.swift`, `Plugins/RipulThemeRedirect/plugin.swift`). On every build it runs `tools/ripul-theme redirect`, which writes one Swift file into the build folder; Xcode compiles that file into the host's own module.
302	- **The generated file** (`tools/redirect/RipulThemeRedirect.swift.txt`, 140 lines) declares SwiftUI's names again: the 11 text styles, `Font.system(size:weight:design:)` and `Font.system(_:design:weight:)`, `Font.weight`, `bold` and `italic`, `Image.font`, `Color.red` and four more hues, `Color.primary` and `.secondary`, `Color(UIColor)`, `foregroundStyle` for the hierarchy styles on `View` and `Text`, and `WindowGroup`. Each is one call into the SDK.
303	- **`ThemeCore/RipulThemeRedirect.swift`** (203 lines) is where each call lands and where everything is decided. With no theme each returns the call site's own value, itself (7 tests).
304	- **The root with no line written.** The generated `WindowGroup` wraps the host's content in the theme root and installs the theme: the one Info.plist names, or the bundle's only theme document when it names none.
305	- **A serif with no second document.** `design: .serif` becomes the display family once a theme names one and is the system's serif until then. Both earlier trials needed a 7-line "standard" document for this.
306	- **The View Explorer's map with no build phase.** The generator reads the unedited source as the migration would have left it and puts the map in the generated file, inside `#if DEBUG`.
307	- **A name the host already declares is left out** of the generated file, so the host's own is used.
308	
309	### What the host did, counted
310	
311	All measured from `git status` and `git diff` in the copy.
312	
313	| | Count |
314	|---|---|
315	| Swift lines added or changed | 0 |
316	| `project.yml` | 3 lines added for the plug-in. (2 more lines replaced the pin with a path to the unreleased SDK; a released SDK is the usual 1-line pin change.) |
317	| Theme document | 1 file, 28 lines, copied from `theme-trial-2` |
318	| Fonts | 4 files, 1.6 MB, and 2 licences and a note (199 lines), copied from `theme-trial-2` |
319	| Info.plist, build phases, scripts, root line, import lines | 0 |
320	| Build time | Debug simulator 19 to 22 s incremental, 4 to 5 s with nothing changed; Release clean 210 s (the second trial: 207 s) |
321	| Release app | 76,724 KB (the second trial: 76,760 KB), no usage map in the binary |
322	
323	Against the earlier trials: 706 lines added in 27 files, then 411 in 23, now 230 in 9 files (8 of them new), of which 199 are licences and the fonts' note, 28 the theme document and 3 the settings.
324	
325	### Under the system look: nothing moved
326	
327	Measured. 18 screens, light and dark, the zero-edit build launched with `-ripul.theme.document system` against the untouched app on the same SDK.
328	
329	- 34 of 36 the same pixel for pixel.
330	- The 2 that differ are the photo gallery: 1,263 and 1,478 pixels, in rows 2249 to 2388. Two captures of the zero-edit build itself differ by 756 and 1,468 pixels in the same rows. That is the glass button the second trial reported.
331	- The baseline was captured once in full, not twice: the Mac's load average was 86 and a pass took half an hour.
332	
333	### On the brand: what took the theme, by kind
334	
335	Counts of call sites are measured from the source. "Seen" means in a screenshot I opened: 10 of the 36 brand screenshots, and 2 more taken with a document that changes sizes.
336	
337	| Kind | Sites in Sandsend | Took the theme? |
338	|---|---|---|
339	| Text with a text style (`.font(.headline)`, `.font(.footnote.weight(.semibold))`) | 23 on text and labels | Yes, all (measured: each resolves to the generated declaration; seen in Source Sans 3) |
340	| Text with a fixed size | 1, the wordmark, a serif | Yes, in the display face (seen) |
341	| Text with no font | most of the app's 54 `Text`s | Yes, through the root's default font (seen) |
342	| The app's own helper, `Font.serif(_:weight:)` | 10 | Yes, in Playfair Display (seen). The helper calls `.system(_:design:weight:)`, which is redirected inside it. The migration left these 10 for a person. |
343	| Symbols: a font on an `Image` | 3 | Correctly not resized. With a document setting title to 48 pt and footnote to 24 pt, the paw (`.font(.title)`) and the chevrons (`.font(.footnote.weight(.semibold))`) kept their size while the text beside them grew (seen for 2 of the 3). |
344	| Symbols: the icon of a `Label` | 9 | They follow the label's font size, as they did before and as they do after a migration (seen for 2) |
345	| Named colours that are a role (red, orange, green, blue, gray) | 0 | Nothing to measure in this app. Compiled and resolved in a scratch file, not seen drawn. |
346	| White, black, clear | 12 | Never themed, by either route |
347	| Hierarchy styles in `foregroundStyle` | 9 (8 secondary, 1 tertiary) | Yes (seen: the brand's dim grey) |
348	| Wrapped system colours, `Color(.systemGroupedBackground)` | 10 | Yes: the paper ground and the cards, light and dark (seen) |
349	| Text with no colour of its own | about 30 (the second trial's count) | No. It stays the system's black or white, not the brand's ink. |
350	| Lists | 2 lists, 3 sections | No. Ground, rows and header colour stay the system's; the header takes the family. In dark the two list screens are black and grey beside navy pages (seen). |
351	| Navigation titles | 3 | The family, not the colour; the same as the migration (seen) |
352	| Tab bar | 1 | Labels in the family at launch, the selected tab in the accent (seen) |
353	| Prominent buttons | 5 | Not touched, on purpose. They carry `.tint(Brand.navy)`, and the brand's dark `onAccent` on that fixed navy would not be readable. They stay navy with white labels (seen). |
354	| The app's own two colours, `Brand.navy` and `Brand.cream` | 13 | No. They are asset colours; no route but a line of code reaches them. |
355	| `.foregroundStyle(.tint)` | 4 | Yes, through the window's tint (seen) |
356	
357	**The View Explorer names tokens for unedited source** (measured, by asking the running app through the debugger, since nobody is signed in to its console). For `stay.cottage` on the brand: "Font | headline | Source Sans 3 17 pt semibold | family from the theme document", "Foreground | ripul.textSecondary | #6A6F80 light, #A4ABC0 dark | theme document", "Background | ripul.surface | #FFFFFF light, #151F3D dark | theme document", and "symbol size | never themed" for the chevron. 16 identifiers are in the map. A font that goes through the app's own helper is reported as "not a theme token" though it is themed: the map reads text and does not follow the helper.
358	
359	### What broke, and the edges
360	
361	Each of these was measured in the real app's build, in scratch files that were removed before the measured build.
362	
363	| Edge | Result |
364	|---|---|
365	| Does Xcode compile a plug-in's generated Swift into an app target, and does XcodeGen express it? | Yes to both. `buildToolPlugins` in `project.yml`; the file lands in `build/Build/Intermediates.noindex/BuildToolPluginIntermediates/`. |
366	| What the host must allow | With the SDK as a local path, nothing: the build ran without `-skipPackagePluginValidation`. For a released package Xcode asks "Trust & Enable" once and `xcodebuild` needs that flag. **Not measured**, because the SDK was not released. It means Sandsend's ship script and the commands in its CLAUDE.md would each gain that flag. |
367	| The plug-in's sandbox | `/usr/bin/python3` runs inside it and reads the host's sources. |
368	| `.font(.body)`, `Font.body`, `SwiftUI.Font.body`, in an array, in a ternary, in generic code | All call the generated declaration (read from the object file's symbols). Even the name qualified with `SwiftUI.` is redirected, so a host has no spelling that means "the system's". |
369	| A redeclared generic method | **Did not work as the probes suggested.** `foregroundStyle<S: ShapeStyle>` and `Image.font(_: Font?)` made every use ambiguous and the app did not compile: SwiftUI's return an opaque type, so the two signatures are never the same. They are now declared as closer matches instead (`foregroundStyle(_: HierarchicalShapeStyle)`, `Image.font(_: Font)`). So the design leans on two compiler behaviours, not one. |
370	| A hierarchy style given to `fill`, `stroke` or `background` | Not redirected. Only `foregroundStyle` is. |
371	| A host with its own `extension Font { static var caption }` or `Color.red` | A compile error, "invalid redeclaration", naming the generated file, until the generator learned to leave such names out. Now it builds and the host's own is used. The generator reads text; a declaration it cannot see is still that error. |
372	| A host type named `WindowGroup`, `WindowGroup(for:)`, a UIKit app delegate | The first is left out by the generator (tested in the tool's tests, not in the app). The other two are not covered: the host adds a flag and writes the root line. |
373	| A second module | A framework target with the plug-in switched on built and was redirected, in Swift 6 language mode. A target without the plug-in is untouched. |
374	| Previews | A `#Preview` compiled. Not run in Xcode's canvas. |
375	| Release and Debug | Both build. The usage map is in Debug only. |
376	| Incremental builds | A host file that gains a clashing name is picked up on the next build (5 s); the generated file changes and the app recompiles. |
377	| Two theme documents and no name | The system look, and a line in the log saying to add the Info.plist key (met by accident, when I added a second document for the symbol test). |
378	| A value equal but not identical | The SDK's new test caught one: `design: .default` was returned as `design: nil`. Fixed before the pixel comparison. |
379	
380	**Is the rule promised?** No. That a module's own declaration is preferred to an imported one with the same name and type is how the compiler's name lookup behaves, and I know of nothing in The Swift Programming Language or an accepted proposal that states it. The closer-match rule (a non-generic or non-optional parameter is preferred) is ordinary overload ranking and is equally unwritten. Tested with Swift 6.4 only, in Swift 5 and Swift 6 language modes. If a release changed either, the likely failure is loud (an ambiguity error in the host's files) and the cure is to switch the plug-in off; the less likely one is silent, the host going back to the system look.
381	
382	Mine, not the design's: a first screenshot pass was blank because captures were taken before a slow launch finished; and two build logs were lost to a filter that closed the pipe.
383	
384	### The two routes compared
385	
386	| | The plug-in (this trial) | `migrate` (the second trial) |
387	|---|---|---|
388	| The host's Swift | 0 lines | about 140 changed or added: 72 at call sites by the tool and one expression, 70 by decision |
389	| Reaches: text styles, fixed sizes, hierarchy styles, wrapped system colours, named hues | Yes | Yes |
390	| Reaches: the app's own serif helper | Yes, with no edit | By hand, 10 sites |
391	| Keeps a serif with no second document | Yes | No, 7 lines |
392	| Symbols keep their size | Yes, at run time | Yes, in the source (`ripulIcon`) |
393	| Text with no colour | No | 30 lines by hand |
394	| Lists, section headers, empty states | No | 22 lines and the themed forms |
395	| Prominent buttons' labels | No | Yes |
396	| The host's own colours | No | 3 lines by hand |
397	| View Explorer | Yes, no setup | Yes, one build phase |
398	| What the source says | `.font(.body)`: nothing shows that it is themed | `.font(.ripul(.body))`: it says so |
399	| Stays themed as the app grows | By itself, for what it reaches | Only with `check` in the build |
400	| Rests on | Unwritten compiler behaviour; a name clash is a compile error | Public API only |
401	| To undo | Remove 3 lines | Revert the edits |
402	| Fails how | Loudly at compile time, or (a compiler change) silently unthemed | A missed site is silently the system's |
403	
404	They mix: a migrated file calls the accessors directly and the rest goes through the generated file. So the plug-in can be the start and the migration the finish, a file at a time.
405	
406	### On the phone: not installed
407	
408	**The build is made and signed (`/tmp/sz-device.app`, measured) and is not on Peter's iPhone.** From 10:40 until I stopped, CoreDevice listed the phone as unavailable and the bridge reported it "waiting_for_listener", not reachable; I checked five times, the last at the end. The install page route was not used: it ships committed work from Sandsend's own repository, which this trial was not to touch. When the phone is reachable: `xcrun devicectl device install app --device 00008150-001C544E0EBA401C /tmp/sz-device.app`, then launch `io.ripul.sandsendretreats`. It opens on the brand with no argument, because the brand is the bundle's only theme document. `/tmp` does not survive a restart of the Mac.
409	
410	### What was checked in the SDK
411	
412	All measured: 56 theme tests pass (5 new on macOS; 2 more are iOS-only and were compiled, not run); 7 tests of the tools pass (3 new); the SDK builds for macOS and for the iOS simulator with the `--triple` form; `check_theme_tokens.py` on Ripul's own sources reads zero; the private-function check is clean; Ripul's app compiles for the simulator (`BUILD SUCCEEDED`; the log also carried "Could not archive SSU artifacts", which I did not look into).
413	
414	### Not tested
415	
416	- **A released package:** the trust prompt in Xcode, and `-skipPackagePluginValidation` on the command line. This is the first thing the blind trial will meet.
417	- Xcode's own interface: adding the plug-in by clicking, and the previews canvas.
418	- A plain Swift package as the host (the plug-in's code for it compiles and was never run).
419	- WAC against this SDK. The change adds files and one fallback line in `RipulBaseTokenProvider`; reasoned, not built.
420	- Mac Catalyst, iOS 17 and 26, Dynamic Type, Increased Contrast, right-to-left.
421	- A switch of theme while the zero-edit app runs, and the picker. Reasoned to work as in the second trial, since the same accessors are read in the same bodies.
422	- A large host: the generator reads every Swift file of the target on every build. On Sandsend's 16 files it is not measurable.
423	- The named hues drawn on screen, and the third `Image` font.
424	- 26 of the 36 brand screenshots, which I did not open.
425	- Any Swift version but 6.4, and the `MemberImportVisibility` upcoming feature.
426	- A person's time. An agent's was about two hours, most of it building the plug-in and waiting for a loaded Mac.

# What the SDK's theme system costs a host app

A trial on Sandsend Retreats (branch `theme-trial`, commit `d19626c`), by an agent acting as the host's developer, using only the public package at v0.7.170, the `ripul_guide` tool and the app's own repository. 11 October 2026, 08:46 to 09:07. The SDK's home repository was not read at any point.

## The answer

- **20 minutes** from the first read to the build running on Peter's iPhone (measured, from the clock). About 10 were the agent working, 8 waiting for builds and screenshots, 2 measuring baselines. These are an agent's minutes: a person would take most of a day, because the work is reading 2,800 lines and editing 12 files.
- **706 lines added, 90 removed, in 27 files** (measured, `git diff main --shortstat`). The app was 1,633 lines of Swift. Only 78 of those lines are what `theming.md` promises a host writes (a token where a system value was).
- **202 of the lines are a script the SDK documents and does not ship**, and without it the View Explorer names no tokens.

## What did not work

Things the package did not tell me, or told me wrongly.

1. **The three scripts `theming.md` tells you to run are not in the package.** `rewrite_theme_tokens.py`, `check_theme_tokens.py` and `theme_usage_map.py` are given with paths under `ripul-native-app/scripts/`. The package has `tools/publish-theme.mjs` and nothing else. So I wrote my own rewrite (30 lines, thrown away), had no lint, and wrote the usage map generator from the keys `RipulThemeUsage.swift` parses (`k`, `role`, `ctl`, `ctlStyle`, `cond`, `form`, `via` …), which are documented nowhere. The explorer's own message, when the map is missing, tells the host to run "scripts/theme_usage_map.py". Even with the script, `theming.md` says it reads `.uiKitIdentifier(` and `.accessibilityIdentifier(`; this app names controls through its own `.identified(` wrapper, which it would not see. Not tested, since I do not have it.
2. **A serif has no accessor, so "the default document is empty" is false for this app.** Its headings were `.system(…, design: .serif)`. The only way to keep them is a non-empty default document naming `display: system-serif`. That `system-serif` in a family with a weight draws the same pixels as `.system(style, design: .serif, weight:)` is said nowhere; I measured it.
3. **A host cannot add a colour of its own.** The vocabulary is 15 roles, closed. This app has two brand colours that are not the accent under the default look (a fixed navy and a cream). I copied the SDK's `accentOr` idea by hand with `RipulTheme.isDefault`.
4. **Text colour at every site.** `theming.md` says a root cannot carry it and gives the reason. It does not say what to do about the 29 texts that never had a colour, and it does not warn that a container is no better than the root: there, even under the default document, a bordered button's label, a prominent button's label, a list's link and a section header all change colour. Found by screenshot.
5. **Lists are not reached.** A grouped list's ground, rows, separators and header colour stay the system's under a theme that names `surface` and `surfaceSunken`. `Section(themed:)` gives a header the family and not the colour. Nothing in `theming.md` mentions list backgrounds.
6. **The run-time switch and font registration that `theming.md` describes belong to the Ripul app.** `-ripul.theme.document`, `ripul://theme?name=` and `RipulAppTheme.registerFonts()` are not in the SDK. The host writes its own loading, its own persistence, its own switch and its own font registration.
7. **`theming.md` is written for the SDK's own migration, not for a host.** It opens by naming a plan in the home repository, its checks are the home repository's build commands, baselines and "streams". The host's part is twelve lines under "For the theme's owner".
8. **SDK fault: changing back to the default while running leaves the selected tab system blue** until the next launch. The app's accent is an asset colour; the root sets the window's tint to nil when the accent returns to default, and the tab bar does not go back to the asset's colour. Measured by screenshot. No cure in the host that I found.
9. **SDK fault: tab bar labels take the theme's family only after a change while running, not at launch.** At a fresh launch on the brand the labels are the system font; the explorer's readout says so in one breath: "`.AppleSystemUIFont 10 pt`" and "Font set by: the theme". After a live switch they are Source Sans. Measured by screenshot.

Smaller:

- A large navigation title takes the `text` family and the system's colour. A brand whose titles are in its display face, in its ink, cannot say so.
- A document cannot ask for a font feature. Playfair's figures are old-style, so "11:00" on the check-out tile and the dates on What's On look unlike the rest. A theme cannot ask for lining figures.
- `devicectl … launch` needs `--` before the bundle id to pass `-theme brand`; one failed launch. The app's own CLAUDE.md, not the SDK.
- I guessed that `.listRowBackground` on a list reaches its rows. It does not. SwiftUI, not the SDK.

**The forbidden repository was never needed.** Everything missing could be rebuilt from the package's source, at the cost of the 237 workaround lines.

My view, as the host. Each line is what it should be, then what stops it today.

1. **Add the package and put one modifier on the root.** True today: `.ripulThemeRoot()`, 1 line.
2. **Name a theme file, and nothing else.** `ripulThemeRoot(document: "sandsend-brand")` or a key in Info.plist. Today: 64 lines to find the file, read it, adopt it, keep the choice and fall back.
3. **Put font files in the bundle; the SDK registers what the document names.** Today: the host registers them.
4. **Switch themes with one call that the SDK keeps**, `RipulTheme.select("brand")`, with the launch argument and the URL that `theming.md` already describes working in any host. Today those exist only in the Ripul app.
5. **Run one command to migrate call sites, and one to check.** `swift package plugin` or a script in `tools/`. Today: the scripts are in another repository. This alone was 80 of my lines by a script of my own, and it would have caught the three `Image` fonts.
6. **Nothing at all for the View Explorer.** The package should bring the map generator as a build-tool plugin, and it should follow a host's identifier wrapper. Today: 202 lines and a build step.
7. **No edit for text that has no colour.** This needs the SDK to find a way: a `Text` wrapper, a container modifier that leaves controls alone, or an honest statement that every text needs a line, with the migration script adding it. Today: 29 hand edits, and every new `Text` forgets it silently.
8. **Lists themed by the root, or by one modifier the SDK ships.** Today: two helpers of my own on 2 lists and 6 sections.
9. **A design for a family** (`"display": "system-serif"` is there, but say it draws the same as `design: .serif`), and a way to name the host's own few colours in the same document, read with the same accessor. Today: a second document and a hand-made `accentOr`.
10. **A theme layer the host can link without the agent.** A `RipulTheme` product beside `RipulCommands` in `Package.swift`, with no dependencies. Today a guest's phone carries 60 MB of developer tooling to colour a holiday guide.
11. **A page of `theming.md` for hosts**, starting from "add the package", with none of the home repository's paths.

### What a host still pays, and four proposals

These were left out because each is a design decision. For each: the proposal I would make, its cost in my own working time (an agent's, reasoned from the size of the code, not measured), and its risk.

**1. A theme layer a host can link without the rest (item 10).**
Proposal: a `RipulTheme` library product in `Package.swift`, with no dependencies, holding `ThemeCore/`; `RipulAgent` re-exports it, so nothing a host or WAC writes today changes.
Cost: about half a day. Eight files move; the usage-map reader and the root have a few reaches into the rest of the SDK to cut (the legacy refresh environment key, the token provider stays behind).
Risk: Xcode links a package product into every configuration, so Sandsend gets the saving only if nothing in its Release build imports `RipulAgent`; today its console is already Debug-only, so it would. The Release app would lose about 60 MB (reasoned from the first trial's measurement, not built). A module rename can break a host that spells a type `RipulAgent.RipulTheme`; none of ours does.

**2. A host's own colours in the document (item 9).**
Proposal: a host declares its roles once in code, each with the colour it is today (`static let navy = RipulHostRole("navy", default: …)`), reads them with the same accessors (`.ripul(.navy)`), and names them in the same document under `roles`. The default is today's value, so the rule that nothing changes holds. The check, the lint and the usage map learn the declared names.
Cost: about a day, most of it the three tools and the tests.
Risk: two role types behind one accessor name can make `.ripul(.x)` ambiguous to the compiler where a host picks a name the SDK also uses; the alternative, turning the fixed enum into an open type, is cleaner to read and touches every `switch` over roles in the SDK. This is also the first step of moving WAC off the legacy engine, so its shape should be chosen with that in mind.

**3. Text that has no colour of its own (item 7).**
Proposal: do not look for a root-level cure; it was measured not to exist. Make it mechanical instead: `migrate` adds `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))` to every `Text` with no foreground in its chain, and `check` counts a bare `Text` so a new one fails the build.
Cost: about half a day, plus a measurement pass in each container (a button, a link, a list row, a toolbar) to prove the added line is an identity there.
Risk: the tool reads text, not types, so a `Text` built in a helper is missed, and inside a control an explicit text role is drawn as the control's tint, which is right today and may surprise under a theme. It is still a line a text; it stops being a line a person writes.

**4. Lists (item 8).**
Proposal: first spend two hours measuring whether a root can do it at all: `scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` set at the root reaches the lists below it, but a row's background set from outside a list does not (the first trial found that). If the root can carry the ground and UIKit's appearance can carry the rows, lists are themed with no edit. If not, one modifier, `.ripulThemedList()`, that `migrate` adds to each `List` and `Form`, with the rows' background applied by the SDK's `Section(themed:)`.
Cost: two hours to know, then half a day either way.
Risk: the system's grouped look has parts no public setting reaches on iOS 26 and later (the inset card's shape and its selected state); a themed row background may lose the system's highlight. Under the default document it must stay the system's own, which a modifier that does nothing until a theme names `surface` guarantees.

Also still the host's, with no proposal here: a font feature in the document (lining figures), the colour of a large navigation title and of a section header, and a way to keep a serif without a second document.
