### What was checked

- Default document: 36 screenshots (18 screens, light and dark). 34 the same pixel for pixel as the untouched app on the same SDK; the other two are the photo gallery, whose glass close button differs by one to two thousand pixels between two captures of the same build (measured).
- Brand: 36 screenshots taken, 8 opened.
- The switch while running: as step 13. Both tab bar faults of the first run are gone (measured).
- `check` zero; `lint` one complaint, which is wrong (below).
- On the phone: installed and running, launched on the brand, which is kept. A screenshot of the phone a minute later showed Peter in another app, so I did not relaunch over him: **the brand on the phone's own screen is not seen by me.**

### What did not work this time

1. **`migrate` adds no `import RipulAgent`, and the page does not say a file needs one.** Nine files were rewritten to call `.ripul(…)` with nothing imported. I knew a cure (`@_exported import`, one line) only from the first run. A fresh host gets nine compile errors and adds nine lines.
2. **`lint` fails on the page's own first step.** With the root line added as step 1 says, `lint` exits 1: "the hunk adds and removes different numbers of lines", on `.ripulThemeRoot(theme: "standard")`. It also counts 51 replacements where `migrate` reported 55.
3. **`migrate` does not follow a host's font helper.** It follows an identifier wrapper; it does not follow `static func serif(_:weight:) -> Font`, which this app uses at 10 headings. `check` lists each. They are mechanical: the helper's body says which family.
4. **`--named` leaves `.black.opacity(…)`.** The page says `--named` writes the system form for black. Inside a gradient's colour list and a shadow it does not (6 lines), and `check` then fails on them.
5. **`-ripul.theme.document` lasts for one launch.** The page calls the key "the choice", which reads as kept. A launch argument overrides a default for that launch and is not stored. The link, which does store it, needs a URL scheme, and this app has none. So there is no way to leave a device on a theme, or to prove a switch while running, without a tap or code of the host's.
6. **A host's agent cannot see what the explorer says.** `usage-map --explain` shows the map, not the answer. The answer is behind a tap in a console that needs a person signed in. I called `RipulTokenInspector.readout` from temporary code, as the first run did.
7. **A control named from a variable is not in the map:** `.identified(name + ".call")`, 8 of this app's 24 named places. The explorer says so plainly when asked; the page does not.
8. **The build line reads "768 identifiers … following .cmsInspectorID, .identified(".** 16 of the 768 are this app's; the rest and the first wrapper are the SDK's own screens. A host reading its build log cannot tell what was found in its own code.
9. **"They should be the same" is not quite true on iOS 26 and later.** A glass control differs between two captures of one build. The page should say to compare twice.
10. **The page's order.** Step 8 opens "Before the first edit". It belongs before step 1.
11. **The page's table and API list leave out `.ripulGlassProminentButtonStyle()`,** which `migrate` writes.
12. **The example document on the host page is this app's brand** (the same navy, paper, ink and both font families). Step 5 here was partly copying. Another host would not have that.

Mine, not the SDK's: a first edit script that failed on its own ordering (1 minute), a shell loop that passed its arguments as one word and photographed the wrong screen (2 minutes), one actor-isolation error in the temporary code (1 minute), and a 4-second wait before each screenshot that was too short for three of 36.

### What the host should still not have had to do

1. **A text colour, a line a text: 30 lines.** Unchanged from the first run, and it is the only cost that grows with every screen. The page is honest about it. Nothing warns when a new `Text` lacks it: `check` reads zero either way.
2. **Lists: 22 lines.** Two helpers of mine (14 lines) and a call on 2 lists and 6 sections. The page gives the modifiers and says they are unmeasured. Measured here: under the default document they change no pixel, light or dark, on both lists.
3. **A second document to keep a serif: 7 lines,** and with it the plain system look is no longer the app's look, so the picker must hide it (`systemTitle: nil`).
4. **The brand's own two colours by hand: 3 lines** of `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent) ? mine : theirs`.
5. **A label taken apart (5 lines) and a row's dimming moved to its texts (5 lines),** both only because a text colour cannot sit on a container.
6. **A lever to keep a theme (5 lines).**
7. **One import line** that the migration should have written.
8. **The whole package in Release.** 76,760 KB for the Release simulator app (measured), to read two JSON files.
9. **What a document cannot say,** seen on the brand: a large navigation title stays black on the paper in light, section headers keep the system's grey, navigation titles are in the text family and not the display one, and Playfair's old-style figures on times and dates.

With 1, 2, 5 and 7 done by the SDK or its tool, this run's hand-written code would have been about 45 lines: a document, a root line, a picker, the build step and the two colours.

### Not measured

- The brand on the phone's own screen, and the picker in the More menu, which no screenshot of mine shows: it needs a tap.
- The 28 brand screenshots I did not open.
- The View Explorer as a person sees it.
- What a fresh host's time would be: see "This run was not blind".
- An archive, TestFlight, Dynamic Type, Increased Contrast, VoiceOver, right-to-left.
- A person's time. Every minute here is an agent's.

## Third trial: no change to the host's source

Sandsend Retreats' `main` in a throwaway copy (`/tmp/sandsend-zero`, removed), against the SDK in this repository at commit `b09493db9` (not released). 11 October 2026. Xcode 27.1 (27A9269), Swift 6.4, XcodeGen 2.45.3, iPhone 18 Pro simulator on iOS 27.0. Every figure is marked measured or reasoned.

Peter's question: "Is there any way to do this without us changing the host's source code?"

- **Yes, it works.** Sandsend builds and runs themed with not one line of Swift added or changed (measured: `git status` shows `project.yml` and new files only). Under the system look all 36 screenshots match the untouched app: 34 pixel for pixel, and the 2 of the photo gallery differ only where two captures of one build differ.
- **What the host does: 3 lines of project settings and 8 new files.** The plug-in on the app target (3 lines of `project.yml`), one theme document (28 lines), four font files, two licences and a note. No root line, no Info.plist key, no build phase, no script. The pin line changes as for any SDK release.
- **What would stop me recommending it as the only route:** it rests on how the Swift compiler chooses between two declarations of one name, which the language does not promise; and it reaches less than the migration does, on this app most visibly the two lists, which stay the system's black and grey in dark beside navy pages.

My recommendation: make this the way a host starts, and keep `migrate` for a host that wants the rest.

### What was built

All in the SDK, opt-in. A host that does not switch the plug-in on gets none of it.

- **A build-tool plug-in, `RipulThemeRedirect`** (`Package.swift`, `Plugins/RipulThemeRedirect/plugin.swift`). On every build it runs `tools/ripul-theme redirect`, which writes one Swift file into the build folder; Xcode compiles that file into the host's own module.
- **The generated file** (`tools/redirect/RipulThemeRedirect.swift.txt`, 140 lines) declares SwiftUI's names again: the 11 text styles, `Font.system(size:weight:design:)` and `Font.system(_:design:weight:)`, `Font.weight`, `bold` and `italic`, `Image.font`, `Color.red` and four more hues, `Color.primary` and `.secondary`, `Color(UIColor)`, `foregroundStyle` for the hierarchy styles on `View` and `Text`, and `WindowGroup`. Each is one call into the SDK.
- **`ThemeCore/RipulThemeRedirect.swift`** (203 lines) is where each call lands and where everything is decided. With no theme each returns the call site's own value, itself (7 tests).
- **The root with no line written.** The generated `WindowGroup` wraps the host's content in the theme root and installs the theme: the one Info.plist names, or the bundle's only theme document when it names none.
- **A serif with no second document.** `design: .serif` becomes the display family once a theme names one and is the system's serif until then. Both earlier trials needed a 7-line "standard" document for this.
- **The View Explorer's map with no build phase.** The generator reads the unedited source as the migration would have left it and puts the map in the generated file, inside `#if DEBUG`.
- **A name the host already declares is left out** of the generated file, so the host's own is used.

### What the host did, counted

All measured from `git status` and `git diff` in the copy.

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Swift lines added or changed | 0 |
| `project.yml` | 3 lines added for the plug-in. (2 more lines replaced the pin with a path to the unreleased SDK; a released SDK is the usual 1-line pin change.) |
| Theme document | 1 file, 28 lines, copied from `theme-trial-2` |
| Fonts | 4 files, 1.6 MB, and 2 licences and a note (199 lines), copied from `theme-trial-2` |
| Info.plist, build phases, scripts, root line, import lines | 0 |
| Build time | Debug simulator 19 to 22 s incremental, 4 to 5 s with nothing changed; Release clean 210 s (the second trial: 207 s) |
| Release app | 76,724 KB (the second trial: 76,760 KB), no usage map in the binary |

Against the earlier trials: 706 lines added in 27 files, then 411 in 23, now 230 in 9 files (8 of them new), of which 199 are licences and the fonts' note, 28 the theme document and 3 the settings.

### Under the system look: nothing moved

Measured. 18 screens, light and dark, the zero-edit build launched with `-ripul.theme.document system` against the untouched app on the same SDK.

- 34 of 36 the same pixel for pixel.
- The 2 that differ are the photo gallery: 1,263 and 1,478 pixels, in rows 2249 to 2388. Two captures of the zero-edit build itself differ by 756 and 1,468 pixels in the same rows. That is the glass button the second trial reported.
- The baseline was captured once in full, not twice: the Mac's load average was 86 and a pass took half an hour.

### On the brand: what took the theme, by kind

Counts of call sites are measured from the source. "Seen" means in a screenshot I opened: 10 of the 36 brand screenshots, and 2 more taken with a document that changes sizes.

| Kind | Sites in Sandsend | Took the theme? |
|---|---|---|
| Text with a text style (`.font(.headline)`, `.font(.footnote.weight(.semibold))`) | 23 on text and labels | Yes, all (measured: each resolves to the generated declaration; seen in Source Sans 3) |
| Text with a fixed size | 1, the wordmark, a serif | Yes, in the display face (seen) |
| Text with no font | most of the app's 54 `Text`s | Yes, through the root's default font (seen) |
| The app's own helper, `Font.serif(_:weight:)` | 10 | Yes, in Playfair Display (seen). The helper calls `.system(_:design:weight:)`, which is redirected inside it. The migration left these 10 for a person. |
| Symbols: a font on an `Image` | 3 | Correctly not resized. With a document setting title to 48 pt and footnote to 24 pt, the paw (`.font(.title)`) and the chevrons (`.font(.footnote.weight(.semibold))`) kept their size while the text beside them grew (seen for 2 of the 3). |
| Symbols: the icon of a `Label` | 9 | They follow the label's font size, as they did before and as they do after a migration (seen for 2) |
| Named colours that are a role (red, orange, green, blue, gray) | 0 | Nothing to measure in this app. Compiled and resolved in a scratch file, not seen drawn. |
| White, black, clear | 12 | Never themed, by either route |
| Hierarchy styles in `foregroundStyle` | 9 (8 secondary, 1 tertiary) | Yes (seen: the brand's dim grey) |
| Wrapped system colours, `Color(.systemGroupedBackground)` | 10 | Yes: the paper ground and the cards, light and dark (seen) |
| Text with no colour of its own | about 30 (the second trial's count) | No. It stays the system's black or white, not the brand's ink. |
| Lists | 2 lists, 3 sections | No. Ground, rows and header colour stay the system's; the header takes the family. In dark the two list screens are black and grey beside navy pages (seen). |
| Navigation titles | 3 | The family, not the colour; the same as the migration (seen) |
| Tab bar | 1 | Labels in the family at launch, the selected tab in the accent (seen) |
| Prominent buttons | 5 | Not touched, on purpose. They carry `.tint(Brand.navy)`, and the brand's dark `onAccent` on that fixed navy would not be readable. They stay navy with white labels (seen). |
| The app's own two colours, `Brand.navy` and `Brand.cream` | 13 | No. They are asset colours; no route but a line of code reaches them. |
| `.foregroundStyle(.tint)` | 4 | Yes, through the window's tint (seen) |

**The View Explorer names tokens for unedited source** (measured, by asking the running app through the debugger, since nobody is signed in to its console). For `stay.cottage` on the brand: "Font | headline | Source Sans 3 17 pt semibold | family from the theme document", "Foreground | ripul.textSecondary | #6A6F80 light, #A4ABC0 dark | theme document", "Background | ripul.surface | #FFFFFF light, #151F3D dark | theme document", and "symbol size | never themed" for the chevron. 16 identifiers are in the map. A font that goes through the app's own helper is reported as "not a theme token" though it is themed: the map reads text and does not follow the helper.

### What broke, and the edges

Each of these was measured in the real app's build, in scratch files that were removed before the measured build.

| Edge | Result |
|---|---|
| Does Xcode compile a plug-in's generated Swift into an app target, and does XcodeGen express it? | Yes to both. `buildToolPlugins` in `project.yml`; the file lands in `build/Build/Intermediates.noindex/BuildToolPluginIntermediates/`. |
| What the host must allow | With the SDK as a local path, nothing: the build ran without `-skipPackagePluginValidation`. For a released package Xcode asks "Trust & Enable" once and `xcodebuild` needs that flag. **Not measured**, because the SDK was not released. It means Sandsend's ship script and the commands in its CLAUDE.md would each gain that flag. |
| The plug-in's sandbox | `/usr/bin/python3` runs inside it and reads the host's sources. |
| `.font(.body)`, `Font.body`, `SwiftUI.Font.body`, in an array, in a ternary, in generic code | All call the generated declaration (read from the object file's symbols). Even the name qualified with `SwiftUI.` is redirected, so a host has no spelling that means "the system's". |
| A redeclared generic method | **Did not work as the probes suggested.** `foregroundStyle<S: ShapeStyle>` and `Image.font(_: Font?)` made every use ambiguous and the app did not compile: SwiftUI's return an opaque type, so the two signatures are never the same. They are now declared as closer matches instead (`foregroundStyle(_: HierarchicalShapeStyle)`, `Image.font(_: Font)`). So the design leans on two compiler behaviours, not one. |
| A hierarchy style given to `fill`, `stroke` or `background` | Not redirected. Only `foregroundStyle` is. |
| A host with its own `extension Font { static var caption }` or `Color.red` | A compile error, "invalid redeclaration", naming the generated file, until the generator learned to leave such names out. Now it builds and the host's own is used. The generator reads text; a declaration it cannot see is still that error. |
| A host type named `WindowGroup`, `WindowGroup(for:)`, a UIKit app delegate | The first is left out by the generator (tested in the tool's tests, not in the app). The other two are not covered: the host adds a flag and writes the root line. |
| A second module | A framework target with the plug-in switched on built and was redirected, in Swift 6 language mode. A target without the plug-in is untouched. |
| Previews | A `#Preview` compiled. Not run in Xcode's canvas. |
| Release and Debug | Both build. The usage map is in Debug only. |
| Incremental builds | A host file that gains a clashing name is picked up on the next build (5 s); the generated file changes and the app recompiles. |
| Two theme documents and no name | The system look, and a line in the log saying to add the Info.plist key (met by accident, when I added a second document for the symbol test). |
| A value equal but not identical | The SDK's new test caught one: `design: .default` was returned as `design: nil`. Fixed before the pixel comparison. |

**Is the rule promised?** No. That a module's own declaration is preferred to an imported one with the same name and type is how the compiler's name lookup behaves, and I know of nothing in The Swift Programming Language or an accepted proposal that states it. The closer-match rule (a non-generic or non-optional parameter is preferred) is ordinary overload ranking and is equally unwritten. Tested with Swift 6.4 only, in Swift 5 and Swift 6 language modes. If a release changed either, the likely failure is loud (an ambiguity error in the host's files) and the cure is to switch the plug-in off; the less likely one is silent, the host going back to the system look.

Mine, not the design's: a first screenshot pass was blank because captures were taken before a slow launch finished; and two build logs were lost to a filter that closed the pipe.

### The two routes compared

| | The plug-in (this trial) | `migrate` (the second trial) |
|---|---|---|
| The host's Swift | 0 lines | about 140 changed or added: 72 at call sites by the tool and one expression, 70 by decision |
| Reaches: text styles, fixed sizes, hierarchy styles, wrapped system colours, named hues | Yes | Yes |
| Reaches: the app's own serif helper | Yes, with no edit | By hand, 10 sites |
| Keeps a serif with no second document | Yes | No, 7 lines |
| Symbols keep their size | Yes, at run time | Yes, in the source (`ripulIcon`) |
| Text with no colour | No | 30 lines by hand |
| Lists, section headers, empty states | No | 22 lines and the themed forms |
| Prominent buttons' labels | No | Yes |
| The host's own colours | No | 3 lines by hand |
| View Explorer | Yes, no setup | Yes, one build phase |
| What the source says | `.font(.body)`: nothing shows that it is themed | `.font(.ripul(.body))`: it says so |
| Stays themed as the app grows | By itself, for what it reaches | Only with `check` in the build |
| Rests on | Unwritten compiler behaviour; a name clash is a compile error | Public API only |
| To undo | Remove 3 lines | Revert the edits |
| Fails how | Loudly at compile time, or (a compiler change) silently unthemed | A missed site is silently the system's |

They mix: a migrated file calls the accessors directly and the rest goes through the generated file. So the plug-in can be the start and the migration the finish, a file at a time.

### On the phone: not installed

**The build is made and signed (`/tmp/sz-device.app`, measured) and is not on Peter's iPhone.** From 10:40 until I stopped, CoreDevice listed the phone as unavailable and the bridge reported it "waiting_for_listener", not reachable; I checked five times, the last at the end. The install page route was not used: it ships committed work from Sandsend's own repository, which this trial was not to touch. When the phone is reachable: `xcrun devicectl device install app --device 00008150-001C544E0EBA401C /tmp/sz-device.app`, then launch `io.ripul.sandsendretreats`. It opens on the brand with no argument, because the brand is the bundle's only theme document. `/tmp` does not survive a restart of the Mac.

### What was checked in the SDK

All measured: 56 theme tests pass (5 new on macOS; 2 more are iOS-only and were compiled, not run); 7 tests of the tools pass (3 new); the SDK builds for macOS and for the iOS simulator with the `--triple` form; `check_theme_tokens.py` on Ripul's own sources reads zero; the private-function check is clean; Ripul's app compiles for the simulator (`BUILD SUCCEEDED`; the log also carried "Could not archive SSU artifacts", which I did not look into).

### Not tested

- **A released package:** the trust prompt in Xcode, and `-skipPackagePluginValidation` on the command line. This is the first thing the blind trial will meet.
- Xcode's own interface: adding the plug-in by clicking, and the previews canvas.
- A plain Swift package as the host (the plug-in's code for it compiles and was never run).
- WAC against this SDK. The change adds files and one fallback line in `RipulBaseTokenProvider`; reasoned, not built.
- Mac Catalyst, iOS 17 and 26, Dynamic Type, Increased Contrast, right-to-left.
- A switch of theme while the zero-edit app runs, and the picker. Reasoned to work as in the second trial, since the same accessors are read in the same bodies.
- A large host: the generator reads every Swift file of the target on every build. On Sandsend's 16 files it is not measurable.
- The named hues drawn on screen, and the third `Image` font.
- 26 of the 36 brand screenshots, which I did not open.
- Any Swift version but 6.4, and the `MemberImportVisibility` upcoming feature.
- A person's time. An agent's was about two hours, most of it building the plug-in and waiting for a loaded Mac.

1	# Ripul guides
2	
3	What an agent needs to know to use Ripul on someone's repository, served one topic at a time. This is how product knowledge ships: not as memories, and not as a long system prompt.
4	
5	## The three parts
6	
7	| Part | Where | What it carries |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| The harness note | `CliServerBase.ripulHarnessNote` (`ripul-native-app/macOS/CliServerBase.swift`) | One paragraph, in every agent's standing instructions: you are inside Ripul, and before using artefacts, plans, the browser, voice or a shared build, call `ripul_guide`. Nothing else. |
10	| The tool | `ripul_guide` (`config/ToolsDefault.yaml`, `src/LLM/Tools/RipulGuideHandler.ts`) | With no arguments, the list of guides and when to read each. With `topic`, that guide. |
11	| The guides | `public/guides/<id>.md`, listed in `public/guides/index.json` | The knowledge itself. Plain Markdown, served beside the app, live with a web deploy. |
12	
13	The note is always an addition to what is already there, never a replacement. Claude gets it through `--append-system-prompt`. Codex has no append: a thread's `developerInstructions` replaces the configured value, so the shared runtime first reads the user's own `developer_instructions` (`config/read`) and sends theirs followed by the note, and sends nothing if it cannot read them. The exec path cannot read them back, so it sends the note (`-c developer_instructions=`) only when the user's `config.toml` sets none. Both get it only when the session has the `ripul_tools` server, since the note names a tool from it. Antigravity has no slot for standing instructions that the host uses yet, so it does not get the note.
14	
15	`ripul_guide` replaced `helpTool`, which loaded thirteen documents from the old Chrome extension through `chrome.runtime.getURL` and so worked nowhere else.
16	
17	## Adding or changing a guide
18	
19	1. Write `public/guides/<id>.md`. Write for an agent in a stranger's repository: no Ripul source paths, no commit hashes, none of our machines. State the rule and the reason, not the incident it came from.
20	2. Check every claim against the code or the live tool. Memories are raw material, not a source: a review on 8 October 2026 thought nearly half of them might be out of date.
21	3. Add an entry to `public/guides/index.json`. `when` is the trigger an agent reads to decide whether to open the guide, so say when, not what.
22	4. If agents should see the topic without listing first, add a line to the tool's description in `config/ToolsDefault.yaml`. Keep that list to the topics most likely to be missed.
23	5. `npm run deploy:all`.
24	
25	A limit that belongs to one tool goes in that tool's description, not in a guide. Something a built-in feature of the agent competes with (its own question tool, its own artifacts) is better switched off by the host than argued with in a guide.
26

# Ripul guides

What an agent needs to know to use Ripul on someone's repository, served one topic at a time. This is how product knowledge ships: not as memories, and not as a long system prompt.

## The three parts

| Part | Where | What it carries |
|---|---|---|
| The harness note | `CliServerBase.ripulHarnessNote` (`ripul-native-app/macOS/CliServerBase.swift`) | One paragraph, in every agent's standing instructions: you are inside Ripul, and before using artefacts, plans, the browser, voice or a shared build, call `ripul_guide`. Nothing else. |
| The tool | `ripul_guide` (`config/ToolsDefault.yaml`, `src/LLM/Tools/RipulGuideHandler.ts`) | With no arguments, the list of guides and when to read each. With `topic`, that guide. |
| The guides | `public/guides/<id>.md`, listed in `public/guides/index.json` | The knowledge itself. Plain Markdown, served beside the app, live with a web deploy. |

The note is always an addition to what is already there, never a replacement. Claude gets it through `--append-system-prompt`. Codex has no append: a thread's `developerInstructions` replaces the configured value, so the shared runtime first reads the user's own `developer_instructions` (`config/read`) and sends theirs followed by the note, and sends nothing if it cannot read them. The exec path cannot read them back, so it sends the note (`-c developer_instructions=`) only when the user's `config.toml` sets none. Both get it only when the session has the `ripul_tools` server, since the note names a tool from it. Antigravity has no slot for standing instructions that the host uses yet, so it does not get the note.

`ripul_guide` replaced `helpTool`, which loaded thirteen documents from the old Chrome extension through `chrome.runtime.getURL` and so worked nowhere else.

## Adding or changing a guide

1. Write `public/guides/<id>.md`. Write for an agent in a stranger's repository: no Ripul source paths, no commit hashes, none of our machines. State the rule and the reason, not the incident it came from.
2. Check every claim against the code or the live tool. Memories are raw material, not a source: a review on 8 October 2026 thought nearly half of them might be out of date.
3. Add an entry to `public/guides/index.json`. `when` is the trigger an agent reads to decide whether to open the guide, so say when, not what.
4. If agents should see the topic without listing first, add a line to the tool's description in `config/ToolsDefault.yaml`. Keep that list to the topics most likely to be missed.
5. `npm run deploy:all`.

A limit that belongs to one tool goes in that tool's description, not in a guide. Something a built-in feature of the agent competes with (its own question tool, its own artifacts) is better switched off by the host than argued with in a guide.

Memories tagged `scope: product`, and the 64 tagged `scope_also: product`, are the backlog for new guides: see `docs/reviews/memory-sort-2026-10-08.md`.

1	# A theme for your app
2	
3	This page is for an app that links the RipulAgent package and wants its own
4	fonts and colours to come from a theme: one JSON document, light and dark,
5	switchable while the app runs. It starts from "add the package" and is in the
6	order to do the work. The full contract, with every measurement behind a rule
7	here, is [theming.md](theming.md); you should not need it to get through this
8	page.
9	
10	What you write, in total: one line at the root, a theme document, your font
11	files, one line of build setup for the View Explorer, and whatever the
12	migration command leaves for a person to decide. Everything else is the SDK's.
13	
14	Where a thing is not built, this page says so. The list is at the end.
15	
16	## The idea
17	
18	Every token has a default that is the system value you write today.
19	`Font.ripul(.body)` is `Font.body`. `.ripul(.textSecondary)` is the system's
20	`.secondary` style. So moving a call site to a token changes no pixel, and an
21	app with no theme document looks exactly as it did. A document changes a token
22	only by naming it.
23	
24	## With no change to your source
25	
26	There are two ways to adopt the theme. The numbered steps below are the first:
27	you move your call sites to tokens, with a command that does most of it. This
28	section is the second: you change settings and add files, and no line of your
29	Swift changes. It is not in a release yet, and it has been measured on one
30	app.
31	
32	What you do:
33	
34	1. Add the package to the app target, as in step 1 below, without the root
35	   line.
36	2. Put your theme document and font files in the bundle (steps 2 and 3).
37	3. Switch on the package's build-tool plug-in, `RipulThemeRedirect`, for the app
38	   target: in Xcode, the target's Build Phases, "Run Build Tool Plug-ins", add
39	   it. In an XcodeGen `project.yml`:
40	
41	   ```yaml
42	       buildToolPlugins:
43	         - plugin: RipulThemeRedirect
44	           package: RipulAgent
45	   ```
46	4. Allow the plug-in to run. Xcode asks once, "Trust & Enable". A command-line
47	   build passes `-skipPackagePluginValidation` to `xcodebuild`. (Not yet
48	   measured with a released package; a package added by local path needs
49	   neither.)
50	
51	With one theme document in the bundle, that document is the app's theme. With
52	several, name one with the Info.plist key `RipulTheme`.
53	
54	**How it works.** On every build the plug-in writes one Swift file into the
55	build folder, and Xcode compiles it into your app's own module. The file
56	declares SwiftUI's names again: `Font.body` and the other text styles,
57	`Font.system(size:)`, `Color.red`, `Color(.systemBackground)`,
58	`.foregroundStyle(.secondary)`, `WindowGroup`. Inside your module your
59	declaration of a name is chosen over SwiftUI's, so your existing `.font(.body)`
60	calls the generated one, which is one call into the SDK. With no theme each
61	returns exactly what SwiftUI's would have. Nothing is added to your repository.
62	
63	**What it reaches,** with no edit:
64	
65	| You wrote | It follows |
66	|---|---|
67	| `.font(.body)`, `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))`, `Font.body` | the type role of that name |
68	| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` | the text family at that size |
69	| `.system(.title, design: .serif)`, `.system(size: 22, design: .serif)`, and your own helper built on them | the display family, once a theme names one; the system's serif until then, with no second document |
70	| `design: .monospaced` | the code family |
71	| a font on an `Image` | nothing: a symbol keeps its system size |
72	| `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and the other hierarchy styles | the text roles |
73	| `Color(.systemBackground)`, `Color(.systemGroupedBackground)`, `Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground)` | `canvas`, `surfaceSunken`, `surface` |
74	| `Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)`, green, blue, gray | `danger`, `warning`, `success`, `info`, `neutral` |
75	| `WindowGroup { … }` | the theme root, with no line written: the accent, the body font for text with none, navigation titles, tab bar labels |
76	| identified elements | the View Explorer names their tokens (Debug builds), with no build phase |
77	
78	**What it does not reach.** These stay the system's under a theme, where the
79	migration command or a line of yours would have reached them:
80	
81	- text with no colour of its own, as in "What it leaves for you", 1;
82	- lists, section headers and empty states, as in 2 and 3;
83	- a prominent button's label (`onAccent`);
84	- a hierarchy style given to `fill`, `stroke` or `background`, and one passed
85	  through a variable of a generic type;
86	- a colour of your own (`Color("BrandNavy")`), and white and black;
87	- UIKit code (`UIFont.preferredFont`, `UIColor.label`);
88	- a `Label`'s icon, which takes its size from the label's font as before.
89	
90	**What can go wrong.**
91	
92	- A name you already declare (`extension Font { static var caption }`, a type
93	  called `WindowGroup`) is left out of the generated file and yours is used.
94	  The generator reads text, not types; one it misses is a compile error naming
95	  both places.
96	- A target is redirected only if the plug-in is on for it. A framework of your
97	  own needs it switched on too.
98	- `WindowGroup(for:)` and a UIKit app delegate are not covered: put
99	  `.ripulThemeRoot()` on the root yourself and add `RIPUL_THEME_NO_ROOT` to the
100	  target's Swift compilation conditions. `RIPUL_THEME_NO_STYLES` leaves
101	  `foregroundStyle` alone.
102	- A font or colour kept in a `static let` is read once and does not follow a
103	  switch while the app runs.
104	- The rule this rests on, that a module's own declaration is preferred to an
105	  imported one of the same name and type, is how the Swift compiler behaves
106	  (measured with Swift 6.4, Xcode 27.1, in Swift 5 and Swift 6 language
107	  modes). The language's documentation does not promise it.
108	
109	The two ways mix: a file you have migrated calls the accessors directly, and
110	the rest goes through the generated file.
111	
112	## 1. Add the package and name your theme
113	
114	Pin the package (`https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk`), then put one
115	modifier on the root view of each window group:
116	
117	```swift
118	import RipulAgent
119	
120	WindowGroup {
121	    ContentView()
122	        .ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")     // brand.json in the app's bundle
123	}
124	```
125	
126	That line is the whole setup. From it the SDK:
127	
128	- finds `brand.json` in the bundle (at its top level, or in a folder named
129	  `Themes` or `Theme`), reads it and puts it in use before the first view is
130	  drawn;
131	- registers the font files the document names (step 3);
132	- keeps a choice made with `RipulTheme.select` between launches (step 6);
133	- falls back to `brand`, and then to the system look, when a document is
134	  missing, is not a theme document, or was written for a newer SDK. It logs
135	  which, with the prefix `[RipulTheme]`.
136	
137	Two other ways to say the same thing, for an app that cannot put it on a root:
138	
139	- the Info.plist key `RipulTheme` with the document's name, and a plain
140	  `.ripulThemeRoot()`;
141	- `RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand")` in the `App`'s `init` or the app
142	  delegate, for a UIKit app.
143	
144	With no name at all, `.ripulThemeRoot()` leaves the app on the system look.
145	
146	The root carries the accent (as the window's tint, so `.tint`,
147	`Color.accentColor` and control tints follow with no edit) and the theme's
148	body font for text with no font of its own. A sheet presented with
149	`.ripulSheet` has a root already. A presented `UIHostingController` of your
150	own needs `.ripulThemeRoot()` on its root view.
151	
152	## 2. Write the document
153	
154	Every key is optional, and an absent key is today's look. Start with
155	`{ "schema": 1, "name": "Brand" }`, which changes nothing, and add to it.
156	
157	```json
158	{
159	  "schema": 1,
160	  "name": "Brand",
161	  "palette": {
162	    "navy":  { "light": "#24386b", "dark": "#a9bdeb" },
163	    "paper": { "light": "#f7f3ec", "dark": "#0d1428" },
164	    "ink":   "#1c2540"
165	  },
166	  "roles": {
167	    "ripul.accent": "navy",
168	    "ripul.canvas": "paper",
169	    "ripul.text": "ink"
170	  },
171	  "typography": {
172	    "families": { "text": "Source Sans 3", "display": "Playfair Display", "code": "system-monospaced" },
173	    "roles": {
174	      "display": { "size": 34, "weight": "bold" },
175	      "eyebrow": { "tracking": 1.8, "uppercase": true }
176	    }
177	  }
178	}
179	```
180	
181	- **`palette`** names your colours. A value is `#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA`,
182	  `system:<name>` (a live system colour such as `system:label`), or a light
183	  and dark pair of those. Light and dark are written here and nowhere else.
184	- **`roles`** gives each colour role a palette name, another role, or a colour
185	  string. The fifteen roles, each with the system colour it is by default:
186	
187	  | Role | Default | For |
188	  |---|---|---|
189	  | `accent` | the app's tint | selection, links, primary buttons |
190	  | `onAccent` | white | text and icons on an accent fill |
191	  | `canvas` | `systemBackground` | the app's background |
192	  | `surface` | `secondarySystemGroupedBackground` | cards and grouped rows |
193	  | `surfaceSunken` | `systemGroupedBackground` | the ground behind cards |
194	  | `text`, `textSecondary`, `textTertiary`, `textQuaternary` | `.primary` to `.quaternary` | text |
195	  | `separator` | `separator` | hairlines |
196	  | `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `neutral` | green, orange, red, blue, grey | state |
197	
198	  The set is closed: a document cannot add a role (see the end).
199	- **`typography.families`** names the three families, `text`, `display` and
200	  `code`. Each is a font family you bundle, or one of `system`,
201	  `system-serif`, `system-rounded`, `system-monospaced`.
202	- **`typography.roles`** changes a type role: `size`, `weight`, `family`,
203	  `relativeTo`, `tracking`, `uppercase`, `catalystSize`. The roles are the
204	  eleven system text styles by their own names, plus `display` (a title in
205	  the display family), `eyebrow` and `code`.
206	
207	**A serif that is yours already.** `"display": "system-serif"` draws what
208	`.font(.system(.title, design: .serif))` draws (compared pixel for pixel in a
209	host's trial on iOS 27, at the default text size). There is no accessor for
210	`design: .serif` itself. So an app whose headings are serif today keeps them
211	by naming `system-serif` as its display family and writing
212	`.font(.ripul(.title, family: .display))` at those headings. Its document is
213	then not empty, and the plain system look (`RipulTheme.systemThemeName`) is
214	not the look it had.
215	
216	Check a dark value against its background yourself: nothing checks contrast.
217	
218	## 3. Fonts
219	
220	Put the font files in the app's bundle, at its top level or in a folder named
221	`Fonts`. Do nothing else. When a document names a family that is not the
222	system's, the SDK reads the bundled `.ttf`, `.otf` and `.ttc` files and
223	registers those that hold a face of that family. No `UIAppFonts` entry and no
224	registration call.
225	
226	- The name in the document is the font's family name ("Source Sans 3"), not
227	  its file name.
228	- A variable font takes weights; a family with one weight draws that weight
229	  whatever is asked, and the system does not fake a bold.
230	- Ship each font's licence beside it. That is yours to get right.
231	
232	## 4. Move the call sites: one command
233	
234	The package brings its tools. In an Xcode project they are in the package
235	checkout, under the build's DerivedData:
236	
237	```bash
238	# with -derivedDataPath build
239	RIPUL_THEME=build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
240	# with Xcode's default DerivedData
241	RIPUL_THEME=$(ls -d ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/<Project>-*/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme | head -1)
242	# in a Swift package
243	RIPUL_THEME=.build/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
244	```
245	
246	They need `python3` and nothing else.
247	
248	```bash
249	$RIPUL_THEME migrate --dry-run --named <your source folder>   # what would change
250	$RIPUL_THEME migrate --named <your source folder>             # change it
251	```
252	
253	Every rewrite is to the token whose default is the value it replaces, so
254	nothing moves on screen. It rewrites:
255	
256	| You wrote | It writes |
257	|---|---|
258	| `.font(.body)`, `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))` | `.font(.ripul(.body))`, `.font(.ripul(.caption, weight: .semibold))` |
259	| `.font(.title2)` or `.font(.system(size: 18))` on an `Image` | `.font(.ripulIcon(.title2))`, `.font(.ripulIcon(size: 18))`: a symbol's size, never themed |
260	| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` on a `Text` | `.font(.ripul(size: 14, weight: .medium))` |
261	| `.caption.monospaced()`, `design: .monospaced` | `family: .code` |
262	| `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and the other hierarchy styles | `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))` |
263	| `Color.primary`, `Color.secondary` | `Color.ripul(.text)`, `Color.ripul(.textSecondary)` |
264	| `Color(.systemBackground)`, `UIColor.systemBackground`, `UIColor.label` | `Color.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.text)` |
265	| any other system colour, `Color(.systemGray5)` | the system form, `Color.ripul(system: .systemGray5)`: drawn as before, never themed |
266	| `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` | `.ripulProminentButtonStyle()`: its label is drawn in `onAccent` under a theme |
267	| with `--named`: `Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)` | `Color.ripul(.danger)`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.warning))` |
268	| with `--named`: `.white`, `.black`, `.yellow` and the other hues | the system form, `.ripul(system: .white)` |
269	
270	Then see what is left, and check the change:
271	
272	```bash
273	$RIPUL_THEME check <your source folder>     # every font and colour still written directly; exit 1 while any is left
274	$RIPUL_THEME lint                           # the working tree's diff: did each replacement keep its value?
275	```
276	
277	### What it leaves for you
278	
279	These need a person, because each is a decision or something the SDK does not
280	yet do for you.
281	
282	1. **Text with no colour of its own.** A `Text` that never had a colour is
283	   drawn in the system's label colour, not the theme's `text`. Give it
284	   `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))`. It must go on the text itself. On the
285	   root, or on a container, it changes what `.secondary` draws and recolours
286	   the labels of bordered and prominent buttons, links in a list and section
287	   headers, even under the default document (measured). Until the SDK finds
288	   a way, this is one line a text, and a new `Text` without it stays the
289	   system's colour silently.
290	2. **Lists.** A grouped list's ground, rows and separators stay the system's
291	   under a theme. Set them where you want them themed:
292	   `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` and `.background(.ripul(.surfaceSunken))`
293	   on the list, `.listRowBackground(Color.ripul(.surface))` on a section or a
294	   row (on the list itself it does nothing), `.listRowSeparatorTint(Color.ripul(.separator))`.
295	   Compare a screenshot under the default document afterwards: these have not
296	   been measured as identical by the SDK.
297	3. **Section headers and empty states.** `Section("Title")` becomes
298	   `Section(themed: "Title")`, a custom header `RipulSectionHeader { … }`, and
299	   `ContentUnavailableView("T", systemImage: "i")` becomes
300	   `ContentUnavailableView(themed: "T", systemImage: "i")`. Without these a
301	   header loses its weight under a themed family. Not inside a menu, a picker
302	   or a toolbar. A header takes the family and keeps the system's colour.
303	4. **A white or a blue that meant something.** `--named` writes the system
304	   form for white. Where the white sits on an accent fill, write
305	   `.ripul(.onAccent)`. Where a blue was the app's own colour and not a
306	   notice, write `.ripul(accentOr: .info)`: the accent once a theme names one.
307	5. **A colour of your own that is not one of the fifteen roles.** There is no
308	   place for it in the document yet. Keep it in your code, and if it should
309	   give way to the theme, read `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)` where it is
310	   used: `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent) ? myNavy : Color.ripul(.accent)`.
311	6. **Fonts the command could not place:** a fixed size on a view that is
312	   neither a `Text` nor an `Image`, a font held in a property
313	   (`var titleFont: Font { .caption }` becomes `.ripul(.caption)`), `.rounded`
314	   and `.serif` designs. `check` lists them.
315	7. **Colours that are data** (a category's colour, a chart's, a brand mark):
316	   mark the line `// theme-exempt: <reason>` and leave it.
317	
318	Never keep a token in a `static let`, a model or a cache: it would not follow
319	a change. Read the accessor where the value is used.
320	
321	### Keeping it themed
322	
323	Run `check` in your build, so a new direct font or colour fails it. As a Run
324	Script phase:
325	
326	```bash
327	"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" check "$SRCROOT/<your source folder>"
328	```
329	
330	An app part way through adds `--baseline "$SRCROOT/theme-baseline.json"`: the
331	first run writes today's counts there, later runs fail only when a count
332	rises, and `--baseline <file> --update` lowers it. A zero from `check` is not
333	proof: it reads lines, not types, and cannot see a bare `.orange` passed to an
334	unlabelled parameter.
335	
336	## 5. Light and dark
337	
338	Both come from the document: every palette entry that should differ is a
339	pair. A role left at its default follows the system in both. Look at every
340	screen in both; the pair for `onAccent` is the one most often wrong (white on
341	a pale dark-mode accent cannot be read).
342	
343	## 6. Switching while the app runs
344	
345	```swift
346	RipulTheme.select("brand-large")              // another document in the bundle; kept for later launches
347	RipulTheme.select(RipulTheme.systemThemeName) // the system look, kept as a choice
348	RipulTheme.select(nil)                        // forget the choice: back to the theme the root names
349	RipulTheme.selectedTheme                      // what is in use; read in a body, it follows a change
350	RipulTheme.bundledThemes                      // every theme document in the bundle, with its own name
351	
352	RipulThemePicker("Look")                      // a picker over all of the above, in one line
353	```
354	
355	Everything on screen repaints, with nothing written in your views.
356	`select` returns false and changes nothing when the document is missing or
357	refused.
358	
359	Two more ways in, for a developer and for tests, with no code:
360	
361	- **A launch argument:** `-ripul.theme.document <name>` (the choice is a
362	  `UserDefaults` key of that name).
363	- **A link, in a Debug build only:** `<your app's scheme>://theme?name=<name>`,
364	  with `name=system` for the system look. The root handles it. A store build
365	  ignores it; pass a URL to `RipulTheme.handleThemeLink(_:)` yourself if you
366	  want it there.
367	
368	A build that must show one theme whatever was chosen before installs with
369	`RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand", keepsChoice: false)`.
370	
371	What does not repaint by itself: UIKit code that read a colour or a font once
372	(read it again on `Notification.Name.ripulThemeDidChange`), and anything
373	computed outside a view's body and kept.
374	
375	## 7. The View Explorer names your tokens
376	
377	In a Debug build, selecting an element in the Ripul View Explorer lists the
378	theme tokens that style it, each with its value and whether it comes from the
379	document. The explorer reads that from a map written at build time. Add one
380	Run Script build phase holding one line:
381	
382	```bash
383	"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map
384	```
385	
386	In an XcodeGen `project.yml`:
387	
388	```yaml
389	    postCompileScripts:
390	      - name: Theme usage map
391	        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
392	        script: '"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map'
393	```
394	
395	It reads Xcode's own settings. It does nothing outside a Debug build, reads
396	the Swift files under the project's folder and the SDK's own screens, and
397	writes `ripul-theme-usage.json` into the app. It never fails a build. The
398	target needs `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = NO`, as any script that reads
399	the source does.
400	
401	An element is known by its identifier: `.uiKitIdentifier("screen.element")` or
402	`.accessibilityIdentifier(…)`. **Your own identifier modifier is followed.** If
403	the app names controls through a wrapper,
404	
405	```swift
406	func identified(_ name: String) -> some View { uiKitIdentifier(name) }
407	```
408	
409	then `.identified("stay.cottage")` is read like the two it wraps. Nothing
410	declares it; the build log says which wrappers it followed.
411	
412	To ask it directly: `$RIPUL_THEME usage-map --roots <folder> --no-sdk --stats`,
413	and `--explain <identifier>` for one element.
414	
415	## 8. Check that nothing moved
416	
417	Before the first edit, take screenshots of your screens in light and dark.
418	After the migration, with no document or an empty one, take them again and
419	compare them pixel for pixel. They should be the same. Where they are not, a
420	replacement was a judgement and not an identity: `lint` names most of those,
421	and the lists and text colours of step 4 are the usual rest.
422	
423	## What the system draws that a theme does not reach
424	
425	- **Reached, with no edit:** the accent on toolbar buttons, toggles, buttons,
426	  menus, progress bars, sliders, the selected tab and alert buttons; the text
427	  family on form rows, buttons, navigation titles (large and inline),
428	  segmented controls and tab bar labels.
429	- **Not reached:** the colour of a large navigation title and of a section
430	  header (the family is); alerts' text, menus, swipe action labels, a menu
431	  picker's value; a navigation title on Mac Catalyst.
432	- **Under a themed accent, things that had no colour take it:** toolbar
433	  buttons, a swipe action with no tint, a toggle's on colour.
434	- A document cannot ask for a font feature (lining figures, for one).
435	- On Mac Catalyst give every sized role a `catalystSize`, and a presented view
436	  needs a root inside it. See "Measured again, with Mac Catalyst" in
437	  [theming.md](theming.md).
438	
439	## Not built
440	
441	Each of these is a decision the SDK has not taken yet. Until it is, the cost
442	is yours, as described above.
443	
444	- **A theme layer on its own.** The theme is part of `RipulAgent`: an app that
445	  wants only the theme links the whole package, in Release too.
446	- **Your own roles in the document.** The fifteen are all there are.
447	- **Text colour without a line a text.**
448	- **Lists themed from the root.**
449	- **Editing a theme in the app.** A look is tried by loading a document.
450	- The widgets and other extensions of an app are not themed unless they link
451	  the package and install the theme themselves.
452	
453	## The API in one place
454	
455	```swift
456	.ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")          // the root of your own tree
457	.ripulThemeRoot()                        // any other root; reads Info.plist's RipulTheme
458	RipulTheme.install(theme:bundle:keepsChoice:)
459	RipulTheme.select(_:)   RipulTheme.selectedTheme   RipulTheme.bundledThemes
460	RipulTheme.handleThemeLink(_:)           RipulThemePicker(_:systemTitle:)
461	RipulTheme.adopt(documentData:)          // a document from anywhere else, such as your server
462	RipulTheme.resetToDefaults()
463	RipulTheme.color(.accent)   RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)
464	
465	Font.ripul(.body)   Font.ripul(.title, weight: .bold, family: .display)   Font.ripul(size: 14)
466	Font.ripulIcon(.title2)   Font.ripulIcon(size: 18)
467	.ripul(.textSecondary)            // as a style: foregroundStyle, fill, background, tint
468	Color.ripul(.danger)              // where a Color is required
469	.ripul(system: .systemGray5)      // a system colour, never themed
470	.ripul(accentOr: .info)
471	UIColor.ripul(.canvas)   UIFont.ripul(.caption)
472	.ripulTextStyle(.eyebrow)   .ripulProminentButtonStyle()   Section(themed:)   ContentUnavailableView(themed:)
473	```

# A theme for your app

This page is for an app that links the RipulAgent package and wants its own
fonts and colours to come from a theme: one JSON document, light and dark,
switchable while the app runs. It starts from "add the package" and is in the
order to do the work. The full contract, with every measurement behind a rule
here, is [theming.md](theming.md); you should not need it to get through this
page.

What you write, in total: one line at the root, a theme document, your font
files, one line of build setup for the View Explorer, and whatever the
migration command leaves for a person to decide. Everything else is the SDK's.

Where a thing is not built, this page says so. The list is at the end.

## The idea

Every token has a default that is the system value you write today.
`Font.ripul(.body)` is `Font.body`. `.ripul(.textSecondary)` is the system's
`.secondary` style. So moving a call site to a token changes no pixel, and an
app with no theme document looks exactly as it did. A document changes a token
only by naming it.

## With no change to your source

There are two ways to adopt the theme. The numbered steps below are the first:
you move your call sites to tokens, with a command that does most of it. This
section is the second: you change settings and add files, and no line of your
Swift changes. It is not in a release yet, and it has been measured on one
app.

What you do:

1. Add the package to the app target, as in step 1 below, without the root
   line.
2. Put your theme document and font files in the bundle (steps 2 and 3).
3. Switch on the package's build-tool plug-in, `RipulThemeRedirect`, for the app
   target: in Xcode, the target's Build Phases, "Run Build Tool Plug-ins", add
   it. In an XcodeGen `project.yml`:

   ```yaml
       buildToolPlugins:
         - plugin: RipulThemeRedirect
           package: RipulAgent
   ```
4. Allow the plug-in to run. Xcode asks once, "Trust & Enable". A command-line
   build passes `-skipPackagePluginValidation` to `xcodebuild`. (Not yet
   measured with a released package; a package added by local path needs
   neither.)

With one theme document in the bundle, that document is the app's theme. With
several, name one with the Info.plist key `RipulTheme`.

**How it works.** On every build the plug-in writes one Swift file into the
build folder, and Xcode compiles it into your app's own module. The file
declares SwiftUI's names again: `Font.body` and the other text styles,
`Font.system(size:)`, `Color.red`, `Color(.systemBackground)`,
`.foregroundStyle(.secondary)`, `WindowGroup`. Inside your module your
declaration of a name is chosen over SwiftUI's, so your existing `.font(.body)`
calls the generated one, which is one call into the SDK. With no theme each
returns exactly what SwiftUI's would have. Nothing is added to your repository.

**What it reaches,** with no edit:

| You wrote | It follows |
|---|---|
| `.font(.body)`, `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))`, `Font.body` | the type role of that name |
| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` | the text family at that size |
| `.system(.title, design: .serif)`, `.system(size: 22, design: .serif)`, and your own helper built on them | the display family, once a theme names one; the system's serif until then, with no second document |
| `design: .monospaced` | the code family |
| a font on an `Image` | nothing: a symbol keeps its system size |
| `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and the other hierarchy styles | the text roles |
| `Color(.systemBackground)`, `Color(.systemGroupedBackground)`, `Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground)` | `canvas`, `surfaceSunken`, `surface` |
| `Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)`, green, blue, gray | `danger`, `warning`, `success`, `info`, `neutral` |
| `WindowGroup { … }` | the theme root, with no line written: the accent, the body font for text with none, navigation titles, tab bar labels |
| identified elements | the View Explorer names their tokens (Debug builds), with no build phase |

**What it does not reach.** These stay the system's under a theme, where the
migration command or a line of yours would have reached them:

- text with no colour of its own, as in "What it leaves for you", 1;
- lists, section headers and empty states, as in 2 and 3;
- a prominent button's label (`onAccent`);
- a hierarchy style given to `fill`, `stroke` or `background`, and one passed
  through a variable of a generic type;
- a colour of your own (`Color("BrandNavy")`), and white and black;
- UIKit code (`UIFont.preferredFont`, `UIColor.label`);
- a `Label`'s icon, which takes its size from the label's font as before.

**What can go wrong.**

- A name you already declare (`extension Font { static var caption }`, a type
  called `WindowGroup`) is left out of the generated file and yours is used.
  The generator reads text, not types; one it misses is a compile error naming
  both places.
- A target is redirected only if the plug-in is on for it. A framework of your
  own needs it switched on too.
- `WindowGroup(for:)` and a UIKit app delegate are not covered: put
  `.ripulThemeRoot()` on the root yourself and add `RIPUL_THEME_NO_ROOT` to the
  target's Swift compilation conditions. `RIPUL_THEME_NO_STYLES` leaves
  `foregroundStyle` alone.
- A font or colour kept in a `static let` is read once and does not follow a
  switch while the app runs.
- The rule this rests on, that a module's own declaration is preferred to an
  imported one of the same name and type, is how the Swift compiler behaves
  (measured with Swift 6.4, Xcode 27.1, in Swift 5 and Swift 6 language
  modes). The language's documentation does not promise it.

The two ways mix: a file you have migrated calls the accessors directly, and
the rest goes through the generated file.

## 1. Add the package and name your theme

Pin the package (`https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk`), then put one
modifier on the root view of each window group:

```swift
import RipulAgent

WindowGroup {
    ContentView()
        .ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")     // brand.json in the app's bundle
}
```

That line is the whole setup. From it the SDK:

- finds `brand.json` in the bundle (at its top level, or in a folder named
  `Themes` or `Theme`), reads it and puts it in use before the first view is
  drawn;
- registers the font files the document names (step 3);
- keeps a choice made with `RipulTheme.select` between launches (step 6);
- falls back to `brand`, and then to the system look, when a document is
  missing, is not a theme document, or was written for a newer SDK. It logs
  which, with the prefix `[RipulTheme]`.

Two other ways to say the same thing, for an app that cannot put it on a root:

- the Info.plist key `RipulTheme` with the document's name, and a plain
  `.ripulThemeRoot()`;
- `RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand")` in the `App`'s `init` or the app
  delegate, for a UIKit app.

With no name at all, `.ripulThemeRoot()` leaves the app on the system look.

The root carries the accent (as the window's tint, so `.tint`,
`Color.accentColor` and control tints follow with no edit) and the theme's
body font for text with no font of its own. A sheet presented with
`.ripulSheet` has a root already. A presented `UIHostingController` of your
own needs `.ripulThemeRoot()` on its root view.

## 2. Write the document

Every key is optional, and an absent key is today's look. Start with
`{ "schema": 1, "name": "Brand" }`, which changes nothing, and add to it.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "name": "Brand",
  "palette": {
    "navy":  { "light": "#24386b", "dark": "#a9bdeb" },
    "paper": { "light": "#f7f3ec", "dark": "#0d1428" },
    "ink":   "#1c2540"
  },
  "roles": {
    "ripul.accent": "navy",
    "ripul.canvas": "paper",
    "ripul.text": "ink"
  },
  "typography": {
    "families": { "text": "Source Sans 3", "display": "Playfair Display", "code": "system-monospaced" },
    "roles": {
      "display": { "size": 34, "weight": "bold" },
      "eyebrow": { "tracking": 1.8, "uppercase": true }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`palette`** names your colours. A value is `#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA`,
  `system:<name>` (a live system colour such as `system:label`), or a light
  and dark pair of those. Light and dark are written here and nowhere else.
- **`roles`** gives each colour role a palette name, another role, or a colour
  string. The fifteen roles, each with the system colour it is by default:

  | Role | Default | For |
  |---|---|---|
  | `accent` | the app's tint | selection, links, primary buttons |
  | `onAccent` | white | text and icons on an accent fill |
  | `canvas` | `systemBackground` | the app's background |
  | `surface` | `secondarySystemGroupedBackground` | cards and grouped rows |
  | `surfaceSunken` | `systemGroupedBackground` | the ground behind cards |
  | `text`, `textSecondary`, `textTertiary`, `textQuaternary` | `.primary` to `.quaternary` | text |
  | `separator` | `separator` | hairlines |
  | `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `neutral` | green, orange, red, blue, grey | state |

  The set is closed: a document cannot add a role (see the end).
- **`typography.families`** names the three families, `text`, `display` and
  `code`. Each is a font family you bundle, or one of `system`,
  `system-serif`, `system-rounded`, `system-monospaced`.
- **`typography.roles`** changes a type role: `size`, `weight`, `family`,
  `relativeTo`, `tracking`, `uppercase`, `catalystSize`. The roles are the
  eleven system text styles by their own names, plus `display` (a title in
  the display family), `eyebrow` and `code`.

**A serif that is yours already.** `"display": "system-serif"` draws what
`.font(.system(.title, design: .serif))` draws (compared pixel for pixel in a
host's trial on iOS 27, at the default text size). There is no accessor for
`design: .serif` itself. So an app whose headings are serif today keeps them
by naming `system-serif` as its display family and writing
`.font(.ripul(.title, family: .display))` at those headings. Its document is
then not empty, and the plain system look (`RipulTheme.systemThemeName`) is
not the look it had.

Check a dark value against its background yourself: nothing checks contrast.

## 3. Fonts

Put the font files in the app's bundle, at its top level or in a folder named
`Fonts`. Do nothing else. When a document names a family that is not the
system's, the SDK reads the bundled `.ttf`, `.otf` and `.ttc` files and
registers those that hold a face of that family. No `UIAppFonts` entry and no
registration call.

- The name in the document is the font's family name ("Source Sans 3"), not
  its file name.
- A variable font takes weights; a family with one weight draws that weight
  whatever is asked, and the system does not fake a bold.
- Ship each font's licence beside it. That is yours to get right.

## 4. Move the call sites: one command

The package brings its tools. In an Xcode project they are in the package
checkout, under the build's DerivedData:

```bash
# with -derivedDataPath build
RIPUL_THEME=build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
# with Xcode's default DerivedData
RIPUL_THEME=$(ls -d ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/<Project>-*/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme | head -1)
# in a Swift package
RIPUL_THEME=.build/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
```

They need `python3` and nothing else.

```bash
$RIPUL_THEME migrate --dry-run --named <your source folder>   # what would change
$RIPUL_THEME migrate --named <your source folder>             # change it
```

Every rewrite is to the token whose default is the value it replaces, so
nothing moves on screen. It rewrites:

| You wrote | It writes |
|---|---|
| `.font(.body)`, `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))` | `.font(.ripul(.body))`, `.font(.ripul(.caption, weight: .semibold))` |
| `.font(.title2)` or `.font(.system(size: 18))` on an `Image` | `.font(.ripulIcon(.title2))`, `.font(.ripulIcon(size: 18))`: a symbol's size, never themed |
| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` on a `Text` | `.font(.ripul(size: 14, weight: .medium))` |
| `.caption.monospaced()`, `design: .monospaced` | `family: .code` |
| `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and the other hierarchy styles | `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))` |
| `Color.primary`, `Color.secondary` | `Color.ripul(.text)`, `Color.ripul(.textSecondary)` |
| `Color(.systemBackground)`, `UIColor.systemBackground`, `UIColor.label` | `Color.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.text)` |
| any other system colour, `Color(.systemGray5)` | the system form, `Color.ripul(system: .systemGray5)`: drawn as before, never themed |
| `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` | `.ripulProminentButtonStyle()`: its label is drawn in `onAccent` under a theme |
| with `--named`: `Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)` | `Color.ripul(.danger)`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.warning))` |
| with `--named`: `.white`, `.black`, `.yellow` and the other hues | the system form, `.ripul(system: .white)` |

Then see what is left, and check the change:

```bash
$RIPUL_THEME check <your source folder>     # every font and colour still written directly; exit 1 while any is left
$RIPUL_THEME lint                           # the working tree's diff: did each replacement keep its value?
```

### What it leaves for you

These need a person, because each is a decision or something the SDK does not
yet do for you.

1. **Text with no colour of its own.** A `Text` that never had a colour is
   drawn in the system's label colour, not the theme's `text`. Give it
   `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))`. It must go on the text itself. On the
   root, or on a container, it changes what `.secondary` draws and recolours
   the labels of bordered and prominent buttons, links in a list and section
   headers, even under the default document (measured). Until the SDK finds
   a way, this is one line a text, and a new `Text` without it stays the
   system's colour silently.
2. **Lists.** A grouped list's ground, rows and separators stay the system's
   under a theme. Set them where you want them themed:
   `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` and `.background(.ripul(.surfaceSunken))`
   on the list, `.listRowBackground(Color.ripul(.surface))` on a section or a
   row (on the list itself it does nothing), `.listRowSeparatorTint(Color.ripul(.separator))`.
   Compare a screenshot under the default document afterwards: these have not
   been measured as identical by the SDK.
3. **Section headers and empty states.** `Section("Title")` becomes
   `Section(themed: "Title")`, a custom header `RipulSectionHeader { … }`, and
   `ContentUnavailableView("T", systemImage: "i")` becomes
   `ContentUnavailableView(themed: "T", systemImage: "i")`. Without these a
   header loses its weight under a themed family. Not inside a menu, a picker
   or a toolbar. A header takes the family and keeps the system's colour.
4. **A white or a blue that meant something.** `--named` writes the system
   form for white. Where the white sits on an accent fill, write
   `.ripul(.onAccent)`. Where a blue was the app's own colour and not a
   notice, write `.ripul(accentOr: .info)`: the accent once a theme names one.
5. **A colour of your own that is not one of the fifteen roles.** There is no
   place for it in the document yet. Keep it in your code, and if it should
   give way to the theme, read `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)` where it is
   used: `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent) ? myNavy : Color.ripul(.accent)`.
6. **Fonts the command could not place:** a fixed size on a view that is
   neither a `Text` nor an `Image`, a font held in a property
   (`var titleFont: Font { .caption }` becomes `.ripul(.caption)`), `.rounded`
   and `.serif` designs. `check` lists them.
7. **Colours that are data** (a category's colour, a chart's, a brand mark):
   mark the line `// theme-exempt: <reason>` and leave it.

Never keep a token in a `static let`, a model or a cache: it would not follow
a change. Read the accessor where the value is used.

### Keeping it themed

Run `check` in your build, so a new direct font or colour fails it. As a Run
Script phase:

```bash
"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" check "$SRCROOT/<your source folder>"
```

An app part way through adds `--baseline "$SRCROOT/theme-baseline.json"`: the
first run writes today's counts there, later runs fail only when a count
rises, and `--baseline <file> --update` lowers it. A zero from `check` is not
proof: it reads lines, not types, and cannot see a bare `.orange` passed to an
unlabelled parameter.

## 5. Light and dark

Both come from the document: every palette entry that should differ is a
pair. A role left at its default follows the system in both. Look at every
screen in both; the pair for `onAccent` is the one most often wrong (white on
a pale dark-mode accent cannot be read).

## 6. Switching while the app runs

```swift
RipulTheme.select("brand-large")              // another document in the bundle; kept for later launches
RipulTheme.select(RipulTheme.systemThemeName) // the system look, kept as a choice
RipulTheme.select(nil)                        // forget the choice: back to the theme the root names
RipulTheme.selectedTheme                      // what is in use; read in a body, it follows a change
RipulTheme.bundledThemes                      // every theme document in the bundle, with its own name

RipulThemePicker("Look")                      // a picker over all of the above, in one line
```

Everything on screen repaints, with nothing written in your views.
`select` returns false and changes nothing when the document is missing or
refused.

Two more ways in, for a developer and for tests, with no code:

- **A launch argument:** `-ripul.theme.document <name>` (the choice is a
  `UserDefaults` key of that name).
- **A link, in a Debug build only:** `<your app's scheme>://theme?name=<name>`,
  with `name=system` for the system look. The root handles it. A store build
  ignores it; pass a URL to `RipulTheme.handleThemeLink(_:)` yourself if you
  want it there.

A build that must show one theme whatever was chosen before installs with
`RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand", keepsChoice: false)`.

What does not repaint by itself: UIKit code that read a colour or a font once
(read it again on `Notification.Name.ripulThemeDidChange`), and anything
computed outside a view's body and kept.

## 7. The View Explorer names your tokens

In a Debug build, selecting an element in the Ripul View Explorer lists the
theme tokens that style it, each with its value and whether it comes from the
document. The explorer reads that from a map written at build time. Add one
Run Script build phase holding one line:

```bash
"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map
```

In an XcodeGen `project.yml`:

```yaml
    postCompileScripts:
      - name: Theme usage map
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: '"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map'
```

It reads Xcode's own settings. It does nothing outside a Debug build, reads
the Swift files under the project's folder and the SDK's own screens, and
writes `ripul-theme-usage.json` into the app. It never fails a build. The
target needs `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = NO`, as any script that reads
the source does.

An element is known by its identifier: `.uiKitIdentifier("screen.element")` or
`.accessibilityIdentifier(…)`. **Your own identifier modifier is followed.** If
the app names controls through a wrapper,

```swift
func identified(_ name: String) -> some View { uiKitIdentifier(name) }
```

then `.identified("stay.cottage")` is read like the two it wraps. Nothing
declares it; the build log says which wrappers it followed.

To ask it directly: `$RIPUL_THEME usage-map --roots <folder> --no-sdk --stats`,
and `--explain <identifier>` for one element.

## 8. Check that nothing moved

Before the first edit, take screenshots of your screens in light and dark.
After the migration, with no document or an empty one, take them again and
compare them pixel for pixel. They should be the same. Where they are not, a
replacement was a judgement and not an identity: `lint` names most of those,
and the lists and text colours of step 4 are the usual rest.

## What the system draws that a theme does not reach

- **Reached, with no edit:** the accent on toolbar buttons, toggles, buttons,
  menus, progress bars, sliders, the selected tab and alert buttons; the text
  family on form rows, buttons, navigation titles (large and inline),
  segmented controls and tab bar labels.
- **Not reached:** the colour of a large navigation title and of a section
  header (the family is); alerts' text, menus, swipe action labels, a menu
  picker's value; a navigation title on Mac Catalyst.
- **Under a themed accent, things that had no colour take it:** toolbar
  buttons, a swipe action with no tint, a toggle's on colour.
- A document cannot ask for a font feature (lining figures, for one).
- On Mac Catalyst give every sized role a `catalystSize`, and a presented view
  needs a root inside it. See "Measured again, with Mac Catalyst" in
  [theming.md](theming.md).

## Not built

Each of these is a decision the SDK has not taken yet. Until it is, the cost
is yours, as described above.

- **A theme layer on its own.** The theme is part of `RipulAgent`: an app that
  wants only the theme links the whole package, in Release too.
- **Your own roles in the document.** The fifteen are all there are.
- **Text colour without a line a text.**
- **Lists themed from the root.**
- **Editing a theme in the app.** A look is tried by loading a document.
- The widgets and other extensions of an app are not themed unless they link
  the package and install the theme themselves.

## The API in one place

```swift
.ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")          // the root of your own tree
.ripulThemeRoot()                        // any other root; reads Info.plist's RipulTheme
RipulTheme.install(theme:bundle:keepsChoice:)
RipulTheme.select(_:)   RipulTheme.selectedTheme   RipulTheme.bundledThemes
RipulTheme.handleThemeLink(_:)           RipulThemePicker(_:systemTitle:)
RipulTheme.adopt(documentData:)          // a document from anywhere else, such as your server
RipulTheme.resetToDefaults()
RipulTheme.color(.accent)   RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)

Font.ripul(.body)   Font.ripul(.title, weight: .bold, family: .display)   Font.ripul(size: 14)
Font.ripulIcon(.title2)   Font.ripulIcon(size: 18)
.ripul(.textSecondary)            // as a style: foregroundStyle, fill, background, tint
Color.ripul(.danger)              // where a Color is required
.ripul(system: .systemGray5)      // a system colour, never themed
.ripul(accentOr: .info)
UIColor.ripul(.canvas)   UIFont.ripul(.caption)
.ripulTextStyle(.eyebrow)   .ripulProminentButtonStyle()   Section(themed:)   ContentUnavailableView(themed:)
```

1	# Ripul inside your own iOS app (the RipulAgent SDK)
2	
3	RipulAgent is a Swift package that puts Ripul into an iOS app. This guide applies when the repository you are working in is an iOS app that imports `RipulAgent`, or is about to. It covers what the app has to do so that agents can work with it.
4	
5	## What embedding gives the app
6
