# Ripul inside your own iOS app (the RipulAgent SDK)

RipulAgent is a Swift package that puts Ripul into an iOS app. This guide applies when the repository you are working in is an iOS app that imports `RipulAgent`, or is about to. It covers what the app has to do so that agents can work with it.

## What embedding gives the app

- **An agent for the app's users.** `AgentView(configuration:registry:)` is a chat panel. The agent in it can call the functions the app chooses to expose as native tools.
- **A console for the app's developers.** `RipulAgentConsole` (or the floating `RipulDevAssistantOverlay`) lets a developer sign in to their own Ripul account inside the app and reach the coding agents on their Mac. While it is open, those agents get tools that act on this app: `device_inspect_screen`, `device_tap_element`, `device_type_text`, `device_scroll_element`, `device_wait_for_element`, `device_screen_frame`, `device_touch`, `device_console_logs` and others.
- **The View Explorer** (`RipulViewExplorer.present()`): a person points at an element on screen and attaches it to a chat, so "this button" reaches the agent with its identifier, type, owning view controller and bounds.

## Adding and pinning the package

Add `https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk` through Swift Package Manager and `import RipulAgent`. The package needs iOS 17 or macOS 14; the console and overlay need iOS 26. Releases are tags of the form `v0.7.169`, and the app's `Package.resolved` records the one in use. Read it before assuming the app has a given feature.

A fix in the SDK reaches the app in three steps: a new version is tagged in the public repository, the app's pin is moved to it, and the app is rebuilt and installed. Until all three have happened the running app has the old code. The View Explorer shows the SDK version that is running; trust that over the pin when they disagree.

## Exposing one of the app's functions as a tool

Write a struct that conforms to `NativeTool`: a snake_case `name`, a `description` the model reads, an `inputSchema` built with `ToolSchema.object(.string(…, required: true), .bool(…), …)`, and `execute(args:)`, which calls the app's existing code and returns a dictionary. Read arguments with the helpers `string(_:from:)`, `optionalString`, `date`, `optionalDate` and `bool`, which throw a readable error when an argument is missing.

Register tools on one `RipulToolRegistry` for the whole app:

```swift
let registry = RipulToolRegistry()
registry.register([CreateEventTool()], audience: .endUser)
AgentView(configuration: config, registry: registry)
```

A tool registered after the agent has connected is announced straight away.

- The model sees what `execute` throws. Throw `ToolError.invalidArgs("what failed and what to check")`, not a raw system error.
- `timeout` is 30 seconds by default. Set it to `0` for a tool that waits for a person.
- A name starting `pick_` marks an interactive picker; return `name` or `value` so the chat can show what was chosen.

## Tools for users and tools for developers

Each tool is registered under an audience, and each `AgentBridge` serves one audience, fixed when it is created (`AgentBridge(registry:audience:)`, default `.endUser`).

- `.endUser` tools appear in the app's own `AgentView`.
- `.developer` tools appear only in the console and overlay, which create a `.developer` bridge themselves.
- The SDK's own inspection and log tools can never reach an `.endUser` bridge, and there is no override. `.ripulDevTools(bridge:)` on an end-user bridge still shows a person the log viewer, but gives the agent nothing.
- The console can borrow the end-user tools for a testing session (`setEndUserTesting(true)`). They run against real app state.

Pass the same registry instance to `AgentView` and to the console's `RipulSessionsConfiguration`. Keep the console behind the app's own developer-only switch.

## Making screens identifiable

Agents address elements by accessibility identifier, visible text, role and class. Identifiers are the only stable one.

- UIKit: set `accessibilityIdentifier` on each control.
- SwiftUI: use `.uiKitIdentifier("screen.element")`, which sets the accessibility identifier and also marks the element's exact frame.
- Give each control its own identifier. An identifier on a container is inherited by what is inside it, and a tap by that identifier becomes ambiguous.
- To say what a component means, add `.ripulAIContext(.init(id:label:value:role:))`, or set `view.ripulAIContext` in UIKit and update it when the value changes.

## Giving the app a theme

The package also carries a theme system for the app's own screens: fonts and colours from one JSON document, light and dark, switchable while the app runs. The page for it is `docs/theming-for-hosts.md` in the package checkout; follow it in the order it gives.

- Setup is one line at the root, `.ripulThemeRoot(theme: "<document name>")`. The SDK finds the document in the bundle, registers the font files it names, keeps a choice between launches and falls back when a document is missing.
- The tools are in the package's `tools/` folder: `ripul-theme migrate` rewrites call sites to theme tokens without changing a pixel, `ripul-theme check` lists what is left, and `ripul-theme usage-map`, as one Run Script line, lets the View Explorer name the tokens of a selected element. Do not write your own versions.
- A default theme changes nothing on screen. Prove it with screenshots before and after.

## What is kept private

When a person attaches Current screen or Selected element to a message, nothing is captured until they choose it and review a preview. To leave a region out, use `.ripulAIContextExcluded()` in SwiftUI, `view.ripulAIContext = .excluded` in UIKit, or the attribute `data-ripul-context-excluded` on a web element. Excluded regions are removed from the description and painted out of the screenshot.

Fields are not excluded automatically, secure fields included: mark every field that holds something private.

## Mistakes that are real today

- **The package README shows `bridge.register(…)` and `AgentView(configuration:tools:)`.** Neither exists. Registration is on the registry, as above.
- **Two tools with the same name stop the app at launch**, even under different audiences. A leading `host_`, `device_` or `web_tool_` is ignored when names are compared.
- **`setTools(_:audience:)` replaces every tool of that audience.** Use it from one place only, or use `register`.
- **Exclusion marks apply only to what a person attaches.** `device_inspect_screen` and `device_screen_frame` do not honour them (inspection withholds only a secure field's text), so they are no boundary against a developer's agent.
- **`device_touch` works in Debug builds of the app only.** In a Release build use `device_tap_element`.
- **The app must be open and in the foreground**, with the developer signed in to the console, or the `device_…` tools get no answer.

---
name: theme-one-system-going-forward
description: "Peter's decision of 11 Oct 2026: the SDK's new base theme layer (RipulTheme, accessors) is the theme system going forward; the older RipulThemeEngine is legacy that WAC carries; build nothing new on it"
metadata:
  type: project
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
  scope_also: repo:wac-ios
---

After the theme migration of 10 October 2026 the SDK held two theme systems: the older engine lifted from WAC (`RipulThemeEngine`: a host registers its own vocabulary, UIKit colour tagging, the editing and publishing screens) and the new base layer built for Ripul's SwiftUI app (`RipulTheme` in `ThemeCore/`: fixed roles, accessors, light and dark, fonts, live repaint, the usage map and `RipulBaseTokenProvider`). I told Peter this was the main thing standing between the theme system and being a real SDK value. His decision, 11 October 2026, in the chat "Design alignment": "I don't mind the WAC app carrying a legacy for a while as long as moving forward it is clean."

**Why:** he wants the theme system to be a key value of the SDK. Applying the older engine to our own app was hard because it fits the UIKit, light-only app it came from, so the forward path has to be the layer that fits SwiftUI apps, kept free of the old one.

**How to apply:**
- Build every new theme feature on the base layer only: editing, the explorer, publishing a base document, migration tools.
- Treat `RipulThemeEngine`, its vocabulary registration and its editor screens (`Theme*.swift` outside `ThemeCore/`) as legacy: fixes only, no features, no new dependents. Do not extend the old editor to edit base roles; write the base layer's editor new, reusing only what is already general (hosting, the publish review).
- No bridges from new to old: nothing of the base layer goes into a host's own palette or roles maps, and the reserved `ripul` key in a host document stays unread.
- WAC stays on the legacy engine unchanged until it is moved as its own piece of work. Do not break it, and do not migrate it as a side effect.
- Still open and not built (my reading of what "clean" needs, not his words): a host adding its own roles to the base layer, and shipping the rewrite script, lint, check and usage map with the SDK and without Ripul's file layout.

The decision is recorded as Decision 9 in `docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md`. See [[theme-framework-sdk-lift]] for how the older engine got into the SDK, and `ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md` for the base layer's contract.
---
name: Generalizable native theme strategies
description: Automatic text theming must use reusable SDK strategies across apps, with app-wide integration and no WAC-specific element rules
type: feedback
metadata:
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
---

Peter explicitly confirmed on 2026-09-10 that automatic text theming must be a series of generalizable strategies that work across many apps, not an implementation specific to WAC. The selected WAC HomeCell subtitle is a proving example, not an SDK special case.

Keep the developer contract to one app-wide SDK/theme hook (or a central screen/component adapter where runtime identity is otherwise unavailable). Do not require every label/button to register itself or look up replacement copy. Prefer existing stable accessibility identifiers, stored view properties/outlets, and reusable-row semantic context. Detect ambiguous targeting and explain the missing central integration instead of matching by current text, coordinates, index paths, or hard-coded host class/property names. Tests should exercise unrelated model/view types so portability is demonstrated.
---
name: feedback_sdk_release_from_clean_worktree
description: "Publish an SDK tag from a detached worktree at HEAD when the monorepo SDK tree is dirty with another agent's WIP — never ALLOW_DIRTY=1, never stash"
metadata:
  type: feedback
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
---

`ripul-ios-sdk/scripts/release-public.sh` refuses a dirty `Sources`/`Package.swift`
tree because rsync copies the WORKING TREE, so another agent's in-flight edits ride
into the public tag (this already shipped an in-flight AgentScreen port as v0.4.14).
In this repo the SDK tree is dirty with foreign work most of the time.

**Do not** reach for `ALLOW_DIRTY=1`, and do not stash. Publish from a clean
detached worktree at the commit you actually want:

```bash
# 1. Stamp + commit the new version in MAIN first — the script's own stamp step
#    would commit to the worktree's detached HEAD and be lost.
sed -i '' 's/^let ripulSDKVersion = ".*"$/let ripulSDKVersion = "X.Y.Z"/' \
  ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/ViewInspectorOverlay.swift
git commit -m "chore(sdk): stamp ripulSDKVersion X.Y.Z" && git push

# 2. Release from a clean checkout of that commit.
git worktree add --detach /tmp/ripul-sdk-release-X.Y.Z HEAD
cd /tmp/ripul-sdk-release-X.Y.Z/ripul-ios-sdk && bash scripts/release-public.sh X.Y.Z --push
cd - && git worktree remove /tmp/ripul-sdk-release-X.Y.Z --force   # ALWAYS remove it
```

Verify the tag got what you meant, in the public clone (`~/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk`):
`git show vX.Y.Z --name-only` lists your files, and `git show vX.Y.Z:<foreign file>`
fails.

**Why:** it gives the user their change on a public tag without touching, shipping,
or asking about another agent's uncommitted work — the only option that satisfies
both CLAUDE.md rule 4 (never silently work around a foreign dirty tree) and the
release script's concurrency guard. **How to apply:** any "release the SDK" /
"ship WAC against the new SDK" ask where `git status` shows SDK edits you did not
make. `/tmp` already holds ~35 stale ripul worktrees — remove yours when done.
See [[project_wac_ota_deploy_flow]], [[feedback_wac_ship_default_target]].
---
name: feedback_sdk_release_after_all_edits
description: Cut the ripul-ios-sdk tag only AFTER every SDK edit for the change is done — a late edit strands WAC on a tag without it
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3a38c80e-bb09-43b5-98aa-662a86f4f64a
  modified: 2026-07-28T08:39:43.264Z
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
  scope_also: repo:wac-ios
---

`release-public.sh vX.Y.Z --push` snapshots the SDK working tree at that moment. Any SDK
edit made *after* the tag — even one that builds clean locally — is NOT in the tag WAC
pins, so WAC fails with `cannot find type 'X' in scope` even though the symbol exists in
the monorepo.

Hit 2026-07-28: released 0.5.40, then made `RipulTokenNode`/`RipulTokenNodeScreen` public
so WAC's scope trees could share the builder. Local SDK build passed (it compiles the
monorepo copy); WAC's build failed against the 0.5.40 tag. Cost a full WAC rebuild cycle.

**Why:** the local `swift build`/`xcodebuild` of the SDK proves nothing about what WAC
sees — WAC resolves the PUBLIC repo at the pinned tag, a separate checkout.

**How to apply:** finish every SDK edit for the change (including access-level widening
discovered while wiring the host) → build SDK → *then* release + bump the pin. If a host
build fails on a missing SDK symbol, check `git log v<pinned>..HEAD -- ripul-ios-sdk/`
before debugging the host. See [[project_wac_consumes_sdk_as_pinned_public_package]].

# Claude

## Project Overview

This is a **web application** that provides AI-powered workflow automation and visualization capabilities.

### Architecture

| Component | Status | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| **Web Application** | Active | Primary codebase - React-based workflow platform |
| **Lightweight Extension** | Active | Minimal Chrome extension that augments the web app with browser-specific features |
| **Full Extension** | Legacy | Deprecated full Chrome extension - not actively maintained |

### Development Focus
- **DO**: Develop features in the web application
- **DO**: Keep the lightweight extension minimal (only browser API features)
- **DON'T**: Add new features to the legacy full extension
- **DON'T**: Frame this project as "a Chrome extension" - it's a web application

### Documentation

| Document | Contents |
|----------|----------|
| **[PROJECT-STRUCTURE.md](./docs/PROJECT-STRUCTURE.md)** | Cross-repo guide: chrome-extension, ripul-native-app, ripul-ios-sdk — structure, build commands, message protocol, and cross-repo dependencies |
| **[GLOSSARY.md](./GLOSSARY.md)** | Core domain terms (Tool, Prompt, PromptTool, MCP, etc.) |
| **[EXTENSION-ARCHITECTURE.md](./EXTENSION-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | Extension history, capabilities, and communication protocol |
| **[NATIVE-BRIDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md](./docs/NATIVE-BRIDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | Native iOS ↔ web communication: JS callables (preferred) vs message protocol (legacy) |
| **[DOM-MINIMIZATION-ARCHITECTURE.md](./docs/DOM-MINIMIZATION-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | DOM reduction pipeline, n-tagging strategy, and the semantic-minimization ↔ rehydration bridge |
| **[Tools System Architecture](./docs/architecture/toolsSystemArchitecture.md)** | End-to-end guide: tool definitions → interceptor chain → handler resolution → CLI bridge → native tools. Links to all subsystem docs |
| **[MCP Tool Surfaces](./docs/architecture/mcpToolSurfaces.md)** | Cross-package map of every MCP/tool surface — why each runtime context and surface exists, consumers, transports, name prefixes, and which gates are security vs curation. Start here for anything spanning CLI/native/device/extension tools |
| **[paneLatching.md](./docs/architecture/paneLatching.md)** | Three-pass plan for latching a mirror to an app's own UI element instead of a fixed crop — what each toolkit actually exposes, and why the manifest comes last |
| **[multiViewerMirroring.md](./docs/architecture/multiViewerMirroring.md)** | Multi-viewer window mirroring (implemented 2026-08-27): per-window captures with subscriber sets, one controller driving with loud refusal for the rest, shared crop, controller-only direct transport — plus the plan it grew from and the accepted gaps |
| **[webMcpAutoToolCreation.md](./docs/architecture/webMcpAutoToolCreation.md)** | How agent page interactions automatically become reusable WebMCP tools |
| **[databaseArchitecture.md](./docs/architecture/databaseArchitecture.md)** | D1 database layer: D1Store base class, scoping model, migrations, shared types, and data access patterns |
| **[rbacArchitecture.md](./docs/architecture/rbacArchitecture.md)** | RBAC enforcement: AuthContext flow, access guard policies, team authorization, handler categories |
| **[themingGuide.md](./docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md)** | Theme system: how to use MUI tokens, `alpha()`, `useThemeColors()`, and anti-patterns to avoid |
| **[iOS Styling Guide](../ripul-native-app/docs/ios-styling-guide.md)** | Native iOS glass effects: prefer `.clear` over `.regular`, vibrancy, and glass modifier library |

---

## Code Quality Rules

### After Code Changes
1. **Always run TypeScript compilation check** after making any code changes:
   ```bash
   npx tsgo --noEmit
   ```
2. Fix any TypeScript errors before considering the task complete
3. If there are build errors, investigate and resolve them immediately

### Testing
- Run relevant test commands if they exist
- Verify changes don't break existing functionality

---

## Technical Guidelines

### React Components
- Ensure proper TypeScript types for all components
- Check that all imports are correctly specified
- Verify that component props match their interfaces

### Workflow System
- The workflow graph uses React Flow for visualization
- Panels can appear in both chat log and workflow graph
- Messages with `.toolStatus` suffix appear in the workflow graph
- Base method names (without `.toolStatus`) create UI panels

### Styling
- Use Material-UI (MUI) components and styling system where possible
- Override styles with `!important` when necessary to override inline styles
- Consider both light and dark themes when making UI changes
- **Use MUI theme tokens** (`'text.primary'`, `'action.hover'`, `'divider'`) instead of hardcoded rgba values
- **Never pass string tokens to `alpha()`** — resolve via `theme.palette.X.main` first
- **Use `useThemeColors()` hook** for common color calculations instead of manual `alpha()` calls
- **Colours and typefaces come from the theme, never from a literal**: no hex or `rgba(` colour and no `fontFamily` string at a call site. Use a palette token, `alpha()` of a palette value, a named colour (`useNamedColours()`) or a family (`useFontFamilies()`). Mark a colour that is data `// theme-exempt: <reason>`
- **Run the literals check before pushing**: `node scripts/check-theme-literals.mjs --strict <paths>`. Every build runs it, and it fails the build for a literal in a finished directory (`src/logging/components/chat/`, `src/logging/panels/`)
- See [themingGuide.md](./docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md) for full details and anti-patterns

### Settings Panels
- For settings dialogs with toggles that reveal more options, follow the established patterns
- See [docs/features/ui/settingsPanelPatterns.md](docs/features/ui/settingsPanelPatterns.md)

### UI Element Traceability
- Add `data-ui` attribute to every rendered element in React components
- Format: `ComponentName.section.element` (e.g., `LLMRequestPanel.header.message`)
- Use static values only - never include runtime data (tool names, IDs, status values, etc.)
- Purpose: Enable tracing from DOM back to source code that created it
- Duplicates are acceptable when the same component is reused
- **MUI compound components** (`TextField`, `Autocomplete`, `Slider`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, etc.) render multiple DOM layers — `data-ui` on the component prop lands on the outer wrapper `div`, not the interactive `<input>`. For any MUI component wrapping a focusable element, also pass `data-ui` through `slotProps`:
  ```tsx
  // ❌ data-ui only reaches the wrapper div
  <TextField data-ui="Foo.bar" />

  // ✅ data-ui also reaches the <input>
  <TextField
    data-ui="Foo.bar"
    slotProps={{ htmlInput: { 'data-ui': 'Foo.bar' } }}
  />
  ```

---

## Deployment & Cloudflare Pages

### CRITICAL: `_routes.json`
- **Location:** `chrome-extension/_routes.json` (copied to `public/` during build)
- **Purpose:** Tells Cloudflare Pages which routes go through Functions vs static files
- `"include"` = routes handled by the Pages Function (`functions/api/[[path]].ts`)
- Everything NOT included is served as static files from `public/`
- **DO NOT** add broad patterns like `"include": ["/*"]` — this routes JS chunks through Functions, which returns `index.html` instead of JavaScript, breaking the entire app
- Current correct config: `/api/*`, the two `/.well-known/` app-link files, `/dl/*` (unlisted downloads from R2, `functions/dl/[[path]].ts`) and `/mac` with `/mac/*` (the address for installing the Mac apps, `functions/mac.ts` and `functions/mac/[product].ts`) — each a narrow path with its own Function. Also the iPhone install pages, each `<base>` with `<base>/*`: `/ios` with the two fixed manifests `/manifest.plist` and `/manifest-alice.plist` (Ripul, `functions/ios.ts`) and `/sandsend` (Sandsend Retreats, `functions/sandsend.ts`), both built on `functions/installPage.ts`

### Chunk Naming & CDN Caching
- Production builds use `chunk-BUILDVERSION-HASH.js` naming (set in `scripts/build.mjs`)
- The build version ensures every deploy produces unique URLs, preventing CDN cache poisoning
- **DO NOT** remove the build version from `chunkNames` — without it, chunks with unchanged content get the same hash across builds, and a single CDN cache poisoning incident becomes permanent
- The `_headers` file sets `/js/*` to `max-age=31536000, immutable` — if the CDN ever caches a wrong response for a chunk URL, it's stuck for a year unless the URL changes

### Incident Reference (2026-03-29)
Missing `_routes.json` in deploys caused Cloudflare to serve `index.html` for JS chunk requests. The immutable cache header then locked the wrong response into the CDN. Fixed by deploying `_routes.json` and adding build version to chunk names.

---

## Development Workflow

1. Understand the requirement
2. Investigate the codebase
3. Make the necessary changes
4. **Run `npx tsgo --noEmit` to check for TypeScript errors**
5. Fix any build errors
6. Test the functionality if possible
7. Document the changes made

---

## Common Commands

```bash
# Check TypeScript compilation
npx tsgo --noEmit

# Build the project
npm run build

# Run tests (if available)
npm test
```

---

## File Structure

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `/src/logging/reactflow/` | Workflow graph components |
| `/src/logging/panels/` | UI panel providers |
| `/src/LLM/Tools/` | Tool handlers for AI interactions |
| `/public/solutions/` | Configuration files for workflows |

---

## Important Patterns

### Dual Message System
Some tools send two messages:
1. **With `.toolStatus` suffix** - for workflow tracking
2. **Without suffix** - for UI panel display

This allows tool authors to control where panels appear.

### Panel Providers
- React-based providers extend `BaseLogPanelProviderReact`
- Providers must implement `canHandle()` and `createLogPanel()`
- Panels can check for methods with or without `.toolStatus` suffix

### API Client & Authentication

**IMPORTANT**: All authenticated API calls must flow through the standard hooks and providers. Never create `ApiClient` instances directly with custom auth.

#### Approved Patterns

**In React components** - Use the hooks:
```typescript
// For LLM Proxy endpoints
const client = useLlmProxyClient();
if (client) {
  await client.get('/v1/endpoint');
}

// For services
const service = useLlmProxyService();
if (service) {
  await service.fetchQuota();
}
```

**Outside React** (only when token is already obtained):
```typescript
// Token already obtained and passed as parameter - OK
const authProvider = new StaticTokenAuthProvider(token);
const client = new ApiClient({ baseUrl, authProvider });
```

#### FORBIDDEN Patterns

**Never** create `ApiClient` with `ClerkAuthProvider` or dynamic token fetching outside the approved hooks:
```typescript
// ❌ WRONG - creates race conditions with token availability
const client = new ApiClient({
  baseUrl: LLM_PROXY_URL,
  authProvider: new ClerkAuthProvider(() => authStore.getToken()),
});
```

#### Why This Matters

Clerk's `getToken()` can temporarily return `null` during session establishment, even when `isSignedIn` is `true`. The approved hooks include retry logic to handle this race condition. Creating custom `ApiClient` instances bypasses this protection and causes auth errors.

#### Existing Approved Locations
- `useLlmProxyClient()` in `src/api/hooks/useApiClient.ts` - React hook with token validation
- `dataProviderAccess.ts` - Uses `ClerkAuthProvider` with retry logic
- Service hooks that depend on `useLlmProxyClient()`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The Ripul SDK's theme tools, for any app that links the package.

  ripul-theme migrate <file or directory>...   rewrite call sites to theme tokens; nothing changes on screen
  ripul-theme check [<file or directory>...]   list the fonts and colours still written at the call site
  ripul-theme lint [<git range>]               check that a migration diff kept every value
  ripul-theme usage-map                        in an Xcode build phase: write the View Explorer's token map
  ripul-theme redirect --out <file> <dir>...   what the RipulThemeRedirect plug-in runs: the file that themes unedited source

`ripul-theme <command> --help` says more. docs/theming-for-hosts.md is the page for an
app adopting the theme; docs/theming.md is the full contract.
"""
import pathlib
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent))


def main(argv) -> int:
    command, rest = (argv[0], argv[1:]) if argv else ("", [])
    if command == "migrate":
        import theme_rewrite
        if not rest or "--help" in rest:
            print(theme_rewrite.__doc__)
            return 0
        return theme_rewrite.main(rest)
    if command == "lint":
        import theme_rewrite
        return theme_rewrite.main(["--lint", *rest])
    if command == "check":
        import theme_check
        if "--help" in rest:
            print(theme_check.__doc__)
            return 0
        return theme_check.main(rest)
    if command == "usage-map":
        import theme_usage_map
        if "--help" in rest:
            print(theme_usage_map.__doc__)
            return 0
        return theme_usage_map.main(rest)
    if command == "redirect":
        import theme_redirect
        if not rest or "--help" in rest:
            print(theme_redirect.__doc__)
            return 0
        return theme_redirect.main(rest)
    print(__doc__)
    return 0 if command in ("", "help", "--help", "-h") else 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# release-public.sh — Publish the monorepo RipulAgent SDK to the public
# ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk repo as a clean, one-way mirror + version tag.
#
# The monorepo copy (this script's parent dir) is the source of truth. Histories
# between the two repos diverged long ago, so we do NOT merge — we overwrite the
# public repo's working tree with the monorepo SDK (rsync --delete), commit, and
# tag vX.Y.Z. The push to GitHub happens ONLY with --push (outward-facing step).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/release-public.sh 0.1.0           # stage locally (mirror + commit + tag), no push
#   scripts/release-public.sh 0.1.0 --push    # also push commit + tag to origin
#
# Env:
#   RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK   path to the public repo clone
#                      (default: $HOME/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk)
set -euo pipefail

VERSION="${1:-}"
PUSH=""
[ "${2:-}" = "--push" ] && PUSH=1

SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"          # monorepo SDK root
DEST="${RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK:-$HOME/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk}"        # public repo clone
REMOTE_NAME="origin"
TAG="v${VERSION}"

die() { echo "❌ $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[ -n "$VERSION" ] || die "usage: $0 <version> [--push]   e.g. $0 0.1.0"
echo "$VERSION" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' \
  || die "version must be semver X.Y.Z (got: $VERSION)"
[ -d "$SRC/Sources/RipulAgent" ] || die "source SDK not found at $SRC/Sources/RipulAgent"
[ -d "$DEST/.git" ]              || die "public repo clone not found at $DEST (set RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK)"

echo "▶ Source (monorepo): $SRC"
echo "▶ Dest   (public):   $DEST"
echo "▶ Version:           $TAG"
echo

# Public clone must be clean and not already tagged at this version.
git -C "$DEST" diff --quiet && git -C "$DEST" diff --cached --quiet \
  || die "public repo has uncommitted changes — clean it first"
git -C "$DEST" fetch "$REMOTE_NAME" --tags --quiet || true
if git -C "$DEST" rev-parse --verify "refs/tags/$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  die "tag $TAG already exists — bump the version"
fi

# Stamp the marketing version into the SDK source, so the View Explorer's
# `sdk: …` line reports the release that is actually running on the device.
# Hand-bumping this drifted (it sat at 0.5.8 through the whole 0.6/0.7 series,
# making every element paste misreport the build), so the release owns it.
# Committed in the MONOREPO — the source of truth — before the dirty check
# below, so the tag and the constant can never disagree.
VERSION_FILE="$SRC/Sources/RipulAgent/ViewInspectorOverlay.swift"
CURRENT_VERSION="$(sed -n 's/^let ripulSDKVersion = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$VERSION_FILE")"
[ -n "$CURRENT_VERSION" ] || die "could not read ripulSDKVersion from $VERSION_FILE"
if [ "$CURRENT_VERSION" != "$VERSION" ]; then
  sed -i '' "s/^let ripulSDKVersion = \".*\"\$/let ripulSDKVersion = \"$VERSION\"/" "$VERSION_FILE"
  git -C "$SRC" add "$VERSION_FILE"
  git -C "$SRC" commit -q -m "chore(sdk): stamp ripulSDKVersion $VERSION"
  echo "▶ Stamped ripulSDKVersion: $CURRENT_VERSION -> $VERSION (committed to the monorepo)"
fi

# Concurrency guard: refuse to mirror a DIRTY monorepo tree. The rsync below copies
# the working tree, so uncommitted edits and untracked files ride into the tag —
# and several agents work in this tree concurrently (v0.4.14 shipped an in-flight
# AgentScreen port to WAC this way). Commit (or set aside) foreign work first, or
# pass ALLOW_DIRTY=1 when you really mean it.
if [ "${ALLOW_DIRTY:-}" != "1" ]; then
  dirty="$(git -C "$SRC" status --porcelain -- Sources Package.swift)"
  [ -z "$dirty" ] || die "monorepo SDK tree is dirty — refusing to scoop uncommitted work into $TAG:
$dirty
(commit it, or override with ALLOW_DIRTY=1)"
fi

# Guardrail: no `import Charts`. A host that already has a module named Charts (WAC links
# the danielgindi Charts pod under that name) shadows Apple's framework at link time, so the
# SDK fails to LINK in that host — v0.7.144 shipped that way and WAC could not take it.
if grep -rnE '^[[:space:]]*import[[:space:]]+Charts([[:space:]]|$)' "$SRC/Sources" 2>/dev/null; then
  die "the SDK imports Charts (see above) — hosts with a Charts pod cannot link it; draw the chart with SwiftUI shapes"
fi

# One-way mirror: make the public tree identical to the monorepo SDK, minus VCS
# and build artifacts. Excluded paths are also protected from --delete on DEST.
rsync -a --delete \
  --exclude '.git/' \
  --exclude '.build/' \
  --exclude '.swiftpm/' \
  --exclude 'scripts/' \
  --exclude 'Package.resolved' \
  --exclude '__pycache__/' \
  --exclude '.DS_Store' \
  "$SRC"/ "$DEST"/

# Guardrail: refuse to publish obvious secrets (high-signal patterns only, so a
# normal release never trips it). Comment lines are ignored. Assignments must
# contain a nonempty string literal: passing an apiKey parameter or checking
# url.password == nil is not an embedded credential.
if grep -rniE \
     "(api[_-]?key|secret|password)[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*[\"'][^\"'[:space:]]|BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY|bearer [a-z0-9]{12}" \
     "$DEST/Sources" "$DEST/Examples" "$DEST/docs" 2>/dev/null \
     | grep -vE '^[^:]+:[0-9]+: *(//|\*|/\*)'; then
  die "possible secret in mirrored tree (see matches above) — aborting before commit"
fi

git -C "$DEST" add -A
if git -C "$DEST" diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "ℹ️  No content changes since last release; tagging current HEAD."
else
  git -C "$DEST" commit -q -m "Release $TAG — sync from monorepo RipulAgent SDK"
fi
git -C "$DEST" tag -a "$TAG" -m "RipulAgent $TAG"

echo
echo "✅ Staged $TAG locally in $DEST"
git -C "$DEST" --no-pager log --oneline -1
echo

if [ -n "$PUSH" ]; then
  echo "▶ Pushing to $REMOTE_NAME …"
  git -C "$DEST" push "$REMOTE_NAME" HEAD
  git -C "$DEST" push "$REMOTE_NAME" "$TAG"
  echo "🚀 Pushed $TAG"
else
  echo "ℹ️  Not pushed (outward-facing step held back). To publish:"
  echo "     git -C \"$DEST\" push $REMOTE_NAME HEAD && git -C \"$DEST\" push $REMOTE_NAME $TAG"
fi

// swift-tools-version: 5.9

import PackageDescription

let package = Package(
    name: "RipulAgent",
    platforms: [
        .iOS(.v17),
        .macOS(.v14),
    ],
    products: [
        .library(name: "RipulAgent", targets: ["RipulAgent"]),
        // Command maps: sentence → an app's own actions, via the on-device
        // model and rules. Deliberately dependency-free and separate from
        // RipulAgent, so an app can adopt it without the agent stack — and so
        // nothing Ripul-specific can leak in.
        .library(name: "RipulCommands", targets: ["RipulCommands"]),
        // The theme for a host that changes none of its source: a build-tool plug-in a
        // host switches on for its app target. Opt-in; a host that does not is untouched.
        .plugin(name: "RipulThemeRedirect", targets: ["RipulThemeRedirect"]),
    ],
    dependencies: [
        .package(url: "https://github.com/gonzalezreal/swift-markdown-ui.git", from: "2.4.1"),
        // 0.2.0 added the frame limit the voice orb needs (VoiceModeOverlay.swift).
        .package(url: "https://github.com/ripulio/thinking-orbs-swift.git", from: "0.2.0"),
        .package(url: "https://github.com/appstefan/HighlightSwift.git", from: "1.1.0"),
    ],
    targets: [
        .target(
            name: "RipulAgent",
            dependencies: [
                .product(name: "MarkdownUI", package: "swift-markdown-ui"),
                .product(name: "ThinkingOrbs", package: "thinking-orbs-swift"),
                .product(name: "HighlightSwift", package: "HighlightSwift"),
            ],
            resources: [
                .process("Resources/providers.json"),
                .process("Resources/InspectorEngine.js"),
                .process("Resources/RipulBranding.xcassets"),
            ]
        ),
        .testTarget(
            name: "RipulAgentTests",
            dependencies: ["RipulAgent"]
        ),
        .target(name: "RipulCommands"),
        .plugin(name: "RipulThemeRedirect", capability: .buildTool()),
        .testTarget(
            name: "RipulCommandsTests",
            dependencies: ["RipulCommands"]
        ),
    ]
)

{"guide":"# Plans

In Ripul a plan is a design document in the repository that can be reviewed: people and agents file comments against its sections, the author answers them, and the fixes become tasks. The user reads and acts on plans in the **Plans** screen of the Ripul apps, where each plan shows as Open or Locked with its comments and tasks. Use this guide when asked to write, review, revise or carry out a plan.

## What a plan is made of

A plan is three files that share a name in `docs/plans/` of the chat's working directory:

- `<slug>.md` is the plan itself, in prose. This is the only file you write by hand, with your normal file tools.
- `<slug>.plan.jsonl` is the log of comments, replies, status changes and tasks. Only the plan tools add to it.
- `<slug>.review.md` is a readable review, rebuilt from the log on every change. Never edit it.

No tool creates a plan. To start one, write `docs/plans/<slug>.md` with a title and `##` sections (the Plans screen starts new plans with Problem, Approach and Open questions). If a file with that name already exists, it is someone's plan: revise it or choose another name.

{"guide":"# Trains: builds and deploys shared between agents

When several agents work on one Mac, their builds and deploys collide: two deploys overwrite each other, a rebuild restarts an app someone is testing, an install lands on a phone mid-test. Trainyard, part of Ripul Host, queues that work. A **track** is one job (a deploy, a build, an install). Agents ask for it; one run serves everyone waiting.

## Does this repository use trains?

It does if it has a file `.ripul/trains.yaml`. Then:

```bash
ripul-train config     # the tracks and resources this repository defines
ripul-train status     # what is running, queued, held and held back
```

Where a repository has tracks, use them. Do not run the underlying build or deploy command yourself, even if you can see it in the file.

## Using a track

```bash
ripul-train request <track> --wait          # board the train and wait for the result
ripul-train hold <resource> --reason "testing sign-in" --ttl 20
ripul-train release <hold-id>               # as soon as the test is done
ripul-train block <commit> --reason "not to ship until the owner says"
ripul-train unblock <block-id>
```

- **Only committed, pushed work ships.** A track normally builds the tip of its branch on the remote, not your working tree. Commit and push first.
- **Take a hold before a test that depends on a shared thing** (the live build, a phone, a running app), and release it straight after. A hold keeps trains that would disturb that thing in the yard. Holds expire: 15 minutes by default, 60 at most.
- **A block stops the whole train**, including other agents' work queued behind that commit. It is for "this must not go live yet", not for routine caution.
- **Disruptive steps wait.** A track can end by restarting or reloading something. Trainyard does that only when the other agents' turns have ended, so the request can take a while to return.
- A repository's own scripts may board a train for you. Its instructions file will say which.

## Setting trains up

A repository without the file has no trains. If its agents are colliding, propose adding `.ripul/trains.yaml` to the user; do not add it unasked. In outline:

```yaml
version: 1
resources:
  staging-site: { kind: manual, description: "The staging site; hold it while testing" }
  dev-server:   { kind: port, port: 3000 }
tracks:
  deploy:
    branch: main
    checks: [ "npm test" ]
    run:    [ "npm run deploy" ]
    verify: [ "curl -fsS https://staging.example.com/health" ]
    disturbs: [ staging-site ]
```

A **resource** is a thing trains affect and agents use. Its kind says how Trainyard knows it is in use: `manual` (only while someone holds it), `port`, `process`, `command` (a probe that succeeds while in use) or `agents` (while any agent is mid-turn). A track lists the resources it disturbs. `ripul-train config` checks the file. The Trainyard screen in the Ripul app edits the same file.
","title":"Trains: builds and deploys shared between agents","topic":"trains"}

{"guide":"# Phones, tablets and simulators

You run on the Mac, but the app you are working on often runs on an iPhone, an iPad or a simulator. Use this guide when you need to put a build on a phone, or look at and operate an app running on a device.

## Two families, two different routes

| Family | Reaches the device through | Needs | Sees |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device_…` screen tools | the app itself, over Ripul's relay | the app running in the foreground, built with the Ripul SDK's developer tools | that one app, element by element |
| `host_bridge_…` | Apple's developer tunnel from this Mac, over Tailscale | an iPhone paired with this Mac | the whole phone, as pixels |

They are independent. The bridge can install and launch an app with no Ripul code in it; the screen tools can drive an app in a simulator, which the bridge cannot reach. A typical job uses the bridge to get the build there and the screen tools to test it.

## Choosing the device

Call `device_list_targets` first. It lists each device's handle (for example `iphone-c603`), model, whether it is connected, which tools it offers, and which agent holds it. For a paired iPhone it also gives the name the bridge tools know it by. Check that `inspect_screen` is among a device's tools: without it the device cannot be operated.

A chat has one **working device**: where every `device_…` call acts when it names no `device`. A message from another phone does not move it. `device_set_working_device` moves the chat, and takes the device for this chat alone: other agents' calls to it are refused until you move, pass `release: true`, or go an hour without using it. Release it when the work is done. If the working device is not connected the call fails; nothing falls back to another device.

`host_bridge_…` calls that name no `phone` act on the working device too, and one that would change a phone another agent holds is refused.

## The loop: install, launch, look, tap, verify

1. `host_bridge_status`: is the phone's tunnel active.
2. `host_bridge_run` builds an Xcode project, installs it, checks the installed build and launches it. If you already have a signed `.app`, use `host_bridge_install` (with `launch`). `host_bridge_ship` is not for your project: it builds Ripul's own app.
3. `host_bridge_launch` brings an installed app to the front, or restarts it with `relaunch`.
4. `device_inspect_screen`. Every element comes back with a short handle such as `e7`.
5. `device_tap_element`, `device_type_text`, `device_scroll_element` or `device_set_value`, addressed by that handle.
6. `device_wait_for_element` for the thing that should appear (or, with state `gone`, disappear). It returns the moment the screen matches.
7. `device_inspect_screen` again to confirm, then repeat from 5.

For a simulator, skip the bridge: install and launch with `xcrun simctl`, then start at step 4.

Prefer `device_set_value` for pickers, switches, sliders and segmented controls: it sets the value and fires the app's handler, which is more reliable than operating the control. Use `device_touch` for gestures or an exact point; it takes the window coordinates that inspect reports, and works in debug builds of the app only.

## What inspect can and cannot see

- **Only the app it runs in.** Not the home screen, not another app, not a phone whose app is closed. For those, `host_bridge_screenshot` returns a picture of the whole screen.
- **Only what a person could see.** Views scrolled out of sight, clipped, or covered by something else are left out and counted in `hidden`. Scroll and inspect again, or pass `includeHidden` to see what was left out.
- **Handles expire.** Inspect again after the screen changes.
- An ambiguous tap fails and lists the candidates; nothing is pressed. Narrow it with `within`, `role` or `id` rather than guessing with `nth`.

## What goes wrong

- **The app is in the background.** iOS suspends it, and `device_…` calls go unanswered. Use `host_bridge_launch`, or ask the user to open it.
- **A timeout is not a failure.** When a tap or typing call times out, the action may still have happened: look at the screen before repeating it. Likewise a `host_bridge_install` or `host_bridge_run` call can be cut off while the work carries on: check `host_bridge_projects` for how the last run ended, or inspect the app, before installing again.
- **The phone's network.** A phone accepts a new tunnel only while joined to a Wi-Fi network or to another phone's hotspot, unlocked at least once since it was switched on, with Tailscale connected. On its own cellular connection, or while providing a hotspot itself, it refuses.
- **A phone that was never paired.** Pairing needs the phone plugged into this Mac by USB once, unlocked, with Developer Mode on. Ask the user.
- **Debugging pauses the app.** `host_bridge_debug` attaches LLDB, runs your commands and detaches; the app is stopped while it is attached.

## Recording

`host_record_screen` records a window or a display of the Mac and shows the video in the chat, with a few stills for you to check. That covers a simulator, whose window is on the Mac, but not a physical phone: use `host_bridge_screenshot` before and after instead. It refuses while the Mac's screen is locked, because apps stop drawing behind the lock screen.

## The `device_bridge_…` twins

These are the same bridge tools on another Mac running Ripul Host, for a phone paired with that Mac; pairing is per Mac. Pass `device` for the Mac and `phone` for the phone: these calls do not follow the working device.
","title":"Phones, tablets and simulators","topic":"devices"}

# Sandsend Retreats

An iPhone app for guests of Sandsend Retreats: three holiday cottages (East Hampton, Montauk, Sag Harbor) in the Saltmoore grounds at Sandsend, owned by the Maude family. It onboards a guest (welcome, which cottage, arriving) and then is their guide to the stay. Native SwiftUI, iOS 26, iPhone only, portrait.

Remote: `github.com/ripulio/sandsend-retreats` (private). The business's website is `www.sandsendretreats.com`.

## What is in the app

- **Onboarding** (`Onboarding/`): welcome, choose your cottage, what you need to arrive. Shown until a cottage is chosen.
- **Stay** tab (`Stay/`): check-in and check-out, the keypad, getting here, parking, your cottage with its photos, dogs, no smoking, contact, the owners' story.
- **Explore** tab (`Explore/`): the neighbourhood's places, twelve activities, the spa, private chefs, the village's history.
- **What's On** tab (`WhatsOn/`): the site's calendar of local events, those still to come first.

**Not in the app, because the website does not have it:** door codes, Wi-Fi details, how the heating and appliances work, bins, emergency numbers, anything about one booking. A guide that onboards a guest properly needs these from Peter. Do not invent them.

## The words and photos come from the website

Every sentence a guest reads, apart from headings and button labels, is the website's own, in `SandsendRetreats/Content/guide.json`. Every photo is from the website, in `SandsendRetreats/Photos`.

- **Do not edit `guide.json` by hand.** Change the wording on the website, then run `python3 scripts/import_site.py` and read the diff. The script cuts each page by the headings it has today and stops with an error when one has moved.
- **Photos are chosen in `scripts/photos.json`**: an asset name, the photo's address on the site, and a caption (the app's accessibility label and gallery caption). Add a line and run the script; it downloads, shrinks to 1320 points and converts to HEIC. It skips photos it already has, so delete a file to fetch it again.
- **Photos are plain files, not an asset catalogue**, shown with `PhotoView` or `Image(photo:)`. In an archive build Xcode re-encodes catalogue photos losslessly: 12 MB of photos became 87 MB of assets, whatever the image set's compression setting, and the 111 MB IPA was too big for build hosting (100 MB). Do not move them back.
- `Content/Guide.swift` is the Swift shape of `guide.json`. A field added to one must be added to the other, or the app stops at launch saying which.
- **Whose photos they are.** The cottages, the beach and the family are the owners' own. The activity and chef photos are stock (Pexels, Unsplash, Pixabay, by their filenames). The twelve neighbourhood photos include some taken from those businesses. Nobody has checked the rights for use in an app; the site's event photos were left out for that reason.
- The site spells one cottage both "Sag Harbor" and "Sag Harbour" (the slate sign says Harbour). The app follows the cottage's own page: Harbor.

## Layout

```
project.yml                    XcodeGen spec. The source of truth for the project.
scripts/import_site.py         Website -> guide.json and the photo sets.
scripts/photos.json            Which photos, from where, with what caption.
scripts/ship_ota.py            Publishes a build to the install page.
SandsendRetreats/Content/      guide.json and its Swift model.
SandsendRetreats/Shared/       Theme, shared views (GuidePage, GuideCard, GuideRow), routes and levers.
SandsendRetreats/Theme/        The two theme documents.
SandsendRetreats/Fonts/        The brand theme's fonts, their licences and where they came from.
SandsendRetreats/Developer/    The Ripul developer console and the identifier helper.
```

## Rules

- **The `.xcodeproj` is generated and gitignored.** Run `xcodegen generate` after cloning, after changing `project.yml`, and after adding or removing a source file. Never edit the `.xcodeproj`.
- **One DerivedData path: `build`.** Always pass `-derivedDataPath build`. Do not invent another.
- **The bundle id is `io.ripul.sandsendretreats`** (`SANDSEND_BUNDLE_ID` in `project.yml`), chosen by Peter on 10 October 2026. Do not change it. The first device build (10 October 2026) was signed with the team's wildcard profile, so the id has no App ID of its own at Apple yet; it will need one for push notifications, TestFlight or any other entitlement.
- Use the platform's own controls and the iOS 26 Liquid Glass material; do not re-skin a web look in SwiftUI.
- **Name every control with `.identified("screen.element")`**, not a bare `.accessibilityIdentifier`. Give each control its own name; a name on a container is inherited by what is inside it.
- **Navy buttons say `.tint(Brand.navy)`.** The accent colour turns pale blue in dark mode, and white text on it cannot be read.
- The app icon is a placeholder ("SR" in the signs' navy and cream).

## The theme (branch `theme-trial-2`, a second trial of the Ripul SDK's theme system)

Every font and colour is a theme token of the Ripul SDK: `.font(.ripul(.headline))`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))`, `.background(Color.ripul(.surface))`. The SDK's page for hosts is the contract: `build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming-for-hosts.md`. Its tools are beside it, in `tools/ripul-theme`. This puts the SDK in Release builds' code: before it, every use was inside `#if DEBUG`.

- **Two looks, each a document in `SandsendRetreats/Theme`.** `standard.json` is the app as it was (it names one thing: the display family is the system serif). `brand.json` is the website's and install page's look: paper and navy, Playfair Display for names and headings, Source Sans 3 for text. The root names `standard`; Stay, More, Look changes it while the app runs, and the SDK keeps the choice.
- **The app has no theme code of its own.** One line at the root (`.ripulThemeRoot(theme: "standard")`), one `RipulThemePicker` in the More menu. The SDK finds the documents, registers the fonts they name and keeps the choice. `@_exported import RipulAgent` in `SandsendRetreatsApp.swift` is why no other file imports it.
- **The fonts are stand-ins.** The website uses IvyPresto Display and Freight Sans Pro, which are Adobe Fonts and may not be put in an app. `SandsendRetreats/Fonts/SOURCES.md` says where the bundled ones came from; their licences are beside them.
- **A new `Text` needs `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))`** or it stays black on the brand's paper. Not on a container: there it recolours the buttons, links and list headers inside.
- **Headings say `family: .display`**; a symbol's size is `.ripulIcon(...)`; white on a photo is `.ripul(system: .white)`; a shade over a photo is marked `// theme-exempt`.
- **`Brand.navy` and `Brand.cream`** are the theme's accent and what reads on it once a theme names an accent. Read them where they are used.
- **A list** takes `.themedList()` and each of its sections `.themedRows()` (`Shared/Components.swift`).
- **After adding a view**, run `build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme check SandsendRetreats`: it lists every font and colour written directly. It read zero on 11 October 2026.
- **The View Explorer names an element's tokens** from `ripul-theme-usage.json`, which the "Theme usage map" build step writes into a Debug build. A control named from a variable (`name + ".call"`) is not in the map.
- **Checking the default look has not moved:** screenshots of eighteen screens, light and dark, before and after, compared pixel for pixel (11 October 2026: all the same, but for the gallery's glass close button, which differs between two captures of one build).
- **What the SDK does not reach (0.7.171):** the colour of a large navigation title and of a list's section headers; navigation titles take the text family, not the display one.

## Looking at a screen without tapping

A Debug build takes launch arguments that open a given screen (`Shared/Routes.swift`, `Levers`). An agent cannot tap until a person has signed in to the developer console, so this is how to check a change:

```bash
xcrun simctl launch --terminate-running-process <simulator> io.ripul.sandsendretreats \
  -onboarded YES -cottage montauk -tab explore -route activity:surfing
```

| Argument | Values |
|---|---|
| `-onboarded` | `YES` the guide, `NO` onboarding |
| `-cottage` | `east-hampton`, `montauk`, `sag-harbor` |
| `-onboardingStep` | `picker`, `arrival` |
| `-tab` | `stay`, `explore`, `whatsOn` |
| `-route` | `cottage:<id>`, `activity:<id>`, `dogs`, `story`, `wellness`, `chefs`, `history` (opens on the tab `-tab` names) |
| `-scrollToEnd YES`, `-scrollY <points>` | where the page is scrolled to |
| `-gallery YES` | with `-route cottage:<id>`, the photos full screen |
| `-theme` | `standard`, `brand`: the look, kept for later launches as a choice in the More menu is |
| `-ripul.theme.document` | `standard`, `brand`: the look for this launch. The SDK's own argument, so it works in Release too |

Then `xcrun simctl io <simulator> screenshot <file>`. Add a lever when a new screen cannot be reached by these. A Release build ignores all but `-ripul.theme.document`.

## Shipping a build: the install page

**https://demo.ripul.io/sandsend** is where a build is installed from, and the app's list of updates: the newest build with what changed in it, and the five before it with theirs. It is hosted by Ripul's build hosting, as app `sandsend`, the way Ripul's own page (`/ios`) is.

```bash
nohup python3 scripts/ship_ota.py "What changed in this build" > /tmp/sandsend-ota.log 2>&1 & disown
tail -n 5 /tmp/sandsend-ota.log
```

- It archives the app, exports a development-signed IPA, publishes it, and then checks the page: that its manifest names this build and that the IPA it serves is the one exported. It ends with "Published and verified" or with the reason it stopped.
- **It ships committed, pushed work only**, and refuses otherwise. Commit and push first.
- **The notes are what a person reads on the page.** Say what changed for a guest, in a sentence or two; they are cut at 400 characters. With none given, the newest commit's subject is used.
- **The page is public.** Anyone with the address can download a build, though only iPhones registered with the team can install one. Peter asked for it to work like Ripul's and WAC's, which are public in the same way.
- Builds are Debug, like a direct install: the developer console and the launch levers are in them.
- A build number is the minute it was made. Publishing twice in one minute is refused with HTTP 409; run it again.
- **A phone registered after the signing profile was made cannot install a build**: iOS says "Unable to Install". The app signs with the team's wildcard profile ("iOS Team Provisioning Profile: *"), and Xcode keeps using its cached copy however old. On 10 October 2026 the copy was from 4 October with 42 phones, and Oxana's iPhone, registered that day, was the 43rd. The cure, once the phone is registered with the team: move the wildcard profile out of `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/UserData/Provisioning Profiles` (to `~/.ripul/appstoreconnect/moved-aside-<date>/`), then ship; the archive fetches a fresh one, using the App Store Connect key in `~/.ripul/appstoreconnect` when the Mac has it. The script prints which profile a build was signed with and for how many iPhones, and `SANDSEND_REQUIRE_DEVICES="<udid> <udid>"` makes it refuse to publish a build those phones could not install. Each Mac has its own cache.
- **The publish token is per Mac**, in `~/.ripul/sandsend-build-token` (the Mac Studio has one). A new Mac gets its own: `openssl rand -hex 32`, then a row in `build_publish_tokens (token_hash, app_id, label)` for app `sandsend`, holding the token's SHA-256, in Ripul's database (`wrangler d1 execute llm-proxy-db --remote --env production`, from `chrome-extension/packages/api` in the ripul repo). Never copy another Mac's token.
- The page's wording and look are in the ripul repo, `chrome-extension/functions/sandsend.ts`: its text, and `LOOK`, the styles (the serif, paper and navy, the card for a build's notes). Its photo is `chrome-extension/public/install/sandsend-hero.jpg`, the beach the app opens on. A change there goes out with Ripul's web deploy, and Ripul's own `/ios` page shares the code underneath, so run that repo's `tests/installPage.test.ts`.

## The Ripul developer console

The app carries the RipulAgent SDK so that coding agents on Peter's Mac can see and tap through it (`device_inspect_screen`, `device_tap_element` and the other `device_…` tools). Read the `sdk` guide from the `ripul_guide` tool before changing any of it.

- **The console exists in Debug builds only.** Every use of the SDK in the app's code is inside `#if DEBUG`: `DeveloperConsole.swift`, the menu item on the Stay tab, and the Debug branch of `.identified`. Keep it that way, and build Release after touching it.
- **The SDK itself is still linked into a Release build.** Xcode links a package into every configuration, so the Release app carries the SDK's code and resource bundles though nothing calls them (57 MB against 93 MB for Debug, simulator builds of the bare app, measured 10 October 2026). Nothing has been done about this. Decide with Peter before the first TestFlight or App Store build: take the package out of Release, or ship it as WAC does.
- **Opening it.** Stay tab, the More menu (top right), Developer Console. After that a bubble floats over the app and comes back on each launch.
- **Opening it without a tap.** Launch with `-openDeveloperConsole YES`. This is how an agent brings the sign-in screen up for a person.
- **Agents get nothing until a person has signed in** to their Ripul account in the console, and only while the app is open in the foreground.
- **The pin is `exactVersion` in `project.yml`.** The project's `Package.resolved` is not in git. To take an SDK release, change that line and rebuild.
- The microphone and speech-recognition descriptions in `project.yml` are for dictation in the console, and are set for Debug only.

## Commands

```bash
xcodegen generate

# Simulator build, no signing. Add -configuration Release to check the build without the console.
xcodebuild -scheme SandsendRetreats \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' \
  -derivedDataPath build \
  ARCHS=arm64 CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build

# Refresh the content from the website
python3 scripts/import_site.py

# Peter's iPhone 17 Pro Max: build, install, launch. Commit and push first.
xcodebuild -scheme SandsendRetreats \
  -destination 'platform=iOS,id=00008150-001C544E0EBA401C' \
  -derivedDataPath build -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=C7AA358R56 CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic build
xcrun devicectl device install app --device 00008150-001C544E0EBA401C \
  build/Build/Products/Debug-iphoneos/SandsendRetreats.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --terminate-existing \
  --device 00008150-001C544E0EBA401C io.ripul.sandsendretreats
```

The phone's id changes when Peter changes phone: `xcodebuild -scheme SandsendRetreats -showdestinations` lists the one to use. Proof an install landed is the app in `xcrun devicectl device info apps --device <id>`, and its process in `… info processes`.

`ARCHS=arm64` is required with the generic simulator destination. Without it Xcode also builds for Intel simulators, and the SDK's Debug code does not compile there (`MainThreadSampler.swift`, SDK 0.7.169). A build for one named simulator does not need it.

The first build after a clone fetches and compiles the SDK, which takes a few minutes. Build with `/Applications/Xcode-27.1.app`, the only Xcode on Peter's Macs.

name: SandsendRetreats
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: io.ripul
  deploymentTarget:
    iOS: "26.0"
  generateEmptyDirectories: true

settings:
  base:
    # Chosen by Peter, 10 October 2026. Automatic signing registers it with the
    # team at the first device build.
    SANDSEND_BUNDLE_ID: io.ripul.sandsendretreats
    DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: C7AA358R56
    CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Automatic
    SWIFT_VERSION: "5.9"
    MARKETING_VERSION: "0.1.0"
    CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION: "1"

# The .xcodeproj is not in git, so neither is its Package.resolved. The exact
# version here is the pin: move it by hand to take an SDK release.
packages:
  RipulAgent:
    url: https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk
    exactVersion: 0.7.171

targets:
  SandsendRetreats:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    sources:
      - SandsendRetreats
    dependencies:
      - package: RipulAgent
    # Debug builds only: lets the Ripul View Explorer name the theme tokens of
    # a selected element.
    postCompileScripts:
      - name: Theme usage map
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: '"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map'
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: $(SANDSEND_BUNDLE_ID)
        TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY: "1"
        GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES
        INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDisplayName: Sandsend Retreats
        INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen_Generation: YES
        INFOPLIST_KEY_UIApplicationSceneManifest_Generation: YES
        INFOPLIST_KEY_UISupportedInterfaceOrientations_iPhone: UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait
        ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME: AppIcon
        ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GLOBAL_ACCENT_COLOR_NAME: AccentColor
        # The usage map's script reads the source.
        ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING: NO
      configs:
        # Voice input in the developer console. Debug only, like the console.
        Debug:
          INFOPLIST_KEY_NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Lets you dictate messages in the Ripul developer console.
          INFOPLIST_KEY_NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription: Turns what you dictate in the Ripul developer console into text.

#!/bin/bash
# Installs the no-source-change Sandsend build on Peter's iPhone as soon as the phone is reachable.
export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-27.1.app/Contents/Developer
UDID=00008150-001C544E0EBA401C
APP=/tmp/sz-device.app
BRIDGE=/Users/petermaude/Documents/ripul/ripul-native-app/device-bridge/ripul-bridge
for i in $(seq 1 240); do
  [ -d "$APP" ] || { echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') build is gone from /tmp"; echo "EXIT_CODE=2"; exit 2; }
  if xcrun devicectl list devices 2>/dev/null | grep "$UDID" | grep -qv unavailable; then
    echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') phone reachable by CoreDevice, installing"
    if xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$UDID" "$APP" 2>&1 | tail -3; then
      xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$UDID" io.ripul.sandsendretreats 2>&1 | tail -2
      echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') INSTALLED via CoreDevice"; echo "EXIT_CODE=0"; exit 0
    fi
  fi
  st=$("$BRIDGE" status 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(next((p.get('state') for p in d.get('phones',[]) if p.get('udid')=='$UDID'),'?'))" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$st" = "active" ]; then
    echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') phone reachable by the bridge, installing"
    if "$BRIDGE" install --launch "$UDID" "$APP" 2>&1 | tail -4; then echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') INSTALLED via the bridge"; echo "EXIT_CODE=0"; exit 0; fi
  fi
  [ $((i % 10)) -eq 1 ] && echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') waiting: CoreDevice unavailable, bridge $st"
  sleep 60
done
echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') gave up after four hours"; echo "EXIT_CODE=1"

- **After adding a view**, run `build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme check SandsendRetreats`: it lists every font and colour written directly. It read zero on 11 October 2026.
- **The View Explorer names an element's tokens** from `ripul-theme-usage.json`, which the "Theme usage map" build step writes into a Debug build. A control named from a variable (`name + ".call"`) is not in the map.
- **Checking the default look has not moved:** screenshots of eighteen screens, light and dark, before and after, compared pixel for pixel (11 October 2026: all the same, but for the gallery's glass close button, which differs between two captures of one build).
- **What the SDK does not reach (0.7.171):** the colour of a large navigation title and of a list's section headers; navigation titles take the text family, not the display one.

## Looking at a screen without tapping

A Debug build takes launch arguments that open a given screen (`Shared/Routes.swift`, `Levers`). An agent cannot tap until a person has signed in to the developer console, so this is how to check a change:

```bash
xcrun simctl launch --terminate-running-process <simulator> io.ripul.sandsendretreats \
  -onboarded YES -cottage montauk -tab explore -route activity:surfing
```

| Argument | Values |
|---|---|
| `-onboarded` | `YES` the guide, `NO` onboarding |
| `-cottage` | `east-hampton`, `montauk`, `sag-harbor` |
| `-onboardingStep` | `picker`, `arrival` |
| `-tab` | `stay`, `explore`, `whatsOn` |
| `-route` | `cottage:<id>`, `activity:<id>`, `dogs`, `story`, `wellness`, `chefs`, `history` (opens on the tab `-tab` names) |
| `-scrollToEnd YES`, `-scrollY <points>` | where the page is scrolled to |
| `-gallery YES` | with `-route cottage:<id>`, the photos full screen |
| `-theme` | `standard`, `brand`: the look, kept for later launches as a choice in the More menu is |
| `-ripul.theme.document` | `standard`, `brand`: the look for this launch. The SDK's own argument, so it works in Release too |

Then `xcrun simctl io <simulator> screenshot <file>`. Add a lever when a new screen cannot be reached by these. A Release build ignores all but `-ripul.theme.document`.

## Shipping a build: the install page

**https://demo.ripul.io/sandsend** is where a build is installed from, and the app's list of updates: the newest build with what changed in it, and the five before it with theirs. It is hosted by Ripul's build hosting, as app `sandsend`, the way Ripul's own page (`/ios`) is.

```bash
nohup python3 scripts/ship_ota.py "What changed in this build" > /tmp/sandsend-ota.log 2>&1 & disown
tail -n 5 /tmp/sandsend-ota.log
```

- It archives the app, exports a development-signed IPA, publishes it, and then checks the page: that its manifest names this build and that the IPA it serves is the one exported. It ends with "Published and verified" or with the reason it stopped.
- **It ships committed, pushed work only**, and refuses otherwise. Commit and push first.
- **The notes are what a person reads on the page.** Say what changed for a guest, in a sentence or two; they are cut at 400 characters. With none given, the newest commit's subject is used.
- **The page is public.** Anyone with the address can download a build, though only iPhones registered with the team can install one. Peter asked for it to work like Ripul's and WAC's, which are public in the same way.
- Builds are Debug, like a direct install: the developer console and the launch levers are in them.
- A build number is the minute it was made. Publishing twice in one minute is refused with HTTP 409; run it again.
- **A phone registered after the signing profile was made cannot install a build**: iOS says "Unable to Install". The app signs with the team's wildcard profile ("iOS Team Provisioning Profile: *"), and Xcode keeps using its cached copy however old. On 10 October 2026 the copy was from 4 October with 42 phones, and Oxana's iPhone, registered that day, was the 43rd. The cure, once the phone is registered with the team: move the wildcard profile out of `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/UserData/Provisioning Profiles` (to `~/.ripul/appstoreconnect/moved-aside-<date>/`), then ship; the archive fetches a fresh one, using the App Store Connect key in `~/.ripul/appstoreconnect` when the Mac has it. The script prints which profile a build was signed with and for how many iPhones, and `SANDSEND_REQUIRE_DEVICES="<udid> <udid>"` makes it refuse to publish a build those phones could not install. Each Mac has its own cache.
- **The publish token is per Mac**, in `~/.ripul/sandsend-build-token` (the Mac Studio has one). A new Mac gets its own: `openssl rand -hex 32`, then a row in `build_publish_tokens (token_hash, app_id, label)` for app `sandsend`, holding the token's SHA-256, in Ripul's database (`wrangler d1 execute llm-proxy-db --remote --env production`, from `chrome-extension/packages/api` in the ripul repo). Never copy another Mac's token.
- The page's wording and look are in the ripul repo, `chrome-extension/functions/sandsend.ts`: its text, and `LOOK`, the styles (the serif, paper and navy, the card for a build's notes). Its photo is `chrome-extension/public/install/sandsend-hero.jpg`, the beach the app opens on. A change there goes out with Ripul's web deploy, and Ripul's own `/ios` page shares the code underneath, so run that repo's `tests/installPage.test.ts`.

## The Ripul developer console

The app carries the RipulAgent SDK so that coding agents on Peter's Mac can see and tap through it (`device_inspect_screen`, `device_tap_element` and the other `device_…` tools). Read the `sdk` guide from the `ripul_guide` tool before changing any of it.

- **The console exists in Debug builds only.** Every use of the SDK in the app's code is inside `#if DEBUG`: `DeveloperConsole.swift`, the menu item on the Stay tab, and the Debug branch of `.identified`. Keep it that way, and build Release after touching it.
- **The SDK itself is still linked into a Release build.** Xcode links a package into every configuration, so the Release app carries the SDK's code and resource bundles though nothing calls them (57 MB against 93 MB for Debug, simulator builds of the bare app, measured 10 October 2026). Nothing has been done about this. Decide with Peter before the first TestFlight or App Store build: take the package out of Release, or ship it as WAC does.
- **Opening it.** Stay tab, the More menu (top right), Developer Console. After that a bubble floats over the app and comes back on each launch.
- **Opening it without a tap.** Launch with `-openDeveloperConsole YES`. This is how an agent brings the sign-in screen up for a person.
- **Agents get nothing until a person has signed in** to their Ripul account in the console, and only while the app is open in the foreground.
- **The pin is `exactVersion` in `project.yml`.** The project's `Package.resolved` is not in git. To take an SDK release, change that line and rebuild.
- The microphone and speech-recognition descriptions in `project.yml` are for dictation in the console, and are set for Debug only.

## Commands

```bash
xcodegen generate

# Simulator build, no signing. Add -configuration Release to check the build without the console.
xcodebuild -scheme SandsendRetreats \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' \
  -derivedDataPath build \
  ARCHS=arm64 CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build

# Refresh the content from the website
python3 scripts/import_site.py

# Peter's iPhone 17 Pro Max: build, install, launch. Commit and push first.
xcodebuild -scheme SandsendRetreats \
  -destination 'platform=iOS,id=00008150-001C544E0EBA401C' \
  -derivedDataPath build -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=C7AA358R56 CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic build
xcrun devicectl device install app --device 00008150-001C544E0EBA401C \
  build/Build/Products/Debug-iphoneos/SandsendRetreats.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --terminate-existing \
  --device 00008150-001C544E0EBA401C io.ripul.sandsendretreats
```

The phone's id changes when Peter changes phone: `xcodebuild -scheme SandsendRetreats -showdestinations` lists the one to use. Proof an install landed is the app in `xcrun devicectl device info apps --device <id>`, and its process in `… info processes`.

`ARCHS=arm64` is required with the generic simulator destination. Without it Xcode also builds for Intel simulators, and the SDK's Debug code does not compile there (`MainThreadSampler.swift`, SDK 0.7.169). A build for one named simulator does not need it.

The first build after a clone fetches and compiles the SDK, which takes a few minutes. Build with `/Applications/Xcode-27.1.app`, the only Xcode on Peter's Macs.

    DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: C7AA358R56

packages:

    exactVersion: 0.7.171

targets:

    type: application

    sources:

    # Debug builds only: lets the Ripul View Explorer name the theme tokens of

# Installs the no-source-change Sandsend build on Peter's iPhone as soon as the phone is reachable.
export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-27.1.app/Contents/Developer
UDID=00008150-001C544E0EBA401C
APP=/tmp/sz-device.app
BRIDGE=/Users/petermaude/Documents/ripul/ripul-native-app/device-bridge/ripul-bridge
for i in $(seq 1 240); do
  [ -d "$APP" ] || { echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') build is gone from /tmp"; echo "EXIT_CODE=2"; exit 2; }
  if xcrun devicectl list devices 2>/dev/null | grep "$UDID" | grep -qv unavailable; then
    echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') phone reachable by CoreDevice, installing"
    if xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$UDID" "$APP" 2>&1 | tail -3; then
      xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$UDID" io.ripul.sandsendretreats 2>&1 | tail -2
      echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') INSTALLED via CoreDevice"; echo "EXIT_CODE=0"; exit 0
    fi
  fi
  st=$("$BRIDGE" status 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(next((p.get('state') for p in d.get('phones',[]) if p.get('udid')=='$UDID'),'?'))" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$st" = "active" ]; then
    echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') phone reachable by the bridge, installing"
    if "$BRIDGE" install --launch "$UDID" "$APP" 2>&1 | tail -4; then echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') INSTALLED via the bridge"; echo "EXIT_CODE=0"; exit 0; fi
  fi
  [ $((i % 10)) -eq 1 ] && echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') waiting: CoreDevice unavailable, bridge $st"

done

content.content:
import Foundation
import PackagePlugin

// The theme for a host that changes no source: one Swift file generated into the build
// folder and compiled into the host's own module (docs/theming-for-hosts.md, "With no
// change to your source"). What the file does is in `ThemeCore/RipulThemeRedirect.swift`;
// what is written is decided by `tools/theme_redirect.py`, which leaves out any name the
// target already declares for itself.

@main
struct RipulThemeRedirectPlugin: BuildToolPlugin {
    func createBuildCommands(context: PluginContext, target: Target) async throws -> [Command] {
        let sources = (target as? SourceModuleTarget)?.sourceFiles(withSuffix: "swift").map(\.path) ?? []
        return [try redirect(sources: sources, into: context.pluginWorkDirectory)]
    }
}

/// The package's own folder: this file is compiled where the package was checked out.
private let package = URL(fileURLWithPath: #filePath).deletingLastPathComponent().deletingLastPathComponent().deletingLastPathComponent()

private func redirect(sources: [Path], into work: Path) throws -> Command {
    let tools = Path(package.appendingPathComponent("tools").path)
    let output = work.appending("RipulThemeRedirect.swift")
    // The target's Swift files, as a list the tool reads: a large target has more than a
    // command line holds.
    let list = work.appending("sources.txt")
    try FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: work.string, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
    let text = sources.map(\.string).joined(separator: "\n")
    if (try? String(contentsOfFile: list.string, encoding: .utf8)) != text {
        try text.write(toFile: list.string, atomically: true, encoding: .utf8)
    }
    return .buildCommand(
        displayName: "Ripul theme: redirect SwiftUI's fonts and colours to the theme",
        executable: Path("/usr/bin/python3"),
        arguments: [tools.appending("ripul-theme").string, "redirect", "--out", output.string, "--sources", list.string],
        inputFiles: sources + [list, tools.appending("theme_redirect.py"), tools.appending(subpath: "redirect/RipulThemeRedirect.swift.txt")],
        outputFiles: [output])
}

#if canImport(XcodeProjectPlugin)
import XcodeProjectPlugin

extension RipulThemeRedirectPlugin: XcodeBuildToolPlugin {
    func createBuildCommands(context: XcodePluginContext, target: XcodeTarget) throws -> [Command] {

// folder and compiled into the host's own module (docs/theming-for-hosts.md, "With no

// what is written is decided by `tools/theme_redirect.py`, which leaves out any name the
// target already declares for itself.

@main
struct RipulThemeRedirectPlugin: BuildToolPlugin {
    func createBuildCommands(context: PluginContext, target: Target) async throws -> [Command] {
        let sources = (target as? SourceModuleTarget)?.sourceFiles(withSuffix: "swift").map(\.path) ?? []
        return [try redirect(sources: sources, into: context.pluginWorkDirectory)]
    }
}

/// The package's own folder: this file is compiled where the package was checked out.
private let package = URL(fileURLWithPath: #filePath).deletingLastPathComponent().deletingLastPathComponent().deletingLastPathComponent()

private func redirect(sources: [Path], into work: Path) throws -> Command {
    let tools = Path(package.appendingPathComponent("tools").path)
    let output = work.appending("RipulThemeRedirect.swift")
    // The target's Swift files, as a list the tool reads: a large target has more than a
    // command line holds.

    try FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: work.string, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
    let text = sources.map(\.string).joined(separator: "\n")

        try text.write(toFile: list.string, atomically: true, encoding: .utf8)

        executable: Path("/usr/bin/python3"),
